Context: as a patient i think telling my story would be helpful for educational purposes and i would love to share it when i listen to other peoples stories i try to find similarities between me and that person

Context: ive found hope and inspiration by listening to other peoples stories and finding points of similarity or connection with them i want to use this conversation as an opportunity to put some hopefulness and possibility out to the world for others who may resonate with me and i think there are some aspects of my story and identity that could be helpful to share
Response: its great to hear that youve found hope and inspiration through connecting with others stories your willingness to share your experience can indeed inspire and help others who might be going through similar situations to create a meaningful impact please focus on the aspects of your journey that you think have been most transformative or empowering and share your coping strategies and resources that have helped you along the way

Context: i felt comfortable enough to stop the conversation in our session
Response: thats great to hear that you felt comfortable stopping the conversation lets take a moment to reflect on our session and discuss your thoughts feelings or any concerns that you might have at this point

Context: i feel like no matter how open minded i am there is still room for me to expand and understand what you are saying about being out and proud and then not wanting other people to feel like they need to be out if they are not there yet
Response: it sounds like youre acknowledging that theres more for you to learn and understand which is a great quality to have your ability to consider how your actions might affect others is quite humble and generous is your dads generosity something that has influenced you in this regard

Context: i find myself emulating my fathers generosity like when he would help families in need by providing them with housing and housewarming gifts im working with a young girl whos in a tough situation herself taking care of her siblings and i had the idea to buy them a months worth of groceries
Response: its wonderful to see that youve inherited your fathers compassionate nature and are applying it to help others in need its important to support others while maintaining your own wellbeing so dont hesitate to reach out for help or advice if you ever feel overwhelmed by the responsibility

Context: recently ive noticed a peculiar pattern in my life i find it hard to explain but its just funny how it keeps happening i need some explanation or advice on how to handle this
Response: its quite common for people to notice patterns in their lives sometimes without even realizing the underlying factors that contribute to them i would be happy to explore this with you further could you please provide more details about the pattern youve noticed and how it has been affecting your life or emotions

Context: i grew up with parents who always wanted a better life for their children although i dont have children yet i see others who need help and liberation my dad was very generous and i hope i have embodied that by sacrificing my privacy and myself even though it feels like im in a cage sometimes
Response: i understand that your parents have instilled values in you that make you want to help others and carry on their legacy of generosity it seems that youre struggling with the balance between helping others and feeling trapped or sacrificing your own wellbeing can you elaborate more on the situations where you feel like youre in a cage

Context: i feel trapped in cages of normativity and gender that are socially constructed by the media and other people i wish i could live happily and confidently knowing that i am living right for myself but these external forces make it difficult
Response: its understandable that you feel trapped in these societal expectations its important to focus on your own values beliefs and wellbeing when navigating through life remember that you have the power to define who you are and how you want to express yourself regardless of external pressures how do you envision your ideal self free from these social constructs and expectations

Context: i could be happy and confident being myself but i fear that my family may get really awkward with me if i am more open with them i believe it could be a christmas gift that i can offer to my family but i worry about their reaction and how they may receive it
Response: its great to hear that you want to be more open and true to yourself especially around your family remember people might need time to adjust to change you cant control how they react but you can control your actions and how you communicate with them share your feelings openly and try to approach the situation with patience and understanding it might be a step towards strengthening the bond you share with your family

Context: i was talking with a friend last night about how im having difficulty coming out to all of my family as transgender my friend mentioned that its better to tell them and put the ball in their court to accept and understand me
Response: its understandable that coming out to your family can be a challenging and emotional process your friends advice about putting the ball in their court suggests that you can only do so much to initiate the conversation and create understanding the rest is up to your familys acceptance and support it might be helpful to think about how you would like to approach this conversation and what kind of support you have in place for yourself during this time remember its important to prioritize your own wellbeing in this process are there any specific concerns or fears you have in regard to coming out to your family

Context: i think its really important to keep rehearsing and remembering the bits of history from when we started with storytelling my transition journey began about two and a half years ago and i wonder if i could find some seeds of it in ideas hopes or dreams that predate those two and a half years
Response: its great that you appreciate the value of storytelling and its importance in carrying your history forward as a counsellor i suggest you reflect on those older conversations dreams or hopes you mentioned to help identify any signs of your transition journey starting earlier than two and a half years ago this deeper understanding could give you more clarity and better prepare you for any future challenges in your transition

Context: ive been reflecting on my past and marking the beginning of a significant transition two and a half years ago ive had conversations with people who have shared their stories and versions of my story which have shaped my understanding of my history i dont necessarily look at my past to make changes but i do recognize the importance of having and retelling that history
Response: its great that youre acknowledging your past experiences and the influence of others in shaping your understanding when reflecting on your history its not always about making changes but rather learning and growing from those experiences think about how your origin story has played a role in your transition and how it can help you move forward in a positive direction is there a specific part of your story that resonates with you the most

Context: i never thought about it but thats probably true i have some very stringent requirements for my close friendships such as acceptance understanding and ability to communicate is that something we should talk a little bit about
Response: its great to see that you value qualities like acceptance understanding and communication in your friendships that can indeed create a space of openness and closeness with the people you connect with if youd like we can explore how these requirements impact your relationships and ways to nurture these qualities in your connections with others do you have any concerns about maintaining these requirements in your friendships as a trans person

Context: im focusing mainly on my transition its not necessarily about gender stuff but its more about physical transitions such as hormones and binding
Response: its important to acknowledge and address any concerns you might have during your transition can you share more details about your current physical transitions and any specific challenges or emotions you are experiencing during this process im here to provide guidance and support

Context: over the past two and a half years i have undergone a transition and have become a completely different person i find it interesting to talk to my friends about how i was like back then i also find that revisiting my history helps me not repeat mistakes
Response: its great to see that you recognize the changes you have experienced and are using your past experiences as a guide to avoid repeating mistakes reflecting on our past can provide valuable insights for personal growth can you share more about the lessons youve learned from discussing your past with friends and how it has contributed to your personal development

Context: i think my mom is so passionate about me being a girl that she would be willing to see me sacrifice my happiness she has made a lot of sacrifices for her happiness so she thinks everybody should do that shes in so much pain because of it her pain has somehow inspired me to do what makes me happy
Response: it sounds like you have a complicated relationship with your mom and her views on gender and happiness its interesting that her sacrifices and pain have motivated you to find your own happiness even if it goes against her expectations how do you plan to navigate this with your mother while maintaining your own wellbeing

Context: i feel like my mom has been really unhappy and has sacrificed a lot for me and my brothers always living in the past i want to break down barriers and help people be more free which is something she could not do can i still find value and meaning in my work to challenge the gender binary and strive for liberation even if my mom may not come to fully understand my intentions
Response: its understandable that you want to create a better life for yourself and others based on your mothers experience your dedication to challenging societal norms and working towards liberation can be valuable and purposeful even if your mother may not fully understand your intentions the important thing is to focus on your goals and what you believe is right and perhaps over time she might come to see the positive impact you are making

Context: i am trying to establish my goals as being valuable to my mom although i dont know how to do it i am confident of her love and working hard because i think it is something she should be proud of however i am not sure what informs her standards and she always pushes me to make a lot of money just like everyone else
Response: it sounds like youre putting in a lot of effort to make your mom proud and ensure she sees your goals as valuable in order to better understand your moms standards you might want to engage in an open conversation with her to gain insight into her thoughts and beliefs you can ask her about her own experiences or about the social cultural or economic factors that may influence her expectations knowing this information might help you to align your goals with her values and ultimately strengthen your relationship

Context: i had a conversation with the counsellor and i realized that i need to work harder on finding the similarity with my mom i want to be able to communicate what im doing as valuable to her
Response: it seems like finding common ground with your mom and communicating the value of your actions is important to you one thing you might want to consider is approaching the conversation on your terms focusing on meaning and intentionality this might help your mom understand where youre coming from do you have any specific strategies in mind for bridging this communication gap

Context: ive always been quite loud and my mom has really traditional views about whats right and wrong especially regarding appearance and attitude we are not able to find similarities between us but i find hope when i listen to other peoples stories and find similarities with them ive been thinking for years about how we can find common ground and maintain a conversation together
Response: its great that you find hope in hearing others stories and it shows your willingness to connect with your mom i understand that its difficult when your personalities and views might clash instead of trying to change each other try to find a common interest or activity that you both could enjoy this way you can focus on building your relationship and understanding each other better potentially discovering similarities you didnt realize were there

Context: im having trouble communicating with my mom we often talk across each other and i think we both have some similarities that get in the way of understanding each other she feels that i need to listen more and while she says she would like to understand my similarities im not sure if thats what she truly means
Response: it sounds like you and your mom are struggling with communication and both of you may have some unresolved similarities that might be affecting your conversations i would suggest when talking with your mom try to focus on actively listening to what she says and understand her perspective if she feels heard she might be more open to understanding your similarities as well additionally you could also express your concerns in a calm manner to her and see if that leads to a more productive conversation

Context: i feel like my mom wants me to be a different person she wants me to be a girl go to college focus on school and live at home but following her expectations doesnt make me feel happy or fulfilled
Response: it seems like you are struggling with the pressure of meeting your mothers expectations which conflict with your own goals and desires remember that its essential to live a life that feels authentic and fulfilling for you it might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with your mom about your feelings and aspirations is there a specific concern you have that makes it difficult for you to express your thoughts to her

Context: i feel like people often say things like i could never do that or youre so brave when they find out im trans i think theyre trying to compliment me but it sometimes comes across as if theyre saying my life is so difficult and they couldnt handle it
Response: its important to remember that people may have good intentions when they make those comments but they might not realize the impact their words have on you try to focus on the positive aspects of their intentions such as their admiration for your strength however if you feel the need you can also gently educate them about the implications of their words and how it makes you feel remember youre in charge of your narrative and can choose how to respond to these comments

Context: i feel like people think im brave for continuing to be myself socially even when ive been ostracized and disowned by my family its hard without my support system and i feel like a lone wolf
Response: its admirable that youre staying true to yourself despite the challenges youre facing with being ostracized and losing your support system its undoubtedly difficult to go through this and your resiliency shows courage can you tell me more about how you cope with feeling like a lone wolf and any strategies youve found to build a new support system

Context: as a person who transitioned i am worried about the upcoming christmas family gathering because half of my family is not aware of my transition additionally i was adopted which adds more complexity to the situation
Response: its completely understandable that you are feeling anxious about the family gathering especially with the added complexity of being adopted its important to recognize your own feelings and have a support system in place would you like to discuss strategies for handling the reactions of your family members during the gathering

Context: i see my mom circling the idea of openness and progressiveness being more tolerant towards socially unacceptable things over the years shes become more accepting of gay people and stuff but the other day she was talking about prop a and how she doesnt think we should have to govern anything and thats not our business i feel like she might need a companion in her journey of becoming more openminded
Response: it sounds like your mom is slowly becoming more openminded and accepting of different viewpoints which is a positive development this can be a challenging process for some people and having a supportive companion can make a big difference have you talked with her about your feelings and the possibility of supporting her in this journey

Context: i came out as a lesbian when i was 15 and later as trans my mom initially asked if i could just be a lesbian she didnt fully support my transition at first but in the last couple of months she seems to have come a long way
Response: it sounds like your mom is gradually coming to terms with your identity even though her initial reaction wasnt supportive it can take time for some family members to understand and accept these changes is there something specific that has happened recently that makes you feel shes more accepting now

Context: ever since i was younger my family has been really focused on image they care about how you dress how you talk and how you conduct yourself i specifically remember my mom telling me at my dads funeral not to cry or make a scene in front of his friends
Response: it sounds like you grew up in a family where appearances and maintaining a certain image were very important this might have been difficult for you especially during emotional times like your dads funeral its important to acknowledge and validate your feelings even if your family might not have been supportive in doing so are there any moments where this focus on image has significantly impacted your life

Context: i have realized that a specific memory has been entrenched in my mind which shows me how significant other peoples opinions on me are and how much i should care about them
Response: its interesting that you feel so strongly about other peoples opinions do you often find yourself focusing too much on what others think instead of what you feel is true for yourself remember its important to listen to our own needs and desires rather than seeking validation and approval from others this will allow you to build a stronger inner sense of self and create a more meaningful life experience

Context: i feel like she cant break free from the systems that blind her due to power and gender also i believe shes smarter than she lets on and is pretty progressive for a chineseamerican born in the us but im not sure what to make of it
Response: it sounds like she may be holding back her true self due to societal pressures and expectations surrounding power and gender as a counsellor i would encourage her to explore these feelings and her own identity helping her recognize her strengths and what makes her unique we could also talk about ways to navigate these systems while staying true to herself by the way what specific systems do you think shes being affected by

Context: i have a family member she was born in 1939 and didnt actually grow up speaking english
Response: thank you for sharing about your family member its interesting to learn about her background especially considering the challenges she may have faced growing up during that time and without english as her first language if you have any specific concerns relating to her language development or any other aspect please feel free to ask

Context: i feel better because i have been accepting changes moving on and not holding on to the past i think its a sign that i am growing and learning and i celebrate that change
Response: its great to hear that youre embracing change and personal growth given your past can you share how recognizing that past has contributed to your current sense of growth and change this can help you gain deeper insights into your personal journey and keep moving forward

Context: lately i often doubt myself and the negative voice in my head tells me that im not growing or doing the right things however when i look back i realize that ive made good decisions and have put emotional effort into things it reminds me that im still a good person and passionate about what im doing and that im okay
Response: it seems like youre dealing with selfdoubt and negative thoughts but its good that youre able to reflect on your past decisions and recognize your growth and positive qualities remember to focus on the accomplishments and passions that make you who you are acknowledging these aspects of yourself can help quiet the negative voice and build selfconfidence are there any specific triggers for these negative thoughts that youve noticed

Context: this voice in my head tries to talk me out of things but when i take stock and look back at where ive been and where im headed i can embrace the chance it makes me feel good about myself and have faith in my abilities
Response: its fantastic that youre able to recognize the progress youve made and how it influences your selfworth and confidence keep focusing on your achievements and use them as a reminder of your capabilities when the negative voice arises is there a specific situation that youve recently faced where you successfully overcame this negative voice

Context: ive been struggling with the idea of transition in my life and im trying to look back and see where ive been and where im headed
Response: transitions can be challenging but taking time to reflect on your past and future can be helpful during this process as your counsellor id encourage you to think about the key moments and lessons youve learned so far what are some achievements or experiences youre proud of recognizing your strengths and accomplishments can give you guidance and confidence as you navigate this transition

Context: i havent told my mother that i carry so much of what she said her voice and values but the tricky part is that she always says actions speak louder than words and my interpretation of what she says differs from hers we used to go to counseling together and it was like pulling teeth
Response: its important to understand that communication can be challenging especially between parents and children as a counsellor i suggest having an open and honest conversation with your mother about your feelings but also recognizing that differences in interpretation are natural perhaps revisiting counseling together with a focus on improving communication could be beneficial for both of you

Context: i dont think my mom understands why im transitioning and she believes its wrong because it doesnt fit with her expectations she doesnt know the values or meaning behind my actions and i think wed need a translator for her to understand the significance and meaning
Response: it sounds like theres a communication breakdown between you and your mom you might consider finding someone who could help facilitate a conversation with her to clarify your values and reasons behind your transition by sharing this information with her your relationship might improve and shell have the opportunity to better understand your journey its important to be open and honest while seeking common ground

Context: as a patient i wanted to clarify my understanding of being a translator in a conversation  that i am conveying my version of what you are teaching me
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate your effort to develop your understanding of the concept to answer your question when talking about the translator metaphor it refers to the idea of interpreting and translating different languages in a conversation its essential to be aware that everyone has their perspectives filters and understanding of things they hear or learn as a translator your role is to capture the essence of the teaching while adapting it to make sense with your unique perspective and experiences

Context: as a patient i attended aa meetings but i found some comments to be foolish im tired of people treating us as special or feeling sorry for us due to our disease the more i read about alcoholism the more i realize that no one knows exactly what it is so i might even say im alcoholdependent until theres a definitive agreement on the subject
Response: as a counsellor i understand that you may feel frustrated with the inconsistencies in the understanding of alcoholism its important to acknowledge that human nature can make things complicated and we are all just trying to learn and find the best path toward recovery what aspects of the aa meetings worked well for you if any or what kind of support would you prefer in your journey towards sobriety

Context: one of the things i didnt like about aa is that they wear it like a badge there is something to be proud of but theres nothing to be ashamed of but you certainly dont do some reverse pride on it i didnt see any difference between those people and normal people
Response: its understandable that you may not agree with how some people in aa choose to present their recovery its important to recognize that everyones journey is unique and what works for one person may not work for another however if youre finding it difficult to relate to others in aa maybe you could explore other support groups or resources that align more closely with your values and beliefs

Context: ive been thinking about how some methods work for certain people but not for me specifically it seems like it works for highly religious people who believe in higher powers and miracles who do you think these methods worked for
Response: its true that some methods can work better for certain individuals depending on their beliefs and values in the case you mentioned it seems that these methods resonate more with religious people possibly because their faith plays a significant role in their lives however we can explore other approaches that may be more appropriate for you focusing on your preferences and needs dont worry there are many different ways to address problems and find solutions that work for you

Context: i am not the type of person who believes some deity will come down and save me anytime i have problems for me there has to be a compelling reason for me to feel like its time to make a change
Response: its important to recognize our own beliefs and values when it comes to problemsolving and making changes in our lives while some people may rely on external forces your inclination to be persuaded by more tangible reasons demonstrates selfreliance and independence embrace this personal trait and use it to your advantage while seeking solutions to challenges you encounter

Context: ive been thinking that the best thing i could do is just start running again and really work on substituting habits instead of trying to get rid of one habit i find it more effective to replace it with another however i sometimes struggle with figuring out what to replace the old habit with and it can leave me feeling stuck
Response: its great that you recognize the effectiveness of habit substitution for yourself its natural to feel stuck sometimes when trying to find a new habit to replace an old one however its important to focus on finding healthy and productive habits that bring positive changes to your life have you considered any particular activities or hobbies that you might be interested in taking up to replace the old habit

Context: i have been getting upset with myself lately and its really bothering me in the past i joined soccer teams and played with people and that helped me feel better im thinking of doing the same now
Response: it seems like joining a soccer team has been a helpful coping strategy for you in the past if it has worked for you before it might be a good idea to give it another try however its also important to understand your triggers and why youre getting upset with yourself in the first place have you noticed any specific situations or thoughts that lead to this frustration

Context: i was in a program where most people were forced to be there and not on their free will so naturally they were resistant in order to get through the program we had to talk behave and do certain things to fit in and play the game
Response: it sounds like you were in an environment where many participants were not fully invested in the process due to being forced into it this could have influenced your experience as well as the overall effectiveness of the program for you how do you think this affected your ability to genuinely engage in the process and pursue personal growth

Context: im struggling with the idea of quitting cigarettes and alcohol even though i know its necessary in order to breathe better but i dont want to think about it
Response: its common to feel resistant to the idea of giving up substances like cigarettes and alcohol especially if theyve been a part of your life for a long time as a counsellor im here to help you through this process and guide you in finding healthier alternatives can you share any specific fears or concerns related to giving up these substances

Context: i sometimes feel like i just want to do something without thinking about it like is there any point in overthinking everything
Response: its natural to sometimes want to act without overthinking as overthinking can lead to stress and indecision its important to find a balance between thinking things through and taking action trusting your instincts can be helpful but make sure youre considering any potential consequences do you find that overthinking is affecting your daily life

Context: ive been struggling with procrastination when it comes to daily tasks like brushing my teeth and going to the gym it feels worse to think about doing these tasks than to just go ahead and do them
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some resistance when it comes to daily tasks its important to acknowledge that its okay to have these feelings and sometimes the best way to overcome this is to tell yourself to just do it perhaps setting up a routine or breaking tasks into smaller steps could be helpful in making them more manageable

Context: as a patient i have been thinking about going to sleep but i cannot fall asleep i hope that makes sense to you
Response: as a counsellor i understand that youre having trouble falling asleep even though youre thinking about it its important to create a relaxing environment and follow a consistent bedtime routine to improve your sleep if youre struggling to fall asleep you can try deep breathing exercises meditation or reading a book to help calm your mind

Context: as the patient i feel like when im thinking about something or trying to do it im not actually doing it its like when i try to go to sleep but i cant
Response: as the counsellor i understand your concern it seems like overthinking or trying too hard is preventing you from actually doing things or falling asleep my suggestion would be to practice mindfulness or relaxation techniques to help you focus on the present moment and let go of any unnecessary thoughts do you have any specific situations where this occurs the most

Context: im struggling with this addiction and it just feels stupid that i keep on playing into it its like with alcohol ive reached a point where i know its not worth it anymore but the addiction persists
Response: its understandable that youre frustrated with the addiction but try not to be too hard on yourself addiction can be challenging to overcome and its great that youve recognized its not worth it with alcohol have you considered seeking professional help or joining a support group to help you deal with your addiction

Context: i used to drink all the time but then i stopped and noticed how much better i felt now i can compare and contrast how i felt when i was drinking and how i feel when im clearheaded
Response: its great to hear that youve realized the benefits of not drinking and staying clearheaded you should be proud of yourself for making this change please let me know if you need any support moving forward or if you have any concerns about maintaining this positive change in your life

Context: ive been comparing myself with and without a certain thing and noticing the difference in my performance it only becomes a problem for me when i see its impact on my performance other peoples opinions dont matter much
Response: its important to trust your own judgment about whether the situation is a problem for you or not rather than just focusing on the pros and cons of the performance difference consider if this is affecting other aspects of your life as well ultimately you should make the decision based on your needs and wellbeing

Context: as the patient i am having trouble understanding your approach towards addiction counseling i just wonder if sometimes people do not want help or if they sometimes push away from the help being offered to them
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concern its important to remember that its human nature to push against something when they feel pressured our approach is to be empathetic and nonconfrontational recognizing each persons individual situation and needs its possible that some people might not be ready for help but our job is to create a supportive environment where they can eventually accept assistance in their journey towards recovery

Context: im not really sure if i want to change because i dont see much harmful effects of my addiction i heard that its progressive and supposed to get worse but thats just not the case with me however i think my addiction to smoking is starting to become a problem as i recently started playing soccer
Response: its normal to feel unsure about change especially when you dont see immediate harmful effects however some consequences develop over time and are not always apparent at the beginning engaging in activities you enjoy like soccer can help you recognize the effects your addiction has on your life reflect on how your addiction may be impacting these important areas of your life and consider whether making a change is worth it for you

Context: i cant breathe because the kids are younger and younger and theyre half my age twice my size im having a problem with it
Response: i understand youre struggling with the age and size differences of the children around you its important to remember that everyones experience is unique and the message about not using at all might not fit your situation could you please clarify what you mean by use at all

Context: i guess you really know nothing about me do you i thought at least they filled you in with some kind or something
Response: i apologize if i seemed uninformed about your situation i have not been given any specific information about you however i am here to listen and help you with any issues youd like to discuss please feel free to share your thoughts and concerns so we can work through them together

Context: i got a dui a while back in 93 and i had one prior to that in 85 im worried about how this is affecting me and what i should do to avoid future issues
Response: i understand that having multiple duis can be concerning its essential to recognize the underlying factors that led to these incidents and work on addressing them you might consider seeking support from a therapist attending alcoholics anonymous meetings or joining a support group to create a positive environment and prevent future occurrences

Context: lately ive been thinking about how everything in life is predictable and sometimes even negative experiences like bad habits relationships and jobs can become addicting because they are familiar
Response: it sounds like youre noticing a pattern in your life where you might be drawn to familiar yet unhealthy situations this could be because our brains often seek comfort in what is known even if its not good for us if youd like to break this cycle its important to be aware of these patterns and consider exploring new healthier experiences and habits is there a specific area in your life where youd like to start making changes

Context: i think im living in a bad area or town and its familiar to me but its not the terrible change that scares me as im growing older i know i cant keep up with the young crowd and ive started saving money in a bank account and even had a college scholarship which i didnt take
Response: i understand your concerns about living in a familiar yet possibly negative environment and growing older its natural to feel scared of change and unsure about the future however its great that youve started saving and had opportunities like a college scholarship it might be helpful to explore what you truly desire in life and consider making small manageable changes to improve your situation and overall wellbeing

Context: ive always had a bank account and put a lot into it but ive been withdrawing from it for a long time and the balance is getting low i think i can only do this for so long before i start feeling the effects and now im not so sure
Response: its good that you realize the importance of replenishing your resources both financially and emotionally its common to feel drained after a period of constant withdrawals without replenishing can you think of any steps you can take to fill up your bank account again and restore your energy and resources

Context: ive been feeling really stressed about my finances lately and i dont want to go into debt i think it would be helpful to do a followup on my financial situation to get a better understanding of my options
Response: its understandable that youre feeling stressed about your finances and its good that youre seeking help to address this concern i would recommend scheduling a followup session where we can dive deeper into your financial situation explore potential solutions and provide you with tools and resources to help you make informed decisions to avoid unnecessary debt

Context: i think it has become important enough for me now to address this issue or else i wouldnt even be thinking about it in the first place i dont really care about my health but i cannot stand if im not the fastest guy out there i have an identity crisis in that sense and im using my arrogance conceit and pride to help me
Response: it sounds like the issue youre facing has finally reached a level of importance for you to take action it seems like youre using your competitive nature and certain negative traits like arrogance and pride as motivation to overcome the problem my question for you is do you think relying on these negative traits is a sustainable way to cope with your situation

Context: i feel like people are too focused on living healthy lives just for the sake of pride and not for their overall wellbeing honestly i dont really care about it since everyone dies eventually im just tired of people making a big deal out of living forever even though theyre not doing what it takes to have a high quality of life
Response: its understandable that you feel frustrated with how some people approach their health primarily out of vanity and not genuine concern for their wellbeing while its true that everyone eventually dies focusing only on that aspect can be limiting its essential to find a balance between living a fulfilling life and maintaining ones health what in your opinion would define a high quality of life for you

Context: i think waking up healthy and being able to do what i want would be nice i would like to do that forever but i know its not possible and accept that for me its more about the quality of life than longevity
Response: it sounds like you have made up your mind to some extent and prioritize quality of life over longevity this is an important realization however i would like to ask you if theres any specific aspect or area of your life youd like to improve to enhance your overall quality of life

Context: im coming here today because my friend told me about the study you guys are doing and as an addiction counselor he thought i might be an interesting subject im not currently in recovery
Response: thank you for coming in and sharing this information with me it sounds like your friend cares about your wellbeing and believes that participating in this study might be helpful for you as an addiction counselor id like to learn more about your experience with addiction and how it affects your life can you please tell me more about your addiction and any challenges youve faced

Context: i have been struggling with cigarette addiction and i used to have problems with alcohol but that has reduced significantly in the past couple of years i believe it might be because of changes in my environment
Response: its great to hear that your alcohol problem has improved over the years as for cigarette addiction it could certainly have a significant effect on your health what specific changes in your environment do you think helped reduce your alcohol consumption and do you think similar changes could help with the cigarette issue

Context: i feel like im not able to keep up with things anymore and i think its because im getting too old
Response: its understandable that you might feel overwhelmed and unable to keep up as you age however its important to recognize your strengths and focus on what you can still do you may want to consider adapting or modifying your activities to better suit your current abilities also remember that its never too late to learn new skills or engage in activities you enjoy age shouldnt define what you can or cannot do

Context: i really dont think i can i really do think that cigarettes are worse for me in the past ive done cocaine and even crack cocaine ive heard its one of the most addictive drugs but from my personal experience i dont find it addictive at all for me its tobacco and alcohol

Context: i feel like my partner appreciates the little things i do for her like making her lunch and having meaningful conversations i think she also likes that i am a feeling person and can express my emotions

Context: i have noticed that the opportunities for teasing have changed i feel like people around me have become more mature and i have to adjust to this

Context: im not feeling very good this week my wife sharon wants to go to a state nursing conference and will be away with her friends for a couple of nights im upset because i feel like her actions are negatively affecting our marriage

Context: i am feeling upset because my partner said she doesnt want me with her for a weekend it doesnt feel good to be left alone for the weekend and i am worried about our future

Context: ive been sitting at home feeling bad and i dont know what to do i thought about mowing the lawn but im not sure if thats the right thing to do i just dont know

Context: when i think about being alone i feel incredibly sad and depressed my sadness is at a 90 out of 100 and my depression is at an 85 when i think about being left alone it also makes me very angry as high as a 95 out of 100

Context: i feel really depressed and sad because my partner is going to the conference and i feel abandoned i dont think theyre treating me fairly and it upsets me the most
