Context: this week i have been dealing with stomach issues and not feeling great so i didnt do the homework that we talked about i want to make changes and deal with my social anxiety but it seems like something always happens when im supposed to do something we discussed
Response: i understand that you are dealing with some health issues and its okay to prioritize your wellbeing we have been working together for about two months to address your social anxiety and plan social experiments its important to recognize that setbacks can happen and its essential to stay committed to making changes can you think of any alternative ways to practice the homework or modify it to accommodate your current situation

Context: ive been feeling afraid lately and i think it might be because im scared of not doing things right or not knowing how to do them i feel like this fear is preventing me from trying new things
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a fear of failure or not being able to perform tasks correctly this can be a difficult topic to discuss but its important to recognize these feelings its completely normal to feel uncertain about new experiences and the key is to not let that fear hinder your growth is there any particular situation where this fear has stopped you lately

Context: i am afraid that i might fail at being better socially this is the first time ive said that out loud i want to change especially for my boyfriend who has been complaining about my lack of socializing but i am really scared of not doing it right or failing
Response: its okay to feel afraid about change and i want to validate how scary it can be however i do believe you can achieve your goals maybe our initial plan was too ambitious so lets take a step back and reevaluate it we can come up with a new plan that helps you gradually improve your social skills while keeping your fears and concerns in mind

Context: i do want to have less anxiety in some situations but im not looking to be someone who goes out all the time and is really talkative i want to have less anxiety as it doesnt feel good but im also worried about letting you down if i dont agree with you
Response: its important to focus on what you truly want for yourself your goal should be about feeling comfortable and less anxious in situations rather than trying to please others or fit a certain mold if we work together to identify specific situations that cause anxiety and address them we can help you achieve your goals without worrying about letting anyone down

Context: i dont want to do that it doesnt feel good to do that however i would like to figure out why i get so anxious in certain situations
Response: thats completely fine its important that we work on a plan that youre comfortable with lets focus on understanding the reasons behind your anxiety in certain situations also please know that youre not going to disappoint me our work together is about helping you overcome your challenges and grow

Context: as the patient i feel that when it comes to being trans and genderqueer its about picking your battles i sometimes wish i had never come out to my mother because it would be easier to pretend with her i need to see more effort from her before i feel like i can change the way i interact with her
Response: as a counsellor i understand your perspective on picking battles with your mother about your gender identity its completely valid to feel that way however it is important to consider if avoiding conflict is the best thing for you and if you would like to try anything different in the relationship do you think theres any particular reason why your mother might struggle with understanding or putting in the effort you need

Context: im glad i have the opportunity to talk with you i try to pick my battles as ive learned from our conversations over the past few months i sometimes struggle with my relationships but i want to improve and learn how to approach certain situations
Response: its great that youre coming here to discuss these issues and ive noticed a significant growth in your ability to open up and process your thoughts you dont have to make any immediate changes its okay to be where youre currently at in the future you may want to improve your relationships but for now focus on meeting others where theyre at and considering when to take a step back we can continue working through this journey together in our future sessions

Context: as a patient i feel like i dont use good coping mechanisms for my wellbeing and i often feel continually exhausted while i have established great circles of social support i still struggle with handling negative feelings
Response: as a counsellor i understand how difficult it can be to find effective coping mechanisms its great that you have a strong social support system in place in order to help you find better coping methods i would like to inquire whether you have tried any specific strategies in the past additionally it might be helpful to explore some relaxation techniques such as deep breathing or journaling to help manage the negative feelings you are experiencing

Context: i feel better with support networks but still struggle with continuous confusion discrimination and misunderstanding i talk to my support networks regularly about specific instances of transphobia or homophobia but everyday glances or offensive comments dont always come up in conversations with people who have similar experiences
Response: its good that you have support networks to talk to about your experiences its normal for routine discrimination not to be discussed as much but its important to address the impact of those daily incidents too are there any coping strategies you use for managing the stress of everyday discrimination or any resources or activities that help you build resilience against those experiences

Context: sometimes i find it hard to draw the line between what is worth processing and what is something that i can put aside i think we all have a mutual understanding of what we are feeling but im not sure if i should always fully process those feelings
Response: its natural to feel unsure about which feelings to process and which to put aside its good that you have a support system to share those feelings with sometimes just acknowledging the feelings can be helpful however if you feel that some emotions are impacting your life or wellbeing its essential to process them further dont hesitate to seek additional support or guidance if needed

Context: ive been struggling with my familys reaction to my identity when i notice someone being insensitive they feel judged and say that im not giving them a chance i feel like ive given them enough chances but im not ready to be vulnerable with them after a turning point on thanksgiving my family became aware of my identity and they mostly avoid talking to or about me i think theyre nervous about it
Response: it sounds like youve faced some challenges with your family regarding your identity and their reactions have made it difficult for you to open up emotionally its understandable that their avoidance of conversations about you might make you feel uneasy in a situation like this one option could be to express your feelings calmly and honestly to them maybe you could ask them about the reasons for their nervousness and try to find a way to communicate openly about each others needs and concerns

Context: i didnt believe my mom was trying to understand my pronouns and chosen name at first but now im starting to believe her it originally seemed like she would only use them when talking to me but not with other people during thanksgiving it felt like a turning point even though everything hasnt improved completely my whole family is now aware of my identity but they mostly try not to talk to me or about me
Response: it sounds like youve experienced some progress with your mom even though it hasnt been perfect change can be difficult so its important to acknowledge the steps shes taking towards understanding as for your extended family its possible that they might not know how to approach the conversation yet would you like to discuss ways to engage with them and help them understand your identity better

Context: i felt ignored and invisible when my family would not talk to me about my feelings or ask me any questions it seemed easier for them to just not acknowledge it and go along with everything else
Response: i can understand how that would feel hurtful and isolating its important to feel heard and acknowledged by the people who are close to you can you think of a time when there was open communication with your family or perhaps consider discussing your feelings with a trusted family member to start the conversation

Context: i have been okay i recently came back from a holiday weekend with my family where we did thanksgiving together it was an interesting experience because my family dynamic has changed since my mom has started to come around in terms of accepting my gender identity and using my chosen name ray
Response: its good to hear that you had an okay experience during the holiday and its positive that there has been a change in your family dynamics due to your mothers acceptance of your gender identity can you share more examples of how your mother has shown her change in thinking or how it has affected your relationship with her

Context: i have been trying to make my partner understand the importance of using my preferred pronouns and addressing me by my correct name and gender weve been going back and forth about this for the last year i initially started off gently but gradually became more insistent as the issue was seriously compromising our relationship it seems like my partner is not making any effort to understand and engage with me on this matter
Response: i understand that this situation can be difficult for you its important for your partner to acknowledge and respect your identity for a healthy relationship have you tried having an open and honest conversation about why shes resisting and what consequences it might have on your relationship sometimes understanding where the resistance is coming from can help address the issue more effectively and seeking the support of a couples therapist might also be a good option

Context: about a month before thanksgiving i hadnt seen my family member for a few months because i was planning to cut her out of my life she started talking to me a little bit about it realizing what was going on and the high stakes involved she told me she was going to tell the family that i prefer ray and used they around me she also said she had been looking at resources online to understand queer and genderqueer identities
Response: it seems like your family member is making an effort to understand and support your preferred name and gender identity which is a positive sign its important to acknowledge this progress while setting boundaries for your relationship do you feel comfortable talking to her about how her actions may have hurt you in the past and establishing rules for your interactions going forward

Context: i didnt really believe her at first i didnt understand where that change came from
Response: its natural to feel skeptical when someone close to you makes a surprising change can you tell me more about the situation and how it has affected your relationship with her

Context: i feel uncomfortable talking about my gender queer identity i internalized these feelings which makes me physically uncomfortable during interactions i believe my discomfort is always related to my body and im not always actively aware of when i internalize these feelings
Response: its normal to feel discomfort when discussing sensitive topics like your gender identity it seems like youre aware of how you internalize your feelings and how it affects your body can you think of any strategies or coping mechanisms that youve used in the past to manage this discomfort it might be helpful to explore these further to handle similar situations in the future

Context: i notice that when certain issues arent pointed out i eventually feel frustrated sad and angry due to feeling rejected this impacts my tolerance of other things that bother me and manifests itself in unexpected ways which can be quite distracting
Response: it sounds like you are dealing with a lot of stressors in your life along with the added burden of feeling rejected and its consequences its important to understand that its natural to feel frustrated and overwhelmed in such situations have you considered exploring healthy coping strategies or seeking professional help to manage these feelings and improve your overall wellbeing

Context: i tend to close off and disassociate from family situations as theres an anticipated misunderstanding from my family they dont seem to notice when i do this and i feel isolated because they dont reach out to me
Response: it sounds awful that your family isnt supportive of you and you feel isolated within your own family whats it like talking about this situation with me do you feel empowered by discussing it with someone who understands

Context: i feel that gender is such a complicated thing and its really personal i appreciate when someone is interested in understanding the intricacies of my own personal gender although its hard for people to completely understand what im feeling i also dont like the secrecy and hiding in some situations like with my family i would prefer them to say transphobic things to my face so that i can explain myself and maybe enlighten them a little bit
Response: thank you for sharing your experience with gender and your feelings about transparency in conversations its important to acknowledge that gender is a personal and complex topic it sounds like youre eager to have open and honest discussions with your family which is a healthy approach can you tell me more about any efforts youve made to communicate with your family about your thoughts and feelings on gender

Context: im feeling frustrated because i cant openly discuss my family situation with my mother as i lack the financial and emotional stability to sever ties instead i feel like i just have to conceal everything and not talk about it
Response: its understandable that you feel frustrated about not being able to openly communicate with your mother its essential to find ways to cope with and manage this feeling are there any support systems or outlets for you to express your emotions and address the situation without putting your stability at risk

Context: im a student of psychology and i feel uncomfortable and dissatisfied with the field of psychology its confusing and makes me not want to spend time at school i study social and cultural psychology but i cant claim my own experience it causes me to feel resentful about the work i put my time and energy into
Response: it sounds like youre struggling with feeling comfortable in your field of study and perhaps having a difficult time connecting your personal experiences with your academic work its important to feel safe when discussing these issues so im glad you feel okay talking about it with me do you think that finding trusted people to discuss your experiences with might help you feel less resentful and more engaged in your studies

Context: i feel really isolated and its different talking to someone outside of my close circles i have to put on a shield and expect to be misunderstood when im not in a safe space with my friends
Response: it sounds like you have a support system within your group of friends but you still experience feelings of isolation and the need to protect yourself in other situations this is a valid concern as people might not always be understanding or open to your experiences as a counsellor my goal is to offer you a safe and nonjudgmental environment where you can feel free to express yourself without the fear of being misunderstood

Context: as a patient i want to express that i dont want to feel judged by people but i know that its inevitable im here to share how im feeling and the struggles im going through its difficult to internalize these negative emotions and it feels heavy and exhausting how should i cope with these things
Response: as your counsellor i understand that youre worried about being judged and its putting a strain on you first of all its great that youre here and willing to discuss your feelings and concerns coping mechanisms may differ from person to person but a good way to start could be to focus on developing a strong support system practicing selfcare and seeking positive interactions with others do you have a support system in place that you can rely on when you need help

Context: i feel like theres a barrier between me and nonqueer or cis people i want them to ask questions to better understand my experiences but i often find that they dont im willing to teach them the language im using but i need to see that theyre genuinely interested
Response: its completely understandable that you require trust and a genuine interest from others in understanding your experiences as a counsellor if i dont have similar experiences i would do my best to ask questions and actively learn from you showing that im truly committed to understanding and empathizing with your perspective what specific questions would you appreciate being asked in these conversations to help bridge that barrier

Context: i felt that they want to learn themselves from the situation
Response: its great to hear that you are observing the other individuals in the situation wanting to learn and grow thank you for sharing this perspective can you provide more details about how this learning process has influenced or impacted you or the situation overall

Context: i felt reasonably comfortable talking with you today i think i have developed the discourse around my issues and its important to be talking to people who share that discourse or have familiarity with it if this conversation happened years ago before i developed this discourse and met others with similar experiences i would have more trouble vocalizing my needs and situating my experiences within a narrative
Response: im glad you felt comfortable talking with me today its great to see that youve developed a discourse around your issues and that you find value in connecting with people who share similar experiences it sounds like youve made significant progress in being able to vocalize your needs and situate your experiences within a narrative are there any particular challenges or scenarios in which you still find it difficult to express yourself and your needs

Context: as a patient i need a therapist who understands my language and the way i talk about my experiences i want to feel heard and not like im being educated or led in a direction that doesnt feel authentic to me its important that i come to my own understanding within the context of my life and social circles
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate your need for a therapist who understands your unique experiences and language i strive to create an environment where you feel heard respected and supported in your journey towards selfunderstanding my approach is not to educate or lead you but rather to facilitate your own growth and insight by listening and asking thoughtprovoking questions tailored to your experience could you please elaborate on what specific aspects of your experiences you would like me to focus on

Context: i prefer having a therapist who identifies as queer themselves because it makes me feel safer and more understood i find it harder to build trust with people who arent queer but once trust is earned with a queer therapist i feel more comfortable opening up to them
Response: i understand how important trust is in a therapeutic relationship and having a therapist who shares your queer identity can definitely help foster that trust it is crucial for you to feel safe and comfortable with your therapist for effective therapy if you need further information or have specific concerns please feel free to share so i can better address your needs

Context: i think in general im treated differently than other people that i see which is the result of a bunch of different things i live an alternative lifestyle which i think is very intertwined with my gender i choose to put myself in social circles where people feel similarly and theyre accepting but when i leave those circles im always shocked at what the real world is like and feel overlooked
Response: it sounds like you are having difficulty feeling accepted and understood in settings outside of your chosen social circles it can be challenging when people treat you differently because of your lifestyle and gender remember that you are not alone in this experience and you can seek out supportive communities to help you navigate this complex social landscape can you think of any strategies to cope with these feelings when youre outside of your comfortable social circles

Context: im a graduate student and i feel like the black sheep of my program my gender is unacknowledged and in those situations im read as queer or lesbian i dont feel safe correcting people
Response: i understand that youre feeling invalidated and unsafe in your academic environment due to the misperception of your gender identity its crucial to have a supportive space where you can express your true self could you share an instance when you tried to address this issue with someone and how they responded

Context: i dont feel like its me when people use the wrong pronouns for me and its confusing i think of it as a role i play i have separate lives  my school life and my personal life and i dont participate in school the way i would if i felt safe to come out there
Response: it seems like youre struggling with people not understanding your true self and using the wrong pronouns which makes you feel like youre playing a role its tough to balance these two separate worlds of school and personal life im wondering if there are any supportive individuals at school or any resources that could help make it a more inclusive and safer environment for you

Context: i feel like this new change is going to be the creation of me its going to be the next step in my life on my own even though ive been on my own i never felt like i was actually going to begin a path
Response: it sounds like youre excited about this new chapter of your life and being more independent embracing change can be very empowering opening up to new dimensions of who you can be is there a particular aspect of this new path that youre most looking forward to

Context: in my new life i would hope to actually create my own family begin a new career and just be myself
Response: it sounds like you have ambitious goals for your new life including starting a family and pursuing a new career these are significant changes that can bring fulfillment and happiness as your counsellor i am here to support and guide you through the process what do you think could be the first step towards achieving this new life you envision

Context: ive been focused on doing my part in the family to keep us together and i never thought a different future would be a possibility now that im considering it its both scary and exciting
Response: its normal to feel a mix of fear and excitement when facing a new possibility embrace the excitement and try to envision how this different future could look for you while also acknowledging and working through the fear remember its okay to explore different paths in life

Context: i have always been focused on taking care of my mom and the kids and never imagined myself moving away from that mentality but now im starting to see and envision a different life for myself and it makes me smile
Response: its great to see that youre exploring new possibilities for yourself and feeling excited about it personal growth and finding happiness in new experiences is important what led you to start considering a different path and what are some ideas you have for this new chapter in your life

Context: ive been struggling with the idea of pulling away from my family but im worried that it might make me feel alone
Response: feeling alone is a natural concern when considering distancing yourself from your family its important to think about why you want to pull away and evaluate if its necessary for your wellbeing are there any specific issues with your family that you would like to discuss to better understand your emotions and analyze potential outcomes

Context: i have been struggling with being pulled in different directions upon reflecting on this conversation i realized its more about finding myself and understanding why this bothers me so much it seems that the values my mom instilled in me are the reason i feel this way if i hadnt learned those values it wouldnt be such a difficult situation for me
Response: i appreciate your honesty and selfreflection during our conversation it seems that understanding the root of your struggle is an important step in moving forward instead of focusing on feeling pulled in different directions try to focus on the values that you have learned from your mother and consider what you truly want also remember that its okay to set boundaries and prioritize your own needs are there any specific situations where you feel this struggle is more prominent

Context: i am trying to understand how i can be pulled and it helps me reinforce and prove to my mom that i am still the person that she raised and i havent changed
Response: its great to see that youre finding this helpful in understanding your connection with your upbringing its natural to evolve and grow as a person but staying true to the core values and principles youve been raised with is important keep reflecting on how your experiences are shaping you is there a specific aspect of your upbringing or relationship with your mom that youd like to explore further

Context: i have been trying to live up to my mothers expectations and fulfill what she wanted for me in my life i listened to everything she ever told me and now i am doing my best to fulfill her expectations as i grow up
Response: thank you for sharing such an intimate decision and its powerful impact on your life it speaks to who you are whats important to you and how you are seeking to honor complex threads of value in your life i appreciate that you shared this with me at this time do you feel that fulfilling your mothers expectations is causing any challenges or stress in your life

Context: as we talk about my relationship with my mother and why its so important i think thats whats making me lean towards this new life if it had been a male she would have asked or pushed me to work on that
Response: it sounds like your mother has a significant influence on your life and decisions can you tell me more about how your relationship with her affects your choice to move towards this new life

Context: i feel scared thinking about losing my family and not having anyone to share my pain with i think i need to put my family on pause to see if thats the happiness im going to get but i dont want them to be out of the picture completely and i know i dont have total control over the situation
Response: its understandable that the thought of losing your family is frightening but its good that youre considering whats best for your happiness remember putting your family on pause doesnt mean removing them from your life entirely its important to take time for selfreflection to understand your own needs while also acknowledging that you cant control every aspect of the situation try focusing on what you can control and find ways to better manage your fears and emotions

Context: i would like to embrace this new direction in my life but i also want to make sure that my heart remains open to my family and especially to my mom is that a fair summary
Response: yes thats a fair summary its important to find a balance between personal growth and maintaining connections with your loved ones moving forward with your goals doesnt mean leaving your family behind its about embracing change while keeping your familys wellbeing in mind do you have any concerns about how to maintain this balance

Context: as the patient i feel a sense of responsibility to advocate for my friend and i would like to find ways on how to push on her behalf
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concern for your friend and your desire to help its important to carefully consider various approaches for providing support if we had more time we could delve into more detail about potential ways to advocate for your friend and develop a plan that is beneficial for both of you

Context: i am struggling to decide whether to maintain a relationship with my family or to create a new life for myself and my partner distancing myself from some hurtful and difficult aspects of my family this decision is related to whether or not to speak to my mother about my sexual orientation
Response: i understand that youre facing a complex decision involving your family and your own wellbeing it seems like there are two sides one is maintaining your relationship with your family while also caring for their feelings and the other is creating a new life for yourself and your partner distancing from the hurtful aspects of your family since this decision is also related to speaking with your mother about your sexual orientation would you mind sharing how that conversation might impact your choice

Context: i made the coming out decision because of my feelings for my partner and my desire to have unity with them and my family family is very important to me
Response: thank you for sharing that with me it seems that you made this decision based on your strong love for your partner and your deep value for family unity was there anything else that influenced your decision or was your primary motivation the hope for unity with your partner and family

Context: i had hope in my family especially with my mom accepting my siblings choices in their significant others even with the mistakes that weve all made it felt like she would accept the good and the bad and it made me hopeful for our relationships
Response: it sounds like you feel a sense of hope and comfort knowing that your mother has been accepting and understanding of your siblings and their choices in relationships this seems to contribute to your overall feelings of optimism for the future of your family do you feel that this hope helps you in handling your own relationships and personal growth

Context: recently ive been struggling with my relationship with myself and feeling responsible for everything i feel like there might be other people who view me differently and have different stories about me im curious if this could be woven into a different account or perspective on my situation
Response: its natural for people to have different perceptions of us and it can be helpful to explore those alternative viewpoints to gain a deeper understanding of ourselves by engaging in conversations and listening to others perspectives you could potentially discover new aspects of your identity and challenge your feelings of responsibility it might be beneficial to connect with those people and learn more about their experiences with you to gain a broader understanding of your situation

Context: as a patient i wanted to tell you about an introduction to externalizing and i also learned about counter stories
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate you sharing the introduction to externalizing and counter stories externalizing helps in separating the problem from the person which allows exploring the issue without judgment and guilt counter stories can be empowering as they challenge the dominant or negative stories about yourself enabling you to rewrite your narrative positively its essential to embrace these techniques and continue discussing them in our sessions if you have any concerns or areas you want to focus on feel free to mention them

Context: im trying to make a decision but sometimes after making one other decisions appear that i never thought of one decision always leads to another and sometimes the next one is harder than the previous one this has been my experience
Response: its common for decisions to lead to other choices and sometimes they can be more challenging can you provide a specific example of a decision you made and the subsequent more difficult decisions that arose from it this will help us understand and address your concerns better

Context: i recently decided to tell my mom that i am gay because i started a relationship with someone in the past i figured if i didnt listen to anybody then what my mom would have to think wouldnt matter but i initially took it hard and expected all of that
Response: it sounds like you have taken a significant step by coming out to your mom and it might have been difficult for you how did your mom react to the news and how are you handling her reaction remember its important to give her time to process this information while also taking care of your own emotional wellbeing

Context: i recently made a decision that my mother is finding hard to accept now i have to decide if i want to continue being a part of my family or pull away and start my own family my mother wants to pretend that my decision doesnt exist and this is making it difficult for my significant other to be a part of my life
Response: it seems like youre facing a difficult choice between maintaining the connection with your family while accommodating your mothers denial or prioritizing your significant other and creating a new family would you like to discuss possible ways to bring your mother to accept your decision while preserving your relationships or share more about what this decision means for you and the potential consequences of each choice

Context: i have been struggling with the idea of making a new life and continuing the family life i always had because im worried about the burden and strain it might put on my new relationship
Response: i understand your concerns about the impact of maintaining your family life on your new relationship its important to have open and honest communication with your partner about your expectations and their thoughts on the matter this will help both of you be on the same page and make informed decisions about your future together is there anything specific about your family life that makes you feel particularly concerned

Context: as the patient i feel that there are certain aspects of my life where i exhibit responsibility but i still struggle with tardiness i would like to explore these exceptions and understand how responsibility plays a role in various aspects of my life
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate your insight into your strengths and areas that need improvement since it seems like responsibility could be a counterstory in your life lets explore the instances where you have displayed responsible behaviors and figure out if there are any patterns or learnings that you can apply to improve your tardiness issue this way we can work together to help you build on your strengths while addressing the challenges in a more positive way

Context: ive been feeling a bit overwhelmed lately with everything going on in my life i tend to focus on my responsibilities but recently ive been trying to explore my curiosity instead however i feel like im struggling to find that balance between responsibility and curiosity
Response: its important to find a balance between your responsibilities and curiosity i understand that it can be challenging when you feel overwhelmed with different aspects of your life can you think of ways you can incorporate your curiosity into your daily routine while still fulfilling your responsibilities this might help you find the balance youre searching for

Context: i have been feeling out of place due to my punctuality in my family they have a different approach to time management and it has been bothering me as it makes me stand out
Response: it seems like punctuality is an important value for you but it is causing some friction in your relationship with your family perhaps we could explore what punctuality means to you and your family and how it is affecting your relationship can you share more about the specific incidents or situations where this difference has caused challenges for you

Context: i have been struggling with feeling responsible for everything happening around me and its affecting my relationships with others i dont know how to deal with this
Response: its important to recognize that its not possible for you to be responsible for every aspect of your life or the lives of others it might help to externalize these feelings and consider how they may be related to a social domain or context this way you can start to understand the origin of these feelings and begin to shift your perspective can you think of any specific situations where this sense of responsibility has affected your relationships

Context: i introduced my partner to my mom at my birthday dinner my mom throws a dinner for me every year and it was during that time when my partner and i were working together my mom was talking with all my friends at the party and some of them already knew her my partner and my mom just grabbed a cup of coffee and sat at the kitchen table while the rest of us were outside
Response: it sounds like you were able to create a comfortable environment for your partner and your mom to meet during your birthday dinner its great that they were able to engage in conversation and bond over a cup of coffee how did you feel about their interaction did you notice any change in your relationship with your partner or your mom after the introduction

Context: i was sitting and feeling all inside of it the next day my mom made a comment about whether to speak to her or not im not too sure about the whole conversation but she remembered her and thats when it counts
Response: it seems like youre reflecting on a recent conversation with your mom that had some emotional significance for you its important that you take some time to process those feelings and try to understand the implications of that conversation if you want to discuss the details further id be happy to help you explore any concerns or emotions surrounding the situation is there any particular aspect of the conversation that youd like to focus on

Context: i recently talked to my mom about my new partner it was a significant moment for me because she has memory issues and she seemed to remember our conversation she even made room in her consciousness for my partner which made me happy
Response: its great to hear that your mother was able to remember your conversation and acknowledge your partner it shows that despite her memory challenges she still cares about you and your life if youd like you can share how your mom reacted after you told her about your partner and if theres anything youd like to discuss further feel free to ask

Context: i didnt tell her that day it was a while after after my partner and i secured more of our relationship it was at a point where i wouldnt say pulling away it was more like i was starting to build the relationship which was taking time away from being able to spend time with my mom
Response: it sounds like you were focusing on building your relationship with your partner which might have made it difficult for you to find time for your mom its important to find a balance in our relationships and make sure everyones needs are met how did your mom react when you eventually told her about your relationship

Context: i was hoping considering my partners history that she would be accepting and open to me bringing my partner into the family however there are formalities involved in introducing them and i am worried about how the informal part before that will unfold
Response: its understandable that you are concerned about the informal part of introducing your partner to your family given your partners history its important to approach this process gently and patiently allowing time for trust and understanding to develop remember you have a supportive role in this and can help facilitate open communication between your partner and family

Context: lately ive been taking my partner to generic parties so that my family especially my mom can get to know them better this is a kind of interaction that my family expects from me and my partner im wondering if this is a common thing to do for other peoples fiances too
Response: yes its common for families to want to get to know their loved ones partners especially in the context of a serious relationship or engagement its great that youre making an effort to include your partner in these social events and helping your family bond with them have you had any previous experience with introducing a partner to your family or is this the first time youve tried this approach

Context: i was hopeful that my mom would get along well with my partner since they both share a similar background of being born in mexico and coming from a small town my partner embodies many qualities that my mom would want for me in a partner so i thought that would help them bond
Response: its understandable that you were hopeful for a connection between your mom and partner given their shared background and your partners qualities that your mom values how did their interactions go after they met were there any specific instances where you saw them bonding or facing challenges in their relationship

Context: ive always been told by my mom to find someone who shares the same likes family values and education as me and who can always make me laugh
Response: its wonderful that your mom has given you guidance on finding a compatible partner its important to have shared interests and values in a relationship as well as a sense of humor are there any specific concerns you have about finding such a partner or is this approach working well for you

Context: i feel like we only briefly touched on my story during our conversation and i noticed that there wasnt enough time to develop the counter story
Response: i understand that our conversation was brief and we didnt get to fully explore your counter story if we had more time i would have wanted to explore in more detail the conversations you have with yourself about the situation can you share any thoughts or feelings that arise when you think about your story and how it might be different

Context: as a patient i need help in exploring my preferences and understanding my future possibilities even if some might be sorrowful i notice there are contrasting aspects in my identity and would like to know more about these counter stories

Context: i feel a lot of pressure in my family to be punctual as everyone is always on time it stresses me out even if im just a few minutes late because of this im really worried about how it affects my work as i dont want to seem unreliable or irresponsible
Response: i can understand that punctuality is important in your family and its causing you worry in your work life to better understand how to handle this pressure can you provide any examples of how your family reacts or deals with situations when someone is late we can explore those situations and identify ways to alleviate the stress and find a balance

Context: over the years i have been struggling with an issue that has affected various aspects of my life such as work family friendships and my selfconcept it also influences my mood and the way i see myself
Response: thank you for sharing this information with me it sounds like this problem has had a significant impact on multiple areas of your life for quite some time im curious if you can identify specific instances when you first started noticing the issue and its effects and share more about how it has evolved throughout time gaining a deeper understanding of the history and progression of the issue will help us determine the most effective strategies to address it

Context: i have been experiencing a lot of pain lately and its been affecting different aspects of my life i started to discuss the issue with someone touching on various domains but i still feel like i havent fully explored the extent of the impact it has on me

Context: ive been feeling overwhelmed with different issues in my work life and family life i feel like we could discuss more aspects if we had more time together
Response: its understandable that youre feeling overwhelmed and that our time together was limited i think its important to further explore the effects these issues are having on you and your relationships with family and friends in future sessions if there is any specific topic that you believe requires immediate attention please let me know so we can prioritize it during our next meeting

Context: i have been feeling annoyed with myself lately and im not sure if this is helpful or not ive also been thinking about whether theres something i should be doing more or less of
Response: its normal to feel annoyed with oneself from time to time but its essential to determine whether its constructive or destructive can you share a specific example of when you felt annoyed with yourself and what you wanted to do differently this will help us assess if these feelings are helping you grow or holding you back

Context: i recently saw my mom and partner in a different light almost to the point where i didnt recognize my mom it was very painful for me because i had big hopes and love for both of them i even told my mom that my partner is the daughter she would have hoped for

Context: i feel like my partner has a characteristic that could make them really good friends with another person ive spoken with them about it and im not sure if they truly understood what i meant
Response: its great that you were open and communicative with your partner about your observations since you are unsure if they heard you or fully understood your point it might be helpful to revisit the conversation and clarify your thoughts did your partner respond in any specific way that made you think they might not have heard or understood you

Context: i feel like my mother believes that being gay is unnatural and unfulfilling and its affecting me negatively shes very traditional and thinks that not having a man in my life will prevent me from being successful
Response: it sounds like youre struggling with your mothers belief about your sexuality and her traditional views its important to remember that being gay is a natural and valid part of who you are i would suggest having an open and honest conversation with her to express your feelings do you feel comfortable talking to her about this

Context: ive been thinking about having a real partner lately i believe that sometimes it is a mans strength that can push women into the next level of womanhood also i have been considering the idea of having kids which might make my mother happy as she wants grandchildren
Response: it sounds like you are considering some important decisions about relationships and family its normal to ponder about these things as they can be significant life choices remember its essential to prioritize your happiness and make decisions based on what feels right for you and not just to please others can you tell me more about your thoughts on what a real partner means to you and how it might impact your life

Context: im concerned that my big family and constant family parties will eventually put a strain on my relationship i feel like i always have to choose between my partner and my family especially since my mom doesnt approve of my partner
Response: it sounds like youre caught in a challenging situation where youre trying to balance your relationship with your partner and your connection with your family its important to have open communication with your partner about this issue and work together in finding a compromise have you discussed this concern with your partner and explored ways on how both of you can handle this situation

Context: i had hopes for my relationships to work well but things didnt go as planned and it was disappointing now im struggling to decide where to put my energy in my relationships with the people i care about and love especially when things are not easily coming together and theres a lack of unity
Response: it sounds like youre feeling disappointed about how your relationships have unfolded and youre facing a challenging decision about where to focus your energy its natural to want unity and harmony in relationships but its important to remember that relationships are fluid and can change over time instead of pressuring yourself to find a perfect solution consider treating each decision as a step in your journey knowing that more opportunities to adjust and grow will come you may also want to discuss your concerns with the people involved and work together to find a path forward

Context: as a patient i understand that my situation is an ongoing process and will not be resolved immediately i am not ready to address a specific issue right now but im sure that there will be more decisions to be made in the future
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate your recognition that this journey is a process that takes time and can involve multiple decisions its alright if you dont want to discuss a particular issue at the moment we can work together at your pace to address challenges and make decisions as they come along

Context: i feel worried about the choices i have to make in my life no matter which path i take i see some pain for me and my loved ones be it my mother or my partner it seems like the pain is unavoidable at least in the immediate future
Response: its normal to feel concerned about making decisions that might affect you and your loved ones however difficult situations often come with an opportunity for growth and learning instead of focusing solely on the pain that may arise consider the benefits of each option its also important to communicate openly with your loved ones about your concerns so you can face these challenges together do you have any coping mechanisms or support systems in place to help you handle these situations

Context: i have somebody but its always been my family you know they have been the the my love for my family has changed right
Response: it sounds like your relationship with your family has evolved which is a natural part of life sometimes changes in relationships can bring up strong emotions could you please tell me more about how your love for your family has changed and how it is affecting you

Context: ive been struggling with the feelings of guilt but my mother has always trusted me and we have been very close throughout our lives
Response: it seems like you have a strong bond with your mother and her trust in you is a testament to your relationship its natural to feel guilty in certain situations but try focusing on the trust and closeness you both share is there any specific incident causing this guilt or is it a general feeling

Context: i want to make sure that i am doing right by my mom showing her that i can have strong family values that she placed in me but she doesnt approve of the family that i am trying to hopefully make and have
Response: it sounds like youre trying to balance your mothers expectations with your own desires to create a family that suits your values if you were to make the decision of putting more energy into restoring the relationship with your mom what do you think might change in your current situation and how would you feel about approaching her to discuss these concerns

Context: i feel that if i rely more on my mom and the structure i had in the past it might take away from my partnership i worry that we can never be a full part of each others lives if i rely too much on my past

Context: i know my partner wouldnt have a problem with me picking a certain path because she is familiar with that as well but i could still see a strain being put on that relationship
Response: its great that your partner is understanding and supportive of the path you want to choose however its normal to worry about potential strain on the relationship can you share more about the specific concerns you have that may cause a strain

Context: i recently had a conversation with my mom who seemed to sense that there was something going on in my life that i wasnt telling her she noticed that i hadnt been coming around as often and asked about it during lunch she told me that she knew something was happening but i didnt have to share it with her if i didnt want to

Context: my sister recently found out about my sexuality and has not allowed me to go back in she even doesnt want us to be together when i have to take care of my niece and nephew her strong reaction is something i didnt expect and as a result i havent spoken to my mom for a month which has been really hard for me because i usually talk to her daily
Response: i understand that your sisters reaction has been hurtful and unexpected causing a strain in your relationship with your family it must be difficult not talking to your mom as you have a close bond with her i wonder if theres any possibility of having an open conversation with your sister to address her concerns maybe this could also help in reestablishing communication with your mom and work towards understanding and acceptance within the family

Context: ive been really struggling lately it just killed me off on everything that i thought i knew about my mom
Response: i understand that youre going through a tough time its natural to feel lost or confused when our understanding of someone close like your mom changes unexpectedly can you tell me what specifically happened that made you question your understanding of your mom this may help us explore your feelings and find a way to cope with this new information

Context: i just had a conversation with someone named donna and we engaged in whats called an externalizing conversation i am curious to know more about what externalizing is and how its used in narrative counseling practice
Response: externalizing is a technique used in narrative counseling largely developed by michael wordsworth and david thexton it involves separating the problem or issue from the person treating it as a separate entity and shifting focus away from internal causes this allows the individuals to explore their relationship with the problem gain new perspectives and ultimately find ways to resist its influence or overcome it feel free to ask if you have any specific questions about how it was applied in your conversation with donna

Context: i am struggling with a habit that seems to have control over me affecting my life and shaping my decisions i feel like the habit is not a part of me but rather an external influence
Response: its important to recognize the distinction between you and the habit acknowledging that the habit is an external influence rather than something residing inside you this perspective can help you better understand your relationship with the habit and give you the opportunity to explore how its impacting your life while taking steps towards regaining control and overcoming this issue

Context: lately ive been feeling like something is wrong with me like i have a problem thats been affecting different aspects of my life i feel like the problem has been around for a long time and its been getting worse
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a problem that has been impacting your life in various ways for an extended period as a counsellor my goal is to help you externalize this problem so instead of believing that theres something wrong with you well work together to explore the issue as an outside influence lets begin by discussing the main areas of your life where you feel this problem has exerted its influence and the specific situations that led you to believe something was wrong

Context: i had a check list in my head the words length breadth and depth
Response: it sounds like you have been mentally organizing your thoughts using key words such as length breadth and depth this might be helpful in categorizing and structuring your thoughts can you please elaborate more on the context around these words and how they help you handle your thought process

Context: ive been struggling with negative selfdoubting thoughts and its difficult for me to hang on to accomplished thoughts when im feeling really low i think my dad leaving when i was just three months old has a big impact on me ive always had this inner fear of abandonment and the idea that he didnt want me replays a lot in my life
Response: thank you for opening up about your thoughts and experiences its clear that your fathers actions have had a lasting impact on you but its important to remember that there can be other ways to interpret those events as a counsellor i would encourage you to explore and experiment with different thoughts and perspectives on the situation which could potentially give you a broader understanding and help alleviate those negative selfdoubting thoughts lets work together to identify what brings you down and what lifts you up so that we can find ways to manage those feelings when they arise

Context: i have struggled with the belief that my father left when i was three months old because he didnt want to be with me he tried to explain his side saying he felt he wouldnt make a good father and we were better off without him due to his own history of abuse its hard for me to wrap my head around this i wish i didnt depend on others for happiness but i dont know how to do that
Response: its understandable that it would be challenging to shift your perspective on your fathers actions its possible that his decision had more to do with his own issues than with not wanting to be with you as we work together well explore ways to tackle the belief that youre not the kind of person people want to be with and help you learn to find happiness within yourself remember its a process and youre already showing courage by discussing this openly

Context: i was feeling tense and unsure about what to do in our counseling session i didnt want to step across any boundaries but now i feel more relaxed and the line seems clearer
Response: im glad to hear that youre feeling more relaxed now its important to have open communication during our sessions and discussing what youre looking for can help us move in the right direction if you ever feel unsure again dont hesitate to bring it up so we can continue to work together in a comfortable and effective manner

Context: as a patient i just wanted to express my confidence in maintaining ethical boundaries and professionalism in my work i feel more relaxed about it now
Response: as a counsellor i can see that youre aware of the importance of ethical boundaries and professionalism its great that youre feeling more relaxed and confident in this area your genuine care and empathy will surely make a positive impact on those around you keep up the good work

Context: im feeling better now but im still a bit concerned about working with a particular client i have a plan to achieve success but im not sure about the limitations of our relationship and the direction they want to go

Context: i am a therapist and have a client who has recently invited me to dinner i want to maintain our professional relationship but i am unsure how to handle this situation without potentially damaging our therapeutic connection what should my next step be for our next session
Response: in the next session you can reintroduce the invitation and once your client brings it up again take the opportunity to decline the offer and explain your reasons for doing so in order to maintain the professional relationship you could then ask your client what they hope to achieve from that dinner and try to understand the bigger picture behind their invitation if they struggle to express themselves you can remind them of the issues theyve faced in previous relationships and how youve worked together to overcome those

Context: im feeling uncomfortable and apprehensive in my counseling sessions because i think the client is trying to flirt with me or has an attraction towards me this is causing me to become more defensive in order to maintain ethical boundaries im not sure if im doing anything wrong or crossing any boundaries unintentionally what should i do
Response: its important to maintain ethical boundaries in a counseling relationship and its great that youre aware of that one suggestion would be to discuss your concerns with a supervisor or colleague to identify any unintentional boundary crossings additionally you could set clear expectations and boundaries with your client and ensure they understand the professional relationship lets discuss the scenarios further to help you address this issue more effectively

Context: im a therapist and ive been working with a client who recently brought me flowers as a gift he told me they were free because they came from his mothers garden although at first i didnt want to accept the gift i eventually did but i decided to place them in our waiting room for everyone to enjoy im trying to make sure i dont cross any boundaries and keep the relationship professional do you think accepting the flowers in this way was appropriate
Response: from your description it seems that you are being mindful of maintaining professional boundaries and prioritizing ethics in your work accepting the flowers and placing them in the waiting room for everyone to enjoy was a thoughtful way to handle the situation as it shows that you value your clients gesture but also ensures that youre not fostering a personal relationship outside of the professional context continue to be aware of these ethical considerations and dont hesitate to seek guidance if you have concerns in the future

Context: this week has been pretty smooth but i have one client that im struggling with he came in for depression and im not sure how i should work with him
Response: its good to hear that things have been going well overall could you provide some more information about this specific clients situation such as their background what theyre going through and any unique challenges they might be facing this will help me provide more tailored guidance on how to better support them

Context: ive been seeing a patient for 12 sessions about his failing relationships and coping skills recently i noticed a change in his demeanor he started dressing differently giving me compliments and seemed happier but now hes making small comments related to us and ive started feeling awkward and more on the defensive his comments are not inappropriate but are different from the norm he even asks about my week and what i do in my spare time
Response: it sounds like your patient is feeling more comfortable with you but its important to maintain a professional boundary in therapy sessions the feelings of awkwardness and defensiveness youre experiencing are valid in the next session its crucial to set clear boundaries and kindly remind your patient about the importance of staying focused on the therapeutic process make sure to address the change in their demeanor and ask if theres anything specific they would like to discuss related to their progress in therapy

Context: as a counsellor i recently received flowers from one of my patients while i dont think i crossed any ethical boundaries im unsure if i should have accepted the gift or not im afraid it might escalate into something else i usually accept gifts if they are gestures of thankfulness and dont have monetary value but should i have discussed this further with the patient
Response: its important to consider both ethical guidelines and cultural factors when it comes to accepting gifts from patients since you have already accepted the flowers one approach to handle the situation now would be to have a conversation with the patient about the meaning behind the gift and explain to them that its not necessary to give gifts to express gratitude this will not only help you understand their intentions but will also establish boundaries and clarify expectations moving forward

Context: i accepted a gift from a client so as not to offend him but then he started asking me out to dinner and trying to make plans with me i feel like the situation has escalated and im not sure how to handle it now
Response: it seems like the situation has become uncomfortable for you in these cases its important to establish professional boundaries and communicate them clearly to the client you can explain to him that as a professional you need to maintain a certain distance and that you cannot engage in personal relationships outside of your professional role if he continues to cross boundaries it might be necessary to discuss this with your supervisor or consider referring the client to another professional

Context: i am a client who is trying to get over a bad relationship and start my life anew i recently mentioned inviting the counselor out and i think it might be related to my desire to start a new relationship
Response: from your description it seems like you might be projecting your desire for a new relationship onto our interactions to better understand your intentions behind this offer id like to ask you what are you looking for when you think about inviting me out and what would you like in the bigger picture for your life perhaps in terms of companionship or personal growth reflecting on this might help us stay focused on the goal of our counseling sessions

Context: i recently faced a situation with a client who made a friendly gesture that crossed a boundary i told them nicely that i appreciate the offer but cannot accept due to professional reasons the client accepted my response but im unsure if i handled it well should i have said something different
Response: it sounds like you maintained your professional boundaries while still being respectful and appreciative of the clients gesture you can consider clarifying your response by stating your appreciation for the friendly gesture but reminding them of the importance of maintaining a professional relationship in such situations its important to feel comfortable with your response so practice and modify it as needed to suit your communication style

Context: last week you asked me if i wanted to go out with you for your birthday in about two weeks but we had to end the session before i could address it i appreciate that you feel comfortable enough with me to invite me to your birthday but i feel that as your counsellor its not appropriate for me to go out with you outside of our sessions
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings about my invitation i understand that as my counsellor it might not be appropriate for you to attend my birthday party outside of our sessions i guess i just felt comfortable around you and saw it as a friendly gesture its alright though and i appreciate your professionalism can you please tell me why attending a clients social event might be considered inappropriate

Context: i prefer to maintain our professional relationship with my client he first came for counseling because he had difficulty maintaining relationships and was dealing with a breakup i believe he now feels comfortable enough with me and is considering starting a relationship however i want to keep our relationship strictly as client and counselor i dont know if that sounds too harsh and i struggle to find a better way to express it
Response: its important to set boundaries in the professional relationship between client and counselor your concern about maintaining the professional relationship is valid instead of worrying about sounding harsh be clear and assertive about your role as a counselor you can express your appreciation for the trust and rapport youve built but emphasize the importance of focusing on the therapy goals and keeping the relationship professional you might ask your client how do you think our working relationship would be affected if we were to become more than client and counselor this can help your client understand the importance of boundaries

Context: i felt silly having to talk to someone about my problem and i thought id look silly as well i also felt a little bit pessimistic about the situation
Response: its completely normal to feel a bit uncomfortable or silly when opening up about personal matters however its important to recognize that seeking help is a brave step and i am here to provide support and guidance without any judgment can you share more about what brings you the most worry or concern in this situation

Context: i dont think i believe people can help me and if im honest there is a part of me that thinks that here as well its really hard for me to say this

Context: i often feel like my mom is sitting on my shoulder especially in situations where a lot is expected from me it reminds me of her telling me to put myself together and not be selfindulgent
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a strong influence from your mom in highpressure situations can you think of any specific examples of when this has occurred and how it affected your decisionmaking or actions in those situations
