Response: its important to communicate your feelings and boundaries to others effectively if youd like to let her know that youre busy consider using a polite but firm approach to express your need for uninterrupted work time you can say something like i apologize but we are really busy with work right now can we discuss this later or at another time i appreciate your understanding

Context: i felt like a naughty school girl being called in front of the headmasters like i did something wrong it happened once in school and thats how it felt this time too in the situation there were two reporting managers due to an overlap in my job roles but i still wonder what ive done wrong
Response: it sounds like the situation of facing two reporting managers brought up feelings of insecurity and worry about doing something wrong similar to a past experience in school its natural to feel this way in such scenarios however its important to remember that the job role overlap might not necessarily imply any wrongdoing on your part can you think of any specific actions or behaviors that might have triggered these feelings

Context: i feel like my organization is picking on me im not aware of it being like that for anybody else and it seems that they may be unfairly targeting me
Response: i understand that feeling targeted can be frustrating and isolating it might be helpful to gather more information on the situation do you think you could find out if others in the organization have experienced similar treatment or if theres a specific reason for their actions towards you

Context: i recently realized that i dont have to hold onto my childhood beliefs anymore and that how i feel isnt necessarily how i look this could explain why my teachers didnt help me and why my parents thought i was alright without assistance i feel like ive taken this belief with me as ive grown
Response: its great that youre recognizing the impact of your childhood beliefs and understanding that you can change them its possible that your outward appearance of calmness or competence might have led others to believe you were alright without support its important to be more aware of this moving forward and find ways to communicate your needs more effectively

Context: ive realized i can use my experiences to my benefit in presentations but i also need to learn to share my feelings more with others im amazed at how much ive learned from this
Response: im glad to hear that youve found value in the therapy and learned something about yourself its great that you see potential for growth both in presentations and in sharing your feelings remember that selfimprovement is a continuous process and keep building on what youve learned

Context: ive been considering using a daily thought record and maybe even keeping a journal because i think it might help me i want to recognize the negative automatic thoughts and challenge them
Response: thats a great strategy to work on your negative thoughts just a question have you noticed any negative automatic thoughts in other people yet remember its not just you who have them and becoming aware of that might help you feel even more supported in your journey

Context: ive learned that when i feel something is true it might not necessarily mean it is true
Response: thats a valuable realization its important to question our perceptions and thoughts as they can sometimes be influenced by our emotions or past experiences this can help us develop a more balanced perspective on ourselves and the situations we encounter do you have any examples where you applied this understanding

Context: ive recently started looking at the evidence for some of my beliefs that people dont help me this has led me to rethink some of my childhood beliefs as well
Response: im glad that youre examining the evidence for your beliefs remember beliefs can sometimes be reasonable reactions to situations but its important to question them and determine if they still serve you well lets explore more about your childhood beliefs and how they may affect you in the present

Context: even if my partner complimented my appearance i wouldnt believe him i dont want to look silly and sometimes i feel like i sound silly or whiny
Response: it sounds like you may have some insecurities surrounding your appearance and how you present yourself its important to remember that everyone has their own unique qualities and beauty additionally it might help to focus on building your selfesteem and trusting your partners compliments can you tell me about a specific situation where you felt this way

Context: i think as i watched the video i was watching your reaction to me as well i think if you had reacted with an expression it might have confirmed that i was wasting your time and being silly but you didnt so there is a part of me that wants to believe your honest feedback
Response: its important to recognize the need for feedback in our sessions my goal is to provide honest feedback to help you in your growth keep in mind that our work together will involve discussing your thoughts and feelings and i will always try to give you genuine feedback is there any specific area where youd like more feedback

Context: i feel like when people including you say something nice about me they might just be saying it to be nice and not because they actually believe it i worry that i sound or look silly and i wonder if youre just trying to be polite
Response: i understand your concern but as your therapist im committed to being honest with you ive also watched the tape and genuinely believe you didnt sound silly or look weird my role is to support you and provide honest feedback so you can trust that im being sincere when i give you compliments

Context: ive been hearing a voice in my head lately and it is very critical of me
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing intrusive thoughts which can be distressing is there a specific situation or thought that triggers these critical voices understanding the possible triggers might help in finding ways to cope with them and reduce their impact on your wellbeing

Context: i never thought of it before but its true  i dont expect anyone to do anything for me in fact when i am in a crowd of people i expect them to be antagonistic and not like me
Response: its interesting how youve developed this belief expecting people to be antagonistic towards you this might be a protective coping strategy which could have helped you in the past but are there times when this expectation might hold you back from forming genuine connections with others or seeking support

Context: ive been feeling like other people think theyre better than me and its been bothering me these beliefs have stuck around even when they may not be accurate or useful anymore
Response: i understand how youre feeling it seems that you have some negative core beliefs and a history that affects your current situation one thing we can do is develop a conceptualization to better understand these beliefs and their origins if your history were different maybe a few people not paying attention to you wouldnt bother you so much over time well work on addressing these beliefs to help improve your overall wellbeing

Context: i often feel like people are not very interested in what i have to say and just vaguely paying attention its disheartening and makes it difficult for me to connect with others
Response: i understand that feeling ignored or dismissed can be discouraging id like to help you explore why you might feel this way and work on strategies to improve communication and connection with others can you tell me about a specific situation where you felt people were not paying attention to what you had to say

Context: i had a presentation recently and noticed that my colleagues seemed more intelligent than me the previous presenter was quite boring so everyone was already disengaged as i was talking about a product they didnt know much about some of them seemed distracted and uninterested
Response: its natural to feel intimidated when comparing yourself to others especially in a work environment however its important not to solely focus on negative thoughts keep in mind that different people have different strengths and a boring presentation can also affect audience engagement remember the concept of cognitive therapy we discussed earlier focus on your own strengths and try to improve your presentation skills it might also help to ask your colleagues for feedback do you have any specific areas youd like to improve

Context: i feel like people are not listening to me and theyre just bored im not making any sense here
Response: it seems you are concerned about not being heard and the idea of others being bored with you can you share a specific situation where you felt this way so we can better understand and provide guidance

Context: i feel like my colleagues are cleverer than me one of them didnt do a great presentation but he is a doctor and i think hes still more intelligent than i am
Response: its important to remember that intelligence is multifaceted and being a doctor doesnt make someone better at everything comparing ourselves to others can be detrimental to our selfesteem focus on your strengths and understand that everyone has different talents if you still feel worried could you provide a specific example of when you felt inadequate compared to your colleagues

Context: i am worried that being clever doesnt necessarily make someone interesting to the audience ive noticed that some great speakers are not particularly technical are there any ways to be both clever and keep the audience interested
Response: its true that being clever does not automatically make someone an interesting speaker however its important to recognize that effective communication and engaging others are skills that can be learned and developed as a counsellor i would suggest focusing on honing your speaking skills sharing your knowledge in a relatable manner and learning how to read your audiences cues to adjust your presentation accordingly remember being both clever and engaging is not mutually exclusive  you can definitely achieve both

Context: ive been really concerned lately about whether im not as clever as others around me
Response: its natural to compare ourselves to others but its important to remember that everyone has their own unique set of talents and abilities instead of focusing on what others can do try to focus on your own strengths and accomplishments if you find that you are struggling in a particular area remember that its never too late to learn new skills or improve on existing ones keep in mind that selfconfidence and selfacceptance play a big role in our overall wellbeing so work on cultivating those qualities within yourself do you find that any particular event or situation triggers these feelings of inadequacy for you

Context: i have been thinking that people dont like me and its bothering me a lot i never thought that maybe they are having some consideration for me by not imposing their dislikes on me
Response: its important to consider alternative perspectives in these situations instead of assuming people dont like you maybe they are showing consideration for you by not imposing their dislikes lets explore more evidence that supports or contradicts this idea we can also look for any positive indications that they do like you remember our thoughts can greatly affect our emotions and wellbeing so its crucial to challenge negative beliefs

Context: i play cards with mike and sovia quite regularly i feel more comfortable when there are not many other people around i guess its because i only feel at ease with my immediate neighbors
Response: its great that you have a close relationship with your immediate neighbors and enjoy playing cards with them its completely normal to feel more comfortable around familiar faces if youre looking to expand your social circle it could be helpful to try participating in activities with a smaller group of people and gradually broaden your comfort zone

Context: i feel left out when more people are involved and i guess i just want to be in a smaller group where i feel better but i dont understand why i feel more left out than others
Response: its understandable that you would prefer smaller groups as it can be easier to connect and have better access to each other however its also natural for some people to feel left out in larger groups can you think of any specific reasons why you might feel more left out than others besides the assumption that people dont like you

Context: i sometimes feel tense and struggle to start conversations with others i often cant think of the right thing to start the conversation with
Response: its common for people to feel anxious about starting conversations and its important to remember that everyone is different in their approach to make it easier try finding common ground or interests to initiate the discussion also practice and experience can help build confidence in social situations what specific situations are you most concerned about

Context: i had to give a lecture using powerpoint in a lecture theater even though i wasnt feeling well and not familiar with the software as i started talking about my product people appeared bored and were chatting at the back this made me lose concentration and my ability to continue speaking i felt embarrassed and ended my presentation quickly
Response: it sounds like you had a challenging experience presenting especially when you werent feeling well and were unfamiliar with the technology it is natural to feel embarrassed in such situations however its important to remember that not every audience will be interested in every topic and their reactions might not be a reflection of your capabilities if you were to give a presentation in the future would you like some guidance on ways to improve your confidence and handle distractions

Context: i was wearing my presentation suit a darkcolored trouser suit but i wasnt feeling my best i had an upset stomach and was in quite a bit of pain which made the situation uncomfortable
Response: im sorry to hear that you were unwell during your presentation it must have been challenging what did you see in the room at that time try to focus on the surroundings and the atmosphere as it can help lead us to a better understanding of how it impacted your experience

Context: i see in the room just tears of people sitting in front of me and they havent dimmed the lights so i cant see them all they are in white coats and they have stethoscopes so i know theyre doctors
Response: it sounds like you are in a situation with medical professionals and its affecting your emotions the room being lit and seeing people in tears seems to be overwhelming how does this situation make you feel and what are your thoughts right now

Context: i remember a horrible experience where i couldnt show my anger around my peers i had to pretend that i was too upset
Response: i understand that you had to suppress your emotions in that situation now that some time has passed how do you feel about what happened and how it affected you its important to consider if that experience has had a lasting impact on how you express emotions now

Context: i think i was quite negligent and the girls were really cruel to me i feel stupid because i didnt have the courage to stick out for myself
Response: it sounds like you had a challenging relationship with them its normal to feel that way in such situations but its important to remember not to blame yourself completely would you like to share more about how this affected you or any attempts you made to assert yourself

Context: i was with a group of people but i felt like there was a boundary separating me from them i attended a coed school and the other girls had all paired up but they were more girly girls and i wasnt
Response: it seems like you felt a sense of isolation within that group of people at school its normal to feel that way when it appears others have formed connections and you might not completely fit in with their interests its important to remember that people have a variety of interests and characteristics and you dont need to be just like others to find your own group of friends did the feeling of isolation affect your interaction with these individuals or your overall experience at school

Context: i didnt fit in with the girly girls because i didnt do ballet or like horses i was different from them and felt alone i dont know why i was like that
Response: its natural to feel different and not fit in with certain groups and it doesnt mean theres something wrong with you it might be valuable to explore your interests and find likeminded people so you feel more connected can you think of any activities or interests that you genuinely enjoy

Context: i dont know why i changed up with them and i dont know why i wasnt on my own i had a sense that i was my own person but i used to try really hard to please them deep down inside i knew that whatever i do they wouldnt like me
Response: it seems like you were trying to find your identity and a sense of belonging its normal to seek acceptance from others but its also important to be true to yourself remember you cannot please everyone all the time focus on fostering genuine connections with people who appreciate you for who you are sometimes people may not like us but thats okay learn to be comfortable with that and be proud of who you are is there any specific situation that made you feel this way

Context: i have been going through therapy and things have been improving however i am about to move to a new area and i am worried about meeting new people and facing new situations which might be triggering for me how can i deal with these situations
Response: its great to hear that your therapy has been helpful thus far as you move and face new challenges its important to remember that life has its ups and downs when you encounter a difficult situation try not to see it as a failure or setback but rather as an opportunity to apply your newly acquired skills since youll be entering a new environment expect to be tested and be prepared to face these challenges headon be proactive and think about how youre going to handle these situations using the coping strategies youve learned in therapy

Context: i feel like the ups and downs in my life look like a graph sometimes i receive tremendous affirmation and other times it feels like no one is helping or supporting me the inconsistency is confusing and overwhelming as it can happen with both my peers and authority figures
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings its understandable that inconsistent support can be confusing and overwhelming from what youve shared it seems like a visual representation such as a timeline of events might help you gain more clarity you can start by writing down instances where you felt supported or unsupported and over time you might be able to identify possible patterns or triggers how does that idea sound to you

Context: ive been really busy with work lately and i find that work is really tiring do you think people around me have noticed a difference in me
Response: as a counsellor i would suggest you to share your experience with the people around you let them know how your work has been affecting you lately they might not have noticed the difference but opening up with them can improve communication and mutual understanding this way you can also get support and encouragement from them

Context: i have no energy left at the weekends and its nice to just sit and not have to talk it feels different when someone says theyll take me as i am
Response: its completely normal to feel drained at times especially after a busy week its important to listen to your body and give yourself the rest and relaxation it needs to recharge its also great to have people around you who are understanding and supportive as this can make you feel valued and accepted if you ever want to discuss your feelings or concerns further know that i am here to listen and help

Context: recently ive been feeling like people are only happy with me when i dont do anything but they do keep inviting me to events
Response: it seems that you are doubting your worth in social situations however the fact that people continue to invite you to events indicates that they enjoy your presence and value your company how do you feel when youre around these people

Context: when i was 12 years old i went on a school trip to france my friends and i were allowed to go shopping but they ran off and left me alone in one of the big stores in paris i was scared and felt like nobody would help me
Response: it sounds like being left alone in a foreign country at such a young age was a frightening experience for you how did this incident affect your relationships with those friends and do you feel any lingering anxiety from that experience when youre alone in unfamiliar places

Context: i remember when i was on a 10day holiday with three girls who excluded me from their activities i felt so left out and hurt the french teachers husband actually noticed i wasnt there and came to find me i had to spend the rest of the holiday with those girls knowing what they had done
Response: i understand that you felt excluded and hurt by the behavior of those three girls during your holiday it must have been a difficult experience for you especially having to spend the rest of the time with them despite their actions its great that the french teachers husband noticed your absence and came to find you how have you handled similar situations since then if they have happened

Context: i feel left out at dinner parties because people dont engage me in conversation and they never greet me like they do others like how they do mma
Response: i understand that you feel left out and excluded during dinner parties sometimes people may not realize that theyre unintentionally leaving someone out if youre comfortable you can try to initiate conversations yourself or join in on discussions additionally regarding your concern about not being greeted with an mma could you provide more context or details on what mma means and why its important to you

Context: i used to have coffee with my friend linda but she doesnt come to see me anymore im not sure why there has been a change
Response: its possible that there could be various reasons for this change in your friends behavior one option is to reach out and initiate a conversation with linda asking her if everything is alright and if theres any specific reason why she hasnt been coming for coffee lately this way you can have a better understanding of the situation and hopefully reconnect with your friend

Context: lately ive been feeling overwhelmed since i started working more and it has been affecting my mental health
Response: i understand that increased workloads can sometimes lead to stress and affect our wellbeing its essential to find a balance between work and personal life consider taking breaks during work engaging in activities that help you relax and maintaining open communication with your supervisor if needed its also a good idea to prioritize selfcare during this time by maintaining a healthy diet exercising regularly and ensuring adequate sleep remember its important to reach out for support when needed

Context: ive noticed quite a change at work recently and it seems like some of my coworkers are avoiding me especially when it comes to socializing outside of work sovia for example has never come over for tea or coffee
Response: its important to consider various factors that could be influencing your coworkers behavior as it might not necessarily be due to them disliking you have there been any changes in your work dynamics or other external factors that may have led to this observed change

Context: ive been feeling upset because i didnt receive any calls for some events even though others got their invitations i dont understand how they could have invited those people without calling me too
Response: i can understand why you would feel left out in this situation perhaps there was a miscommunication or a different method of invitation used for you it might be helpful to express your concerns to the event organizers and ask for any possible explanations this way you can gain clarity on the situation and avoid feeling excluded in the future

Context: im in a highpressure situation where people seem to not listen to me and i feel like they think im stupid im not as clever as them and i feel like a fool how do you think someone else in the same situation might feel
Response: its common for people to feel pressured in this type of situation someone else experiencing the same thing might also feel embarrassed nervous or even angry its important to remember that these feelings are not uncommon and its okay to feel this way do you want to talk about any strategies to cope with these emotions

Context: ive been feeling angry and anxious lately its difficult for me to feel good or safe and i think my thoughts are playing a big role in that i feel like only a small minority of people could feel laid back in my situation
Response: its completely understandable that youre feeling angry and anxious due to your thoughts its true that our thoughts have a significant impact on our emotions its important to remember that everyones experience and threshold for feeling good or safe is different it may be helpful to focus on your behavior and actions that you can control to cope with these feelings can you tell me about any coping strategies that youve tried so far

Context: i felt exposed and rushed trying to hurry up and not look at people around me i just wanted to get out of there as quickly as possible because i thought people became aware of me feeling stuck
Response: its normal to feel exposed and want to escape from uncomfortable situations the fact that you hurried up might make people notice but most of them will not judge you for it to cope with this anxiety you can practice deep breathing exercises and focus on the present moment try not to overthink about how others may perceive you is there a specific reason why you feel so exposed and concerned about peoples opinions

Context: im sure at that point they were beginning to sort of shifting their seats and it was obvious that i was you know not finishing the presentation properly i was you know rushing it
Response: it sounds like you felt uncomfortable when you noticed people shifting in their seats during your presentation and that you were rushing it can you tell me more about what was going through your mind at that moment and how it affected your performance

Context: i feel like i might not be as clever as my colleagues and because of that i worry that i wont be able to hold their interest in conversations or during presentations
Response: its understandable to have concerns about how we compare to others but its important to remember that everyone has their strengths and weaknesses additionally whether or not youre perceived as clever doesnt necessarily determine your ability to engage others can you think of any specific instances where you felt this way and what happened during those situations this information can help us better understand and address your concerns

Context: i recently gave a presentation to a room of about 40 or 50 people i noticed that a few people especially a row at the back and some doctors in the front were not paying attention to me it made me feel anxious and unsure about my performance
Response: firstly its important to remember that during presentations not everyone will always be fully attentive people can get easily distracted for various reasons however its essential to focus on the majority of the audience who were engaged and listening to you its natural to feel anxious when presenting but try not to let the few inattentive people affect your confidence would you like to discuss any specific concerns regarding your presentation

Context: i felt that the four or five people out of 50 in the room who were not paying attention to me were the most important ones and i am concerned about their lack of engagement
Response: as a counsellor i understand that youre feeling concerned about those few important people who didnt seem to be engaged its quite natural to seek validation from others especially key individuals however try to focus on the fact that a majority of the people in the room were indeed paying attention to you you might also want to explore why you perceive these particular individuals as important and how that impacts your selfworth

Context: i feel anxious when i notice people looking out of the window during my presentation i start having negative thoughts like theyre not listening to me and they think im stupid
Response: it seems like the trigger for your anxiety is peoples disengagement during your presentation leading to negative thoughts about yourself one approach we could take to cope with this anxiety is to explore and challenge these negative thoughts additionally developing strategies for maintaining focus and confidence in your presentation could also be helpful is there any specific instance or presentation that this anxiety impacts more than others or do you feel it is a general concern in all kinds of presentations

Context: i feel like im not as clever as others and it makes me feel like a fool
Response: its normal to sometimes compare ourselves to others and feel inadequate however its essential to recognize that everyone has unique strengths and comparing ourselves to others isnt always helpful you shouldnt feel like a fool for not being as clever as you perceive others to be instead try to focus on your own skills and accomplishments and be compassionate to yourself if this is an ongoing issue for you can you share any specific situations or triggers that make you feel this way

Context: as a patient i find myself struggling with nerves during presentations and feel like i dont handle the pressure as well as my coworker sheila who seems to not worry quite so much and is more confident in front of groups i think it would be great if i could be a bit more like her
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concerns about feeling nervous during presentations its completely natural to compare ourselves to others like your coworker sheila but we need to focus on improving our skill set and finding ways to grow you can learn and practice techniques to manage your nerves and boost your confidence during presentations remember its not about trying to be exactly like someone else but improving yourself and your abilities lets explore some strategies to help you become more comfortable in front of groups can you share a specific situation where you felt most nervous while presenting

Context: i feel like my friends dont like me because theyve met without inviting me when six or four of them gather
Response: as a counsellor i understand why you might feel that way lets consider the evidence supporting your negative thoughts about your friends not liking you could there be an alternative explanation for them meeting without inviting you maybe it was an oversight or the gathering was related to a specific topic youre not involved in its important to remember that there could be other reasons outside of them not liking you

Context: ive noticed that some people have met without me and are attending weight watchers supposedly to help me as i have been writing these things down im actually feeling that it must be true
Response: its understandable that you might feel left out and concerned about these events its good that youre recognizing your feelings as you write things down it might be helpful to talk to those people and ask them about their intentions but also remember to be open to their perspective is there anything else youd like to discuss or add before we proceed

Context: i often struggle with timing in conversations by the time i figure out what i want to say the conversation has moved on and it feels too late to say anything i find myself trying to think of something entertaining amusing interesting or funny to say but its difficult to find the right moment
Response: i understand that timing in conversations can be challenging especially when trying to make a meaningful contribution its important not to put too much pressure on yourself to be entertaining or funny instead try focusing on being present and engaged in the conversation and allow your natural responses to flow without overthinking them remember that people appreciate genuine connection more than a perfect comment if you still struggle you could practice your conversational skills in a lowstakes environment or even consider joining a group or workshop specifically designed to help you improve your communication skills

Context: i feel like in fastmoving conversations i might have stopped trying quite hard i have been worried and tired with work lately and i think that has affected my communication
Response: it seems that your work has had a significant impact on how you participate in conversations especially when theyre fastpaced its natural to feel worried and tired but its important to acknowledge these feelings and find ways to manage them can you think of any strategies you can apply to improve your communication and cope with the stress from work

Context: ive been struggling a lot with my job lately because it involves a lot of talking presenting and performing and i feel like its becoming really hard for me ive even stopped trying quite hard because of how challenging it has become
Response: it sounds like your job is causing you significant stress due to its demanding nature im sorry to hear that youre struggling can you share some specific aspects or situations in your job that you find most challenging this may help us identify ways to cope with or address these difficulties

Context: iaposm having trouble acting naturally and just saying whats on my mind im concerned about coming across as silly i remember talking about an appraisal and not giving my permission to ask ive been feeling tired and a bit fed up with work which has made me less engaged
Response: it seems like youre worried about expressing yourself openly one way to manage this could be to apply the principle you learned during the appraisal situation you might want to give yourself permission to be open and actively participate even when youre feeling tired or fed up with work remember its normal to have concerns but sharing your thoughts can lead to better understanding and growth

Context: i recently found out that a schoolmate of mine went through the same issues with her parents but she actually became worse because she couldnt mourn with them at school after that they still carried on afterward what do you think about this situation
Response: it sounds like your schoolmate experienced a difficult situation with her parents and wasnt able to properly address her emotions its not uncommon for such unresolved issues to lead to negative consequences as a counsellor i would encourage open communication and support for individuals facing similar challenges do you feel comfortable sharing any other details about this situation or how it has affected you

Context: ive been reflecting on my past and realized that my parents tried to help me in certain situations but it actually didnt turn out to be helpful im wondering if this has impacted my current mindset
Response: its quite possible that your past experiences with your parents help might have shaped your current mindset sometimes even with good intentions the help we receive could feel unhelpful or intrusive which may lead to a reluctance to accept help in the future its important to recognize this pattern and work on building trust in others ability to provide support would you like to explore more examples from your past or discuss strategies for addressing this issue moving forward

Context: as the therapy is coming to an end i feel somewhat worried about losing the positive changes ive made during this process ive heard that many times those gains do not generalize to the persons life and get washed out how can i ensure that i maintain the progress ive made
Response: its natural to feel concerned about maintaining your progress after therapy in cognitive behavioral therapy cbt we emphasize the importance of developing takeaway materials that you can use during and after therapy these materials are designed to help you integrate the lessons and techniques youve learned into your daily life and maintain your gains in the long term i encourage you to utilize these tools and continue practicing the skills that have helped you make progress so far

Context: ive been feeling that no one will help me but i suppose some people have actually helped me in the past i cant expect everyone to help me but maybe i can expect some people to help me im just as likely as anyone else to be helped
Response: its great that youre recognizing that some people have indeed helped you in the past it is important to remember that not everyone will be able or willing to help but there will always be others who are willing to support and assist you when needed try to focus on the positive experiences and interactions and remind yourself that you are deserving of help and support just like anyone else

Context: ive been feeling like theres something different about me that makes me less worthy of helping others but im starting to realize that im just like everyone else i might even be more helpful or attractive to some people i help
Response: its great to hear that youre recognizing your own selfworth and the potential you have to help others remember no one is perfect and everyone has their unique strengths and weaknesses embrace your individuality and continue to focus on the positive aspects of yourself this mindset will not only benefit you but also those you help keep this perspective in mind as you continue your journey of selfgrowth

Context: ive been struggling with negative thoughts and feeling alone my counsellor frank suggested i start a positive log where i write down instances when people have helped me this way i can remind myself that there are people who care for me when im feeling low i told him that he has helped me a lot too
Response: its great to hear that you are considering starting a positive log this can be an effective tool in combating negative thoughts and reinforcing the belief that there are people who care about you as your counsellor im glad to be part of your support system and would be happy to be included in your log remember you can always reach out to your support network when you need help and reviewing your log regularly will remind you of the people in your life who are there for you

Context: lately ive been noticing that i have some double standards and its been bothering me i think i shouldnt have let it get to me this much but im feeling really selfcritical about it
Response: its important to recognize double standards and work towards resolving them however its also essential not to be too hard on yourself remember that growth is a process and its okay to feel selfcritical but try not to dwell on it for too long allow yourself space to improve and learn from these experiences is there a specific incident that made you feel this way

Context: ive noticed that i might be being tougher on myself than i am with other people im usually empathic towards others and its an important aspect of my job since i have to understand my clients needs
Response: its great that youre aware of your empathy towards others my suggestion would be to try extending that empathy towards yourself as well this might help you find a balance between being understanding with others and also being kinder to yourself which could lead to better overall wellbeing

Context: i feel like the more i share about myself and how im not functioning well the less likely i am to come to these sessions also i was worried about not looking good in a video and when i watched it i was right
Response: its important to remember that these sessions are meant to help you and sharing your struggles is a crucial part of the process as for not looking good in the video remember that our selfperception can often be critical and may not reflect how others see us is there a specific reason why you feel sharing more about yourself might prevent you from coming to the sessions

Context: i just had a conversation with my husband and we were discussing something together i feel like his opinion might be biased but im not sure
Response: its natural to feel that our loved ones opinions might be biased especially if it involves a situation concerning us its important to consider multiple perspectives and communicate openly with your husband about your concerns you can also seek advice from a third party like a trusted friend or a professional to gain more insights and make informed decisions

Context: i feel embarrassed when im blushing and its especially embarrassing when someone is being nice to me i think its because i dont expect people to treat me kindly so its always a surprise
Response: it sounds like you might feel undeserving of kindness or have some selfconfidence issues causing you to feel embarrassed when people are nice to you its important to know that you deserve kindness just like anyone else can you think of any specific reasons or past experiences that make you feel surprised when people treat you kindly

Context: i feel silly needing to talk because i should know better and be able to cope on my own i dont think its weak for others to seek help but for some reason i hold myself to different standards
Response: its interesting that you hold yourself to different standards than others when it comes to seeking help remember its okay to ask for support when needed what would it feel like if you allowed yourself the same leeway you give others who seek therapy this might help improve your wellbeing and even your sleep

Context: lately ive been struggling with sleep because i tend to chastise myself during my postmortem thoughts at night i think if i was kinder to myself i might sleep better
Response: its great that youve identified how being hard on yourself might be affecting your sleep lets explore some strategies that can help you be kinder to yourself during these latenight reflections which in turn might improve your sleep quality one approach could be trying mindfulness exercises to redirect your thoughts or practicing selfcompassion through positive affirmations

Context: i dont believe anyone would help me because i cant expect everybody to help me all the time even though there have been people who have helped me been really helpful and influential and given me lots of positives
Response: its important to acknowledge and appreciate the support that you have received from others in your life while its true that you cant expect everyone to help you all the time its great that youve had some positive influences its crucial to focus on those positive experiences and not let negative thoughts overshadow them have there been any strategies or tools that helped you cope during the more challenging times such as the paris incident you mentioned

Context: ive noticed that i tend to forget about living in the present and always worry about the next problem its almost like im constantly looking for problems instead of enjoying whats here and now i feel like my worry is like blinkers stopping me from seeing anything other than the issues in my life
Response: its understandable that you want to anticipate future problems to some extent as it can be helpful in certain situations however excessive worrying can hinder your ability to enjoy the present and focus on other aspects of your life its important to recognize when your worry goes beyond its usefulness and learn to switch it off when necessary consider finding a balance between addressing potential issues and allowing yourself to live in the present moment do you have any strategies for managing your worries

Context: i felt that my parents gave a lot of encouragement to my brother after he failed his exams but when it came to me they kind of just assumed that i would do well and didnt provide much support i also had to go to a different school than i preferred because of my sisters experience
Response: it seems like you feel that your parents didnt provide you with the same level of support and encouragement as they did for your siblings it might be helpful for us to explore how this lack of support has affected you and if there are any ways you could communicate your feelings to your parents or find alternative sources of support do you think the differences in the way your parents treated you and your siblings have had longterm effects on your selfesteem or relationships

Context: when i was younger my sister had a negative experience at her girls grammar school so my parents decided not to send me there instead they sent me to a coed school ive often wondered how my relationship with my parents might have been different if they had made a different decision
Response: it seems like your parents made the decision based on your sisters experience and what they thought would be best for you remember that we cannot control the past and its important to focus on the relationship you have with your parents now how do you feel about your parents decision now and have you talked to them about how it has impacted your life

Context: i feel like my parents didnt have much energy left for me growing up they were focused on my sister because she had problems during her teenage years and my brother had an accident when he was little and fractured his skull which led to a long stay in the hospital
Response: i can understand how that could have made you feel neglected or overlooked as a child it sounds like your parents were dealing with significant challenges with your siblings and it may have been difficult for them to provide adequate attention and care to everyone how do you think this has affected your relationships and selfesteem in your current life

Context: i felt really uncomfortable during a recent meeting because there was an extra person present and it felt like they were watching my back and out to find faults in me i normally do better in onetoone situations but having this additional person really made me feel like i needed to perform at a higher level this incident also triggered my core belief that people arent really there to help me
Response: it sounds like this unexpected situation made you feel vulnerable and pressured to perform stirring up your core belief that people arent supportive its natural for certain situations to trigger these feelings but its important to remind ourselves that not all people are the same and some might be genuinely interested in helping you if you encounter similar situations in the future would differently knowing about the other persons presence beforehand make you feel more at ease

Context: i just walked in and roared they there and i could feel my heart racing i could feel all the similar symptoms i get when i stand up and do a presentation so i was having to concentrate on trying to reduce those and not look stupid in front of them which actually made things worse
Response: it sounds like you experienced anxiety and some physical symptoms related to that since these feelings are similar to when you do a presentation it could be a sign of performance anxiety in order to help you manage these emotions can you share any strategies youve used before to deal with your anxiety during presentations

Context: as the patient i feel that there is a very pervasive issue that im facing and it seems like even therapists can see it that way
Response: as the counsellor i understand that the issue youre experiencing seems to be quite significant and pervasive its not uncommon for therapists to recognize such concerns as well can you please elaborate on the specific issue youre dealing with so i can better assist you and provide appropriate guidance

Context: ive been experiencing conflicts with my partner over trivial things for example we can be reading the newspaper and when we discuss whats going on in the world bill will share his opinion and ill disagree he gets indignant when i tell him i dont think hes right this competitive dynamic makes me feel unsure about how to handle these situations
Response: i understand that you and your partner are having conflicts over small disagreements it seems that both of you are getting into a competitive mindset where it becomes more about winning the argument rather than understanding each others perspectives perhaps you could try expressing your feelings and opinions in a more constructive way without directly challenging bills opinion to avoid triggering his indignation by doing so you might be able to deescalate the situation and have a more productive conversation

Context: i dont think of myself as being competitive but my husband keeps telling me that i am and that im always trying to oneup him this really bothers me because i never thought of myself as competitive and i think im just competitive with myself not with others
Response: it sounds like theres a difference in perspective between you and your husband regarding your competitiveness while you dont see yourself as competitive he perceives your actions differently its important to communicate with your husband about this issue and try to understand each others perspectives it might also help to reflect on any past relationships where competition was a prominent issue can you give me an example of a situation where your husband thought you were being competitive but you didnt agree with him

Context: i dont think im a competitive person but others say that i am im not sure why theres a difference in perception
Response: its interesting that you dont see yourself as competitive but others do it could be due to a difference in individual perceptions or maybe they notice certain behaviors that you might not be aware of can you think of any specific situations where people might have seen you as competitive

Context: i am in my second marriage now and im very happy with my husband bill however i see the same thing happening to him that happened when i was married to my first husband john
Response: its good to hear that youre happy in your current marriage but its concerning that youre noticing similar patterns from your previous marriage can you please share more details on what exactly is happening with bill and how its similar to your past relationship with john

Context: i always feel like im wrong in every situation and end up in petty arguments even though i try to be cooperative i do everything to help and still get accused of being unreasonable which i dont believe i am i think im quite reasonable actually
Response: it seems like youre feeling misunderstood and blamed in these situations even though youre trying to be cooperative and reasonable could you provide a specific example of a recent situation where this happened so we can better understand the context and explore potential ways to handle such interactions

Context: i feel like im always getting into arguments and giving in even when i think i might be right i never hear them say im right only that they are this pattern is similar to what i experienced in my previous relationship and now its creating problems in my marriage
Response: it seems that youre struggling with communication issues in your relationships leading to repetitive arguments and impacting your current marriage have you considered discussing this with your partner and finding ways to communicate more effectively so both of you can understand each others viewpoints and work on resolving disagreements in a healthier manner

Context: i feel like my husband doesnt care about me because he doesnt pick up on my feelings or agree with me this makes me depressed and both of us withdraw and sulk for a week i think its his fault since he never really reaches out and seems to reject my efforts to connect my previous marriage had similar issues
Response: so you feel unappreciated and disconnected when your husband doesnt understand your feelings or support you its essential to remember that communication is a twoway street youve acknowledged similarities between your current and previous marriage this may indicate that you might have a role to play in these conflicts can you identify any patterns in your behavior that might be causing this disconnect with your partners

Context: i feel like i understand what youre saying but its going to be hard for me to change i already feel like im ready to fight again and im trying to justify my actions even when i know they are wrong i realize this seems to be a pattern ive established
Response: its great that youre recognizing this pattern of behavior and acknowledging that change might be challenging as your counsellor id encourage you to reflect on the reasons behind this pattern and why it has become difficult for you to let go of it are there any specific factors or situations that trigger this behavior

Context: i often find myself disagreeing with the men in my life when were discussing current events for example my friend will share his opinion about a situation in the news and i dont think hes analyzing it correctly so ill tell him that i dont think hes right and explain my viewpoint
Response: its completely normal to have differing opinions on various topics engaging in healthy debates can lead to gaining new perspectives and understanding however if these disagreements are causing distress try approaching the conversation with an open mind and listening intently to their point of view if you still feel your perspective is more accurate you can express it calmly and respectfully what kind of impact do these disagreements have on your relationships

Context: i feel really conflicted because on one hand i think i am able to handle the situation but on the other hand i cant help but feel angry about it

Context: i have been feeling annoyed and angry lately and i seem to have this underlying anger thats similar to what i feel toward my exhusband

Context: as a patient id like to discuss some issues ive been facing recently im struggling with integrating certain aspects of my life and its not easy for me i think i might need some help in changing some patterns that are causing me distress

Context: i have decided to take risks in different aspects of my life such as friendships work and school as i attempt this recovery journey i am not a half measures person so i want to commit to this journey wholeheartedly

Context: i feel like therapy is a shared experience and i cant trust someone if they dont offer me something i need a really good sense of the therapist and who they are as a person even though theres so much i dont know about you i think i have a good sense of that would i be sensitive if you were suddenly trying to coerce me in some way yes very sensitive

Context: i think im pretty sensitive to other peoples intentions and i would feel it if someone was pushing me somewhere ive had therapy before where it almost felt like the therapist was trying to convince me to recover

Context: ive noticed that when people around me try to encourage my healthy self it sometimes causes me to respond with my eating disorder voice leading to a debate between their healthy intentions and my eating disorder

Context: i am struggling with the idea of not having a family and trying to convince myself it would be okay i think i would focus on my job hobbies and friendships to find meaningful pieces in my life my heart feels ready to commit to marriage and live with someone but the realization of not having a family is hard for me when my sister just had a baby

Context: ive always tried to be an independent person moving away from home and establishing meaningful relationships in new places but sometimes i feel like im battling between my desire for independence and the desire for marriage or close friendships

Context: i had a conversation recently that was not judgmental at all and it made me feel really safe and at ease i feel comfortable being here and talking about it
Response: its great to hear that you had a positive experience and felt safe in that conversation creating a nonjudgmental environment is essential for building trust and making progress in therapy do you want to share more about what made that conversation helpful for you

Context: i was almost surprised that i feel a lot better having talked to him not that this is a huge huge deal but i

Context: i have been feeling like i need to think about and work through my issues more but i feel like i have a good foundation to move forward my burdens feel lighter but there was one thing that i wished was addressed during our conversation about my belief that my life is going to go the way it goes and where that belief comes from

Context: i am feeling unsure about something but i am not clear about what exactly is bothering me

Context: i feel that there is a difference between the feminist movement and my experience as a black woman because the movement tends to view men as oppressors however i dont see black men as my oppressors

Response: thank you for sharing your thoughts it seems like you feel certain societal expectations and struggles within your relationships with white males and black males can you tell me more about your experiences or specific instances where you encountered these feelings id like to explore this with you so that we can better understand the underlying factors and work on ways to cope with these feelings and situations

Context: i am majoring in psychology and im very interested in humanities thats the reason i am focusing on racial issues

Response: i understand that you feel the difference in generations contributes to the change in how racial issues are perceived its true that times have changed since the civil rights movement and the issues might appear more subtle can you share a specific situation where you experienced this subtlety so i can better understand your perspective

Context: as a black woman of afrocaribbean descent i have been thinking about how feminist issues affect us i dont necessarily label myself as a feminist but agree with many of the standards associated with it ive always stood up for equal treatment and held others accountable for infringing upon my dignity and selfesteem by the time the feminist movement got going i had already been on that path for a long time
Response: thank you for sharing your thoughts on feminism and its impact on black women of afrocaribbean descent its great to see that youve been advocating for equal treatment and holding others accountable for a long time its important to remember that everyones experience with feminism can be unique and what matters most is how you choose to embrace the ideals that resonate with you is there any specific aspect of feminism that you would like to explore further or have concerns about

Context: as a patient i struggled with coming to terms with living in the united states and being told that as a black woman there were certain places i couldnt go easily the feminist movement was intriguing to me because it stood up for justice and against the injustices i faced based on my gender and race
Response: as a counsellor i understand that it can be challenging to navigate societal expectations and limitations placed upon you due to your identity as a black woman its great that you find the feminist movement empowering and worth exploring can you share some specific instances where you felt limited or discriminated against so we can discuss strategies to cope and find support in such situations

Context: i have worked mostly in predominantly white environments and from my personal experience the black male has not been an obstacle for me however i also believe that they do not get off scot free and have their own sort of chauvinistic code the black family in general has always had this strong mother figure i find it difficult to see my own mother as oppressed because shes handled the most difficult family situations with great tact
Response: it sounds like youve had unique experiences in your work environment and upbringing which has led you to see black males in a different light than others might the strong mother figure you describe in your family shows resilience and strength while its important to recognize the positive role models in your life it is also helpful to acknowledge that societal structures and systems may have an impact on the people around you and their experiences how have these experiences shaped your understanding of gender and race in the workplace and family dynamics

Context: as a patient i feel a sense of oppression from both white women and white men due to my past experiences with them my mother was a domestic worker and they didnt give her social security or good work situations i find it difficult to simply buy into feminist movements without considering my personal experiences with race and oppression
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings and experiences its completely understandable that your personal experiences and family history shape your perspective on societal issues its important to acknowledge these experiences and emotions when engaging in discussions or movements related to race feminism and oppression remember you dont have to simply accept any movement without questioning it or reflecting on your own values and experiences have you tried engaging in conversations within these movements that focus on the unique struggles faced by people of color and intersectional feminism

Context: as a patient im facing some experiences of subtle racism and issues of feminism in my daily life people often refer to women as girls which i find disrespectful im not fighting two separate battles but rather im dealing with a covert form of racism unlike the overt racism faced by previous generations like my mothers
Response: as a counsellor i understand how these experiences can be challenging and frustrating its great to see that you are raising awareness about the importance of using respectful language covert racism can be more difficult to address so its essential to continue having conversations and confronting these issues mindfully are there any specific situations or incidents that have been particularly challenging for you recently

Context: i was raised by afroamerican parents with my mother being the one setting the philosophy of our family she believed that education was the key to freedom and encouraged us to be independent and selfmanaging she had concerns about marriage implying that she might have made different choices herself i grew up thinking that being aggressive was necessary for survival especially as a woman and black person now i struggle to see black males as primary oppressors but i acknowledge their actions can be oppressive
Response: it sounds like your mother has had a significant influence on your life and perspectives your experiences growing up as a black woman in an environment where aggressiveness was deemed necessary have shaped the way you perceive the world its also important to acknowledge the distinction between oppressive actions and primary oppressors can you describe any specific incidents or experiences that have contributed to your current views about black males and oppression

Context: i feel like talking to you has lifted a weight off my shoulders and now i can focus on other things in my life

Response: i agree with you and its great that you are recognizing your needs and what you deserve in a relationship you deserve someone who respects and treats you well what specific behaviors from your ex do you want to avoid in your future partner its important to be aware of them and address any red flags early on in a new relationship

Context: ive been trying to do more activities to take my mind off my recent breakup its painful but i think its getting easier for me i hope so
Response: its normal for breakups to be painful but im glad to hear that youre trying to keep yourself occupied it will definitely get better with time how does it feel to be talking about the breakup right now

Context: i found it really hard to talk about my issues at first but after opening up it feels good to get things off my chest its comforting to know that you understand what im saying because youve had similar experiences

Context: as a patient im struggling with negative thoughts and im having a hard time identifying them and understanding how theyre affecting me
Response: as a counsellor its important to first recognize and identify the negative thoughts that youre experiencing once we have a clear understanding of what they are we can work together to challenge and reframe these thoughts in order to move forward in a healthier and more positive manner

Context: i feel so discouraged when people dont understand me and i dont know how to talk to adults easily i doubt that an older person like you could understand someone like me

Context: my mom told me that shes going to put me in the hospital if i dont talk to someone so i came to see the counsellor

Context: i have been experiencing hallucinations and illusions and i believe others have been discussing it with you as well

Context: i am unhappy and feel like theres no life in me my girlfriend recently dumped me because she likes another guy and i dont know how to deal with this

Response: its understandable that you would prefer to have good supervision and be recognized as an effective supervisee however its important to remember that people dont have to meet our expectations and we can still be okay even if they dont so try to focus on what you can control like your effort and performance rather than expecting others to validate your worth also consider discussing your concerns with your supervisors to seek possible improvements in your working relationship

Context: i have a strong preference for people to follow and be okay but im struggling to find a reason why they must do so i also wonder where it is written or heard that they should
Response: i understand that your preference is strong but its important to recognize that people have the right to make their own choices it isnt necessarily written or heard anywhere that they must follow your preference instead try to accept and respect others choices even if they differ from yours is there a specific issue you are facing that has led to this concern

Context: ive been struggling with my supervisors trying to intimidate me ive been trying to tell myself that i am good wise and true to get rid of this feeling but i still feel intimidated
Response: its great that youre trying to build up your selfesteem by reminding yourself of your positive attributes however to deal with the intimidation from your supervisors you could try assertive communication and set boundaries remember no one should have the power to intimidate you and you have the right to stand up for yourself without being confrontational if you still feel overwhelmed consider discussing your concerns with someone you trust like a colleague or a family member to gain a different perspective

Context: i dont like when people put me down give me bad marks and provide lousy supervision it makes me feel intimidated and im wondering if i should just like say i refuse to be intimidated by these people out loud

Context: i feel like people around me are uncomfortable and intimidated if i choose to contribute a little bit more i could lessen the angst in the environment
Response: its great that you recognize the impact you can have on the environment if you can accept others without anger and intimidation and contribute positively to their comfort it will help in creating a more inclusive and harmonious atmosphere however also remember that its crucial to take care of your own wellbeing are there any specific situations or examples of when you have felt this way or tried to make others comfortable

Context: i have been feeling intimidated and angry with my supervisors because of their actions theyre not bad people just making some stupid decisions and its affecting my emotional state
Response: its important to separate peoples actions from their worth as individuals its okay to dislike their actions but try not to label them as bad people first work on managing your feelings of intimidation and anger once you feel more in control of your emotions consider whether theres any practical approach you can take to help them understand the situation better or improve their decisionmaking process remember even supervisors can change but it starts with our own responses and perspectives

Context: i have been imagining a situation where people around me are getting worse and worse becoming more prejudiced against me and making nasty remarks i feel rejected and its affecting me emotionally
Response: i hear your concerns about feeling rejected and how this imagined scenario affects you emotionally remember its important to separate peoples actions from their value as individuals you can disagree with their behavior but refrain from labeling them as bad by focusing on their actions instead of their character you may be able to help them change try practicing rational emotive imagery vividly imagining the worst possible scenario and then disputing irrational dysfunctional beliefs you have about it this can help you cope with your feelings of rejection and develop a healthier mindset

Context: i am feeling very rejected low and down maybe even depressed i am trying to get in touch with these feelings and not suppress or repress them i feel very low and rejected
Response: its essential to acknowledge and understand these feelings of rejection and depression its a brave step to confront them openly as a counsellor im here to help you navigate this emotional state can you pinpoint any specific experiences or thoughts that are causing these intense emotions

Context: lately ive been feeling overwhelmed and anxious my workload has been steadily increasing and i cant seem to find enough time to do everything its causing me a lot of stress and its starting to affect my sleep
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing quite a bit of stress due to your workload its important to recognize when we need to take a step back and find ways to manage our stress more effectively consider looking into time management strategies setting realistic goals or seeking help from others to lighten your load additionally practicing relaxation techniques or engaging in activities that you enjoy can help alleviate stress remember its essential to prioritize selfcare in times of high stress

Context: ive noticed that some people around me are acting very stupid and its frustrating me i feel like its too bad they dont act intelligently i wish they could just change their behavior
Response: its normal to feel frustrated when people around you are acting in a way you dont understand or appreciate however its important to remember that people have different capacities and perspectives it would be helpful to focus on the things you can control such as your reactions and emotions and accept that some people may not act as intelligently as you would like try changing your perspective and practicing empathy to better understand their actions

Context: ive realized that i become easily intimidated by others and its really frustrating i feel like people who are incapable of acting intelligently should do something but i end up getting angry at myself for letting them intimidate me its such a waste of my energy
Response: its important to acknowledge that feeling intimidated can be a natural response to certain situations however it becomes unhelpful when it leads to anger and frustration instead of focusing on the behavior of others which you cant control try working on your own reaction to these situations you might still feel sorry or displeased by their behavior but you can learn to not let it intimidate you or make you angry remember its okay to be nonintimidatable and conserve your energy for more important things

Context: i get really intimidated by some people and then i put myself down for being intimidated i feel like a loser for letting it happen but i dont know how to stop it
Response: first accept that youre feeling intimidated and recognize that its not a reflection of your worth tell yourself its bad and stupid for me to be intimidated but right now thats the way i am and im not a louse a worm or a loser for being intimidated but its wrong then focus on the intimidators and realize that they should respect you and not try to intimidate you say to yourself i refuse to be intimidated consider if there is anything practical you can do to change their behavior or reduce their impact on you

Context: i have noticed that if i spent less energy on being angry i might have better control over my emotions and reactions
Response: youre heading in the right direction by recognizing the negative impact of anger on your overall wellbeing its important to work on managing your emotions and finding healthy ways to channel that energy have you considered any specific strategies for coping with your anger

Context: ive always felt that something was missing in my relationship with my father i remember one incident when i was around 1315 years old i just needed him to be kind to me but instead it felt like he was always focused on the negatives and getting on my case
Response: it sounds like you have some unresolved feelings about your relationship with your father it must have been difficult for you to seek kindness and support from him only to be met with negativity if you could communicate with him today what would you say to help him understand your perspective and needs remember expressing your feelings could be a helpful way towards resolving these emotions and possibly improving your relationship

Context: im peter and when i was 15 i had some problems with my school work so a friend and i decided to skip school and instead went to the library in birmingham to read about our hobby which was more interesting than the school work i wrote a letter to the school saying i was not well and signed it myself my parents thought we were going to school
