Context: i had a friend and we used to play truant together for a significant amount of time my parents found out when the school called them asking if i was really off sick they were shocked and couldnt understand what was going on i got scolded by my mom when i came home
Response: it sounds like you and your friend made a decision that ultimately had negative consequences for you both your parents reaction to the situation is understandable as they were likely concerned for your wellbeing and education sometimes we make choices that lead to unforeseen consequences and its important to learn from these experiences can you tell me more about why you and your friend decided to play truant and have you had a conversation with your parents to explain your actions and feelings

Context: my father recently started to act very strangely he suddenly decided to hand over all of his financial records and even his selfwritten obituary to me it feels like he believes its his time to die and im finding it extremely hard to cope with this situation
Response: i understand that witnessing your fathers strange behavior must be unsettling and worrisome its essential to consider seeking professional help for your father such as a therapist or a counselor to assess his mental state in the meantime try to have an open and honest conversation with him to understand his thought process and offer your support for seeking help if you feel overwhelmed dont hesitate to reach out to a mental health professional for yourself too can you think of any specific event that might have triggered his behavior

Context: i feel guilty because i wasnt as helpful and sympathetic towards my dad when he was trying to talk to me about his life and feelings i didnt take him seriously and now i wish i could have sat with him to try and understand his emotions
Response: its understandable that you feel guilty about not being there for your dad when he needed you however its important to remember that we cant change the past but we can learn from it and make amends in the present can you think of any ways to honor your dads memory or actions you can take today to ensure youre more empathetic and supportive to the people around you

Context: ive given up work now and im worried that our finances are going to be a complete mess this was the root of my worries thinking that we wont be able to make ends meet even though it turned out to be unnecessary later on
Response: its understandable that you were concerned about your finances after giving up work however its good to know that your worries turned out to be unnecessary moving forward its important to communicate openly about your financial situation and develop a plan to ensure that you can make ends meet if youre still worried is there anything else thats causing you concern

Context: i am struggling to accept that my dad has passed away i really wish i had been able to communicate and connect with him earlier on we had some superficial contact during our last couple of conversations i tried to cheer him up but i feel like i did it poorly and i wish i could have done better for him
Response: its completely understandable to feel sadness and regret for not having deeper conversations with your dad while he was alive grieving the loss of a loved one can be challenging and sometimes we feel like we could have done things differently its important to recognize that you did what you could at that time and its normal to wish for more connection as you process your grief try to focus on the positive memories you shared with your dad can you share a particular memory that brought happiness to both of you

Context: i wish i could have told my dad that i loved him before he had ect but its difficult because we never talked about feelings i finally managed to tell him but it feels awkward for both of us
Response: its understandable that expressing feelings in a relationship where it hasnt been done before can be challenging and awkward its important that you were able to express your love despite the discomfort it may take some time for both of you to adjust but these moments can help strengthen your bond is there anything else youd like to discuss about this situation that might ease your feelings of awkwardness

Context: i find it difficult to contact my own feelings and its awkward for me i think its because of my upbringing and my relationship with my mom we never hugged and i wish we could have had a more affectionate relationship
Response: i understand that your difficulty in accessing your emotions may be connected to your upbringing and lack of affection shown by your mother its important to acknowledge the impact this may have had on you and your feelings moving forward you may benefit from exploring and expressing your emotions with a therapist its never too late to develop emotional awareness and work towards healing from your past experiences

Context: i had a friend who had a good sense of humor but it was more of a poker face sense of humor his idea of humor usually involved plays on words and sometimes it felt like forced humor
Response: it sounds like your friend had a unique sense of humor that might not have been easily understood by everyone its important to remember that people have different ways of expressing themselves including their sense of humor its also essential to appreciate the differences in the people around us and try to understand their perspective do you have any specific concerns or issues related to your friends humor that youd like to discuss

Context: i have been thinking about my father lately he was a very talented man played the piano and was a world war ii veteran he was wounded in the war and may have been traumatized but he never talked much about it i have two brothers and we were his family
Response: it sounds like your father was an interesting man with various talents its common for veterans to not discuss their wartime experiences especially if they were traumatic its important to remember that each person has their own way of processing past events if youd like we could explore your feelings and thoughts about your fathers experience and how it has impacted your relationship with him and your family

Context: as the middle of three brothers i felt that my father was a distant figure in our lives he would only show up to discipline us if we misbehaved which involved some sort of ceremonial beating with our trousers down
Response: it sounds like you had a challenging relationship with your father who seemed distant and primarily involved in discipline this must have been difficult for you and your brothers can you share more about how this experience has affected your relationship with your father and your perception of authority figures in general

Context: i remember my father being very formal if there was a problem he would be brought in to administer punishment i never got to know him and it always felt like he was at a distance im trying to think back to my earliest memories of him
Response: it sounds like you had a distant relationship with your father and he was primarily involved in discipline when you were growing up this can certainly influence the way you perceive your relationship with him its good that youre trying to explore your earliest memories of him can you recall any situation where you felt positive or close to your father

Context: i cant really remember much about my father hes a bit of a blank to me the only things i can recall are that he was musical a great pianist and he wanted us to be successful together with my mother
Response: its common for certain memories to be unclear especially if they are distant or emotionally charged however you do seem to remember some positive attributes about your father like his musical talent and his aspirations for your familys success if youre comfortable doing so you could try exploring those memories more deeply or engage in activities that remind you of those positive qualities is there any specific reason why youre trying to remember more about your father

Context: ive been thinking about what to share with you today and i wanted to talk about my parents particularly my father i had a difficult relationship with both my parents and my mother was very critical of me
Response: i appreciate you opening up about your difficult relationship with your parents its important that we address these issues as they can be a significant factor influencing our lives can you please share more details about how your mothers criticism and your fathers behavior impacted you and the dynamics of your relationship with them

Context: my mom was hard on me and very critical but my father was the one i wanted to talk about today by the time my mom died we had come to an understanding and i started to like her however my father and i never really connected and i am now in my 60s
Response: it sounds like youve been able to resolve some of the feelings and experiences with your mother before she passed away and thats a great accomplishment it must be tough to feel disconnected from your father even now that youre in your 60s how has this disconnection affected your relationship throughout the years

Context: i was born in 1946 and my father died in the 1990s at the age of 80 my early upbringing was in the late 40s and the 50s in a household where children were seen and not heard and big boys dont cry
Response: it sounds like you grew up in a household with strict rules and emotional suppression your fathers passing and the traditions of the time might still affect you today can you share any specific childhood memories or current feelings youre experiencing that you think could be related to these experiences

Context: im having trouble finding the right word to describe my father people would often describe him as poker faced
Response: it seems like youre trying to express that your father had a neutral or unreadable expression most of the time which might have made it difficult to understand his emotions is there any particular situation or event that led to your feelings about your fathers expression

Context: i have been carrying something bothering me since childhood and feeling as if i was the silly one in my family my father mother and the overall family situation contributed to this feeling also my mother was very concerned about my appearance and would constantly remind me to sit up straight

Context: my mother always focused on appearance and seemed to pass judgment on my children based on their inherited physical traits i was the one in the family always getting into trouble and there was a disconnection between me and my father now im thinking about my position in the family and this feeling is connected to both of my parents although more directly to my mother because she would be explicit about things
Response: it seems that you are reflecting on your upbringing and how your parents especially your mother affected your selfesteem and relationships within the family understanding the dynamics of your family and recognizing the impact they had on you is an essential step in processing your emotions do you feel that this realization is affecting your current relationships or selfimage

Context: i remember my father always having a frown on his face and my mother seemed to see him as unsuccessful im not sure exactly why she felt that way but it has always bothered me

Context: growing up my parents always pushed me and my siblings to be successful however we never really talked about our feelings for each other when i was a teenager i faced a lot of problems at home and was seen as the clumsy and difficult one

Context: my older brother was the clever one and my younger brother was seen as the loved one i felt like i was stuck in the middle missing out on both love and cleverness i was always the one in trouble and got punished more

Context: when i was around seven or eight years old in prep school we were given 100 conduct marks at the beginning of each quarter and we were supposed to have at least 50 left by the end i dont know why but i was the one who always lost marks sometimes going into the negatives why was i so naughty

Context: i remember when i was younger my brothers would get good marks for conduct like 50 or more but my conduct marks would go down and down even into negative territory im beginning to think there must have been something wrong with me at the age of seven or eight
Response: its natural to compare ourselves to others especially our siblings however its important to remember that each person is unique and develops at their own pace its possible that you struggled with conduct at that age but that doesnt mean there was something inherently wrong with you lets explore more about your childhood experiences to better understand the factors that led to this situation can you recall any specific incidents or conditions that may have affected your behavior at that time

Context: well i could feel umm as if it was happening as if it was really happening so now im feeling as if uh i dont know whether the word is catharsis as if uh let something go that i hadnt like before a little bit of relief and release just a bit more relaxed

Context: i felt a sense of relief when i realized someone cared about me but it was also painful like a balloon bursting

Response: it sounds like that interaction with your father was a powerful and emotional moment for both of you its not uncommon for people to struggle with expressing love especially in relationships with complex emotions however its never too late to work on improving communication and expressing love to the people that matter to us

Response: it sounds like your fathers absence and lack of connection in your life has left a painful void its important to remember that while you may not feel like you had a strong connection with your father it doesnt mean you are lacking anything essential on your own can you think of any specific instances or situations that particularly emphasize this feeling of pain and loss in your relationship with your father

Context: i recently started leading an unemployment group consisting of people who have lost their jobs theres so much loss involved in this whole scenario especially for men whose jobs defined their identity

Context: i went up to the top of the roof at school and looked down 10 miles to the world trade center and saw the smoke and flames it was very upsetting and reminded me of when i was in college at georgetown when martin luther king was killed soldiers were on the streets and places were closed it felt like the loss of my political innocence and i was thinking ted went through this experience at the same time

Context: ive noticed that many people regardless of their age are seeking more fulfilling careers wanting to get married and have children and finding more happiness in their relationships it seems like everyone suddenly realized that life is short and they want to make the most of it as a midlife issues specialist i see this pattern in both younger and older clients
Response: its quite common for individuals to reevaluate their lives at different stages and seek improvements in various aspects like career relationships and personal fulfillment it could be helpful for them to explore their values passions and goals in order to better align their lives with what truly matters to them encouraging them to create a plan and take incremental steps towards achieving their goals can make a significant difference in their overall happiness and satisfaction

Context: ive been working on calming myself and my anger down for two and a half years now and i feel like im making progress but its taking a lot of time
Response: i understand that managing your anger and staying calm is a challenging process that takes time its great to hear that youve been working on it for two and a half years and are making progress remember that everyones journey is different and changes dont always occur quickly be patient with yourself and appreciate the progress youve made so far

Context: i had just moved with my mom to montana and i was at a bar playing pool and listening to rap music a guy there made a racist comment which i confronted him about my mom tried telling me that people are different here but i stood my ground because i dont tolerate racist comments and it should offend her too since im her son
Response: i understand that you faced a challenging situation dealing with racism its important to stand up for what you believe in and it must have been hurtful for you that your mom didnt initially support you the way you expected its important to have conversations with her about your experiences and feelings can you tell me more about how your relationship with your mom has been since this incident and if youve discussed it further

Context: recently there was a situation where i was mad at someone and my friend advised me to calm down i didnt really listen to her at the time but ive noticed that from then till now ive calmed down a lot i dont get mad as easily as i used to and dont flip out as bad as i did though sometimes i still do but it just takes a lot of time for me to work on it
Response: its great to hear that youve been making progress and learning to manage your anger better anger is a normal emotion but its important to know how to handle it constructively keep being patient with yourself and continue working on those skills if you find yourself struggling with specific triggers or situations feel free to share more details so we can work on strategies that might be helpful

Context: i have a few favorite recreational activities  i like playing football and basketball as well as drawing and writing music
Response: its great to hear that you have a diverse range of hobbies and interests like playing sports such as football and basketball and engaging in artistic pursuits like drawing and writing music these activities can help provide enjoyment relaxation and potentially foster social connections can you tell me if there is any specific aspect of these activities that you find particularly rewarding or fulfilling

Context: i enjoy writing lyrics football basketball and drawing those are my favorite things to do however i also seem to hate these same activities because they make me mad sometimes
Response: its interesting to hear that the same activities you love can also cause you frustration its normal to feel a mix of emotions toward the things we care about can you provide more details about what aspect of these activities makes you mad and if theres any specific situation that triggers this feeling

Context: i get frustrated and mad when i dont perform well in activities like basketball football drawing or writing music these are my favorite things to do but they can also be my worst experiences when i struggle with them
Response: its normal to feel frustrated when you dont meet your own expectations in activities youre passionate about the key is to recognize that failure and setbacks are part of the learning process sometimes taking a step back and giving yourself a break can help you return to these activities with a fresher perspective can you think of any strategies to manage your frustration in those situations

Context: i dont really mean to be a perfectionist but i try to be i dont like to be
Response: its interesting that you recognize your perfectionism as a factor in your anger perfectionism can be a doubleedged sword where it motivates us to achieve high standards but also causes emotional distress when things arent perfect lets explore ways to manage your perfectionism and understand how its impacting your anger can you share an example of a situation where your perfectionism led to anger

Context: i never feel like ive done well enough whether its in a sport like basketball or football or even in my drawings its never quite perfect and i feel a lot of pressure because of that i think this is why i get angry and take it out on others
Response: it sounds like perfectionism is at the root of your anger the constant pressure to be perfect can be overwhelming making it difficult to ever feel satisfied with your achievements to help you manage your anger well need to address your perfectionism and understand why it matters so much to you have you noticed any specific situations or factors that intensify your need to be perfect

Context: i need your help because when things dont go right when i dont score 30 when i dont do things perfectly i go berserk how can you help me with this perfectionism problem
Response: its important to realize that perfectionism can be detrimental to your overall wellbeing and performance instead strive for progress and acknowledge your accomplishments along the way when you catch yourself getting angry take a step back and breathe remind yourself that everyone makes mistakes and focus on what you can learn from the situation why do you think you expect perfection from yourself in every game

Context: it feels different in a way like i dont want to miss anything and i want to be the best player always no matter who im playing with i really dont like to get beaten or do anything wrong because if i do it just shows that im weak
Response: i understand that you have a strong drive to perform well and avoid showing any weakness on a scale of 0 to 100 considering the last time you played basketball what percentage of competence or skill would you give yourself keep in mind 100 percent would be a perfect day and 0 percent would be a total failure

Context: ive played a sport and i would rate my performance about 50 most of the time i had a couple of times when i achieved 100 in my game but i still wouldnt give myself an a for those times
Response: it sounds like youre critical of your performance even when youve done well im curious to know why you wouldnt give yourself an a even when youve achieved 100 in your game what factors are stopping you from acknowledging your achievements

Context: i never give myself 100 percent because i can always do better i wouldnt give anybody 100 percent except for a couple of people in the nba i can make every shot but i cant play my best playing my best means never getting touched never having the ball stolen never getting stopped dunking and everything
Response: it sounds like you set very high standards for yourself and others and it might be difficult to achieve those standards constantly have you considered that nobody is perfect and allowing yourself some room for growth and improvement could be beneficial as well

Context: as a patient i feel like i struggle to be perfect and achieve a certain level of success i can manage to barely reach it but i cant seem to fully succeed its like i can only rim but not dunk and its frustrating that i have to do everything perfectly without making a single mistake
Response: as a counsellor i understand how striving for perfection can be both motivating and frustrating its essential to recognize that nobody is perfect and its okay to make mistakes learning from our mistakes helps us improve and grow instead of focusing on being perfect try setting more realistic goals for yourself and appreciate the progress you make along the way remember it is not about never failing its about learning and growing from those experiences

Context: i recently started drawing and writing music as noncompetitive hobbies but i still get frustrated with myself im wondering if quitting smoking might help me feel less uptight
Response: its great that youre exploring noncompetitive hobbies like drawing and writing music frustration is a common experience when trying new activities but its important to be patient with yourself as for quitting smoking it can have numerous health benefits and might help with feeling less uptight however its essential to acknowledge that quitting may be challenging and might require additional support how long have you been smoking and have you tried quitting before

Context: i think nicotine might be affecting my mood because its a stimulant i do smoke and i know i should quit
Response: yes nicotine can indeed impact your mood as it is a stimulant its great that youre aware of the need to quit smoking improving your health by quitting can help your mood and overall wellbeing do you have any specific plans or strategies for quitting smoking

Context: im working on quitting smoking but its really hard i still smoke almost every day but i dont think it affects me when i play basketball because ive been doing both for so long
Response: i understand quitting smoking is a difficult process and its great that youre working on it its possible that you may not immediately notice the effects of smoking on your physical performance but it can still have longterm consequences have you considered trying any support resources or strategies to help you quit

Context: as a patient ive been struggling with quitting smoking i know i could greatly improve my physical performance if i quit since i would have more stamina and wouldnt get tired so easily its just that quitting is so hard and i have mixed feelings about smoking  i hate it but also like it
Response: as a counsellor i understand that quitting smoking can be a challenging process especially when you have mixed feelings about it it might be helpful to focus on the positive aspects of quitting such as improved physical performance and explore the reasons why you like smoking to better handle those cravings have you considered any specific strategies to help you quit smoking

Context: i find it hard to change the way i think because it feels stuck in my mind and im struggling with managing my anger issues as a result
Response: its true that changing the way you think can be challenging but its also one of the main techniques that psychologists use to help people manage their anger better be patient with yourself and consider working with a mental health professional to learn strategies to modify your thought patterns and improve your anger management

Context: im struggling with the idea that i need to think differently and not focus on being perfect i find it hard to think of certain things as just a game or something that doesnt matter
Response: it seems youre experiencing difficulty with perfectionism and adjusting your mindset it can be challenging to shift our thought patterns perhaps you could practice thinking that it doesnt matter slowly integrating this perspective into your life remember its okay not to be perfect and nobody is do you have any specific situations where this mindset has caused you problems

Context: i often think about things that matter to me and it affects my mood but my friend shawn is suggesting that i should change my way of thinking to feel better what should i do if i cant change my thoughts
Response: its great that youre open to changing your thinking however it can be challenging to change our thoughts especially if theyve been with us for a long time instead of focusing on completely changing your thoughts try practicing mindfulness and acceptance allowing your thoughts to come and go without judgment remember progress is more important than perfection additionally you can seek support from a mental health professional who can guide through this process

Context: im finding it difficult to change the way im thinking i tried playing a game but its not helping and im worried that if i keep failing ill just get even more frustrated
Response: i understand changing thought patterns can be challenging instead of focusing solely on the game lets try exploring some alternative strategies such as practicing mindfulness or identifying and reframing negative thoughts when youre ready we can discuss your experience with these techniques and make adjustments as needed

Context: ive been trying to improve at something so i thought maybe taking a break from it for a while might help when i stop playing and then start again i usually find that im a little better do you think taking some time off or trying a new hobby could be beneficial
Response: its great that youve noticed some improvement after taking breaks taking time off can indeed help you gain a fresh perspective and might even improve your performance exploring a new hobby can also be a good idea since it can provide you with a mental break and foster creativity remember balance is key in life so taking breaks or engaging in different activities can contribute to your overall wellbeing

Context: as a patient i have faced some challenging situations in life like moving from utah to california also my parents got divorced and i believe that these events had a significant impact on my mental and emotional wellbeing
Response: as a counsellor i understand that moving and dealing with your parents divorce can be quite challenging these are major life events and its completely normal for them to have an impact on your mental and emotional health lets focus on identifying the underlying feelings and thoughts associated with these events to better understand whats driving your actions and emotions we can then explore strategies and steps to cope with and overcome these challenges in a healthy and constructive manner

Context: when my parents divorced it was challenging my dad decided to move to california and took my siblings with him but not me we moved from utah to california and the two places had very different cultures
Response: it sounds like the events of your parents divorce and your dad taking your siblings but not you have had a significant impact on you moving to a different place with a different culture can also be difficult lets start by exploring how these experiences have shaped your perspective on the world yourself and others we can discuss any additional challenges that may come up during our conversation

Context: ive been struggling with my grades and recently got caught cutting class a few times with my friends just to have some fun and relieve stress my grades were really important to me but now theyre not my priority and i dont know why
Response: its understandable to feel stressed and seek ways to have fun but cutting class may not be the best solution its important to identify why your priorities have shifted and whats causing this change lets discuss your current challenges and stressors and work on finding healthier ways to cope without affecting your academic performance

Context: lately ive been prioritizing hanging out with my friends over school i dont really know why theres a shift in my priorities ive been playing sports with them for a long time and its just us you know doing our own thing my stepmom used to talk with me but now shes been fighting a lot with my dad so we dont get to talk as much
Response: its normal for friendships to be important at this stage of your life but its also crucial to maintain a balance between social activities and school its possible that the conflicts happening at home between your stepmom and dad have led you to seek more comfort and support from your friends i understand that can be tough but try to find a balance and consider talking to your stepmom or another trusted adult about the shifts youre experiencing

Context: i have been facing a lot of conflict lately and my life revolves around school and sports leaving me no time for anything else this has led me to get into some trouble and im not sure why i am acting this way when i am under stress
Response: its understandable that managing school sports and personal life can be challenging and lead to stress it might be helpful for you to identify the factors influencing your behaviors when youre stressed we can work together to better understand these triggers and develop coping strategies to deal with them in a healthier manner does any specific situation or incident come to your mind where you faced severe stress and had difficulty handling it

Context: i feel like my dad and that part of my family like me but i also feel like an outsider sometimes it was hard for me to find someone who would accept me for who i am because i felt like i always had to change myself to fit in i feel angry at my dad and also sad and disappointed about being left out and not staying true to myself in school
Response: it seems like youre struggling with feelings of not being accepted or good enough and this has caused you to feel angry sad and disappointed its important to acknowledge these emotions and understand which aspects of your life contribute to them would you be able to provide more details on how your relationship with your dad has influenced these feelings

Context: some days i really think about my situation and it gets me down especially when my mom is at work and i feel alone but the change has also kind of helped with the feelings my thoughts about my parents divorce and my dad taking my siblings elicit a lot of anger sadness and disappointment
Response: i understand that your feelings can vary depending on the day and situation its important to acknowledge that we cant change certain aspects of our life such as your parents divorce and moving from utah however by examining your thoughts associated with these events we can work on managing the emotions they bring up its evident that youre a caring person and your behaviors may be a result of your thoughts and feelings being overwhelming as a next step lets explore some coping strategies that will help you manage these emotions better

Context: i went from a nondiverse school in utah to a diverse one in california and after that move i felt like i didnt fit in anywhere additionally my parents divorced when i was young which was devastating for me
Response: it sounds like youve experienced some significant life changes and challenges which have left you feeling like you dont belong its completely normal to feel this way when going through such transitions especially in an unfamiliar environment can you tell me more about how youve tried to cope with these feelings or if youve found any activities or groups that help you feel more connected

Context: i feel like my dad didnt think of me as his daughter and that i was an outsider he didnt really care about me and i felt like i wasnt a priority my mom was the only one who really cared but she was working all the time and didnt have much time to spend with me so i was often alone
Response: it sounds like you have experienced a difficult relationship with your father leading you to feel like an outsider and unloved by him this combined with your mothers busy schedule might have contributed to your feelings of loneliness and being less of a priority can you identify any specific events or situations that reinforced these beliefs about yourself

Context: ive been struggling with negative thoughts due to some past events in my life and i wonder if i can change these thoughts that lead to my actions does that make more sense
Response: yes it definitely makes sense while i cannot take away the roots of your negative experiences what i would like to do is help you add more positive roots to your life a lot of the times we tend to focus only on whats gone wrong but by revising our thoughts and creating more balanced ones such as replacing im not good enough with a more positive statement you can eventually influence your actions in a healthier way

Context: i attended a counselling session and we discussed some issues that were troubling me the counsellor made sure i understood everything and i found the session to be really helpful at the end we agreed to set up an appointment for next week
Response: im glad to hear that you found our session helpful and that everything made sense to you its important for you to feel comfortable and supported during our sessions im looking forward to seeing you at our next appointment and continuing our work together if you have any concerns or questions before then please feel free to reach out

Context: ive noticed that when im under the influence of anger and sadness i end up behaving differently lately ive been hanging around with some kids who tend to bully others and ive realized that i dont stand up for the victims and this goes against my value system
Response: its important to recognize that our emotions can influence our behaviors as youve mentioned if youre not comfortable with these new behaviors and they go against your values its crucial to find ways to manage these emotions or distance yourself from situations that contribute to them can you identify any specific triggers or situations that lead to you feeling this anger or sadness

Context: i often feel spiteful towards my parents and that might be the reason why i cut class and choose to hang out with my friends instead of going home after i do these things i feel guilty especially when i dont stick up for others when my friends make fun of them and when my grades go down because i know i can do something about it
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a mix of anger and guilt in response to your behaviors its important to acknowledge these emotions and understand the consequences of your actions which seem to involve both actual punishments and ongoing feelings of guilt or anger i want to ask you one question have you tried discussing your feelings with your parents or considered finding healthier ways to cope with these emotions

Context: i have been feeling stuck in a past relationship that is already over and i think its preventing me from making new connections not just in terms of romantic relationships but also with friends
Response: its important to recognize and acknowledge your feelings about the past relationship it seems like youre aware of how its affecting your current situation i would suggest reflecting on what youve learned from that experience and focusing on moving forward by doing so youd gradually become more open to forming new connections with others is there anything in particular that youre struggling with when trying to reach out to new people

Context: i often find myself constantly thinking about a particular person and it feels like i cannot move on with the rest of my life because of this obsession does this mean i am still in love with him
Response: it seems that your obsession with this person may be preventing you from moving forward in your life however constantly thinking about someone doesnt necessarily mean youre still in love with them it might be helpful to explore why youre so preoccupied with this person and if there are any unresolved emotions or issues that you need to address in order to let go and focus on your own wellbeing

Context: i raised my children by myself after my husband left and everyone says i did a good job they are trying to better themselves and get their careers together and theyre serious about school also my son told me the other day i did a very good job as his mother which made me feel good
Response: it sounds like you have done an incredible job raising your children especially considering you did it on your own its great to hear that they are focused on their education and career paths as it shows that you instilled strong values in them it must have been incredibly validating to receive that positive feedback from your son is there any specific area you feel concerned or unsure about with their development

Context: ive had this ongoing pattern in my life of choosing people like sylvester and im worried about falling into the same pattern again in the future i thought i would just try to be more careful take things slower and really get to know someone before getting involved with them i believe this experience has been a lesson for me
Response: its understandable that youre concerned about repeating past patterns taking things slower and getting to know someone better before becoming involved is a reasonable strategy however its important to also analyze the underlying reasons behind these patterns such as any unmet emotional needs or unresolved past experiences i wonder if you have considered any strategies or support systems to ensure you maintain this new approach in your future relationships

Context: lately ive noticed red flags in potential romantic partners and have dismissed them right away i wonder if im holding onto my ex sylvester to slow things down and avoid getting involved in another relationship i seem to have a pattern of picking losers and hoping they would change i might be a rescuer
Response: its great that youre becoming more aware and cautious of red flags in relationships its possible that holding onto sylvester is a way to prevent yourself from quickly entering new relationships but its also important to explore your pattern of trying to rescue partners reflect on why you tend to choose people who need saving and work on setting boundaries and improving your own wellbeing before entering new relationships

Context: i used to believe that i could fix peoples problems
Response: as a counsellor its important to understand that our role is to guide and support clients not to fix their problems for them we can help them find solutions but ultimately its up to the individuals to make the necessary changes in their lives its great that youre acknowledging this now as it can help you maintain realistic expectations and prevent potential burnout as a helper

Context: i was talking to my therapist about my relationship we discussed how my partner tends to sabotage our relationship but i am still blaming them for it i brought this up during our session and shared my concerns with the therapist
Response: thank you for sharing your concerns about your relationship its important to acknowledge and address any issues that may be causing strife between you and your partner remember its essential to look at the situation from both perspectives and understand the reasons behind your partners actions it might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with your partner about your feelings and concerns would you like some guidance on how to approach this conversation

Context: i feel like i dont have any other way to handle my victimization other than blaming others i know i need to stop isolating myself but i think its okay to be alone sometimes im considering going to selfhelp groups but im not sure if that supports my powerlessness i also want to try to let go of past relationships but im not very confident about it im also worried about pleasing others and seeking their approval in therapy
Response: from your description it seems that you are struggling with handling your emotions effectively and maintaining a healthy balance between being alone and seeking support from others its alright to want some alone time but selfhelp groups can provide valuable support and help you regain your confidence as for letting go of past relationships its a process that takes time and effort in therapy your primary focus should be your own wellbeing and growth not pleasing others are there specific concerns or challenges youve faced while trying to seek help or express your emotions

Context: i struggle to present myself in a positive way and build meaningful connections with people i tend to play the victim and dont know how to handle relationships with people who genuinely love me because ive never had anyone who truly loved me not even my mother
Response: its important to recognize the patterns in your relationships and learn healthier ways to handle them as your counsellor i can help you with psychoeducation to teach you the necessary skills for building more positive connections and recognizing when someone truly loves you lets also discuss any past experiences that might have contributed to your current mindset can you share some instances where you felt unloved or played the victim role with someone close to you

Context: im coming from a chinese background and i believe in taoism sometimes i meditate to attain peace i would like to know your philosophy as a therapist especially when youve traveled to different places and learned from various cultures
Response: its great to learn about your background and beliefs when i work with clients i value the education and understanding i gain from their diverse cultures which helps me adapt my approach accordingly its always fascinating to see how theories and techniques can be adjusted for different cultural contexts i believe that every therapist should be open to learning evolving and adapting their methods based on the unique needs of each client

Context: as a patient i feel like the counsellors i see in videos or during workshops seem so perfect in their sessions i cant help but compare myself to them and feel like i am not as good as them im worried i might not be an effective counsellor
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concern but remember that those videotaped sessions usually show the best moments and dont include any challenges or difficulties the counsellors might face comparing yourself to those idealized examples may not be fair focus on your own improvement and learning from your experiences and keep in mind nobody is perfect and we all have our unique strengths and areas of growth is there any particular skill or area that you feel youre struggling with

Context: as a patient coming from a chinese culture background i appreciate how serious and attentive you were when i was sharing my problems also i noticed that you remembered a lot of details from our previous conversations which made me feel like you had a map in your mind however i felt a bit unsure when you were trying to provide insights about my issues like identifying patterns or attachments it seemed you didnt have any doubt when moving on to the next agenda
Response: thank you for your feedback im glad you noticed and appreciated my attentiveness and efforts to remember details its important to me to create a safe and supportive environment for my clients regarding the insights i apologize if it seemed that i didnt have doubts or hesitations in our next session i will make a conscious effort to explain my thought process and welcome your input to ensure we maintain an open dialogue if you feel unsure about any of my insights or suggestions please feel free to voice your concerns or ask for clarification

Context: i have been thinking about your comments on how you dont really care about the techniques ive been trying to identify your counseling style but its hard to pinpoint as i can see elements of rogerian and solutionfocused approaches that has made me question your overall design for helping me achieve my desires
Response: i appreciate your observations and i understand that it might be difficult to label my counseling style my approach is to use different techniques and strategies tailored to your needs and circumstances rather than strictly adhering to one specific therapy model my ultimate goal is to support and guide you in discovering and achieving your desires if you have any concerns please let me know

Context: as a patient i feel frustrated that as a beginner in therapy im looking for concrete answers and specifics about how the process works im also concerned about the fact that the outcomes of therapy might not be exactly what i expect or remember
Response: as a counsellor i understand that it can be difficult for those new to therapy to grasp the complexities of the process its important to acknowledge that therapy doesnt always provide concrete answers and the outcomes can be different from what we expect its not always about the specific techniques or interventions but more about the connection and deeper understanding developed during therapy its important to be patient and open to growth during the process can you share more about your expectations from therapy

Context: i have been working with harriet in therapy but i sometimes wonder if she really wants to change or if shes just here to look like shes making an effort i try to trust her and believe what she presents during our sessions
Response: its understandable to have concerns about a patients motivation for change however building trust is essential in a therapeutic relationship so its important to continue validating harriets feelings and experiences additionally you can gently explore her goals and motivations for attending therapy to gain a better understanding of her true desires for change remember the therapeutic process can be complex and sometimes progress may not be apparent right away

Context: as the patient i didnt provide any information or ask any questions
Response: as the counsellor i am unable to provide any feedback or ask any questions as there was no information provided or questions asked by the patient

Context: i really dont know what it would take for me to not only realize when someone is not giving me what i deserve and what i want in a relationship but also to remember it when it really counts right now this situation feels so low and i dont feel like i have the energy or the drive to do what it would take
Response: its completely understandable that youre feeling low and lacking energy at the moment navigating relationships can be challenging and recognizing what you deserve is an essential step for personal growth when you feel ready consider reflecting on your past experiences and what you desire in future relationships you may also benefit from discussing your feelings with a trusted friend or therapist who can provide support and help you identify patterns and set boundaries remember healing takes time and its crucial to be patient with yourself throughout this process

Context: i am feeling a bit out of control in one area of my life while everything else seems to be going well i am attending classes and bettering myself in other ways but i have noticed that i seem to make poor choices in relationships like the one i had with sylvester
Response: its great to hear that you are investing time in personal growth and bettering yourself i understand that you feel out of control in one area and it is related to past relationships and the choices made since this is not the first time youve experienced similar relationship issues i would encourage you to reflect on the patterns in these relationships could you share with me the most common problems you have faced in these situations

Context: i was in a relationship with a drug addict and it was really bad so i ended up in deep depression and stayed away from relationships for about 3 years my previous partner sylvester was very angry i think i just pick the wrong people maybe because my father was emotionally distant and my mother wasnt very helpful
Response: it sounds like youve had some challenging experiences in your past relationships and its possible that your family background may be influencing your choices as a counsellor id like to explore how your upbringing has impacted your relationship patterns and help you develop healthier strategies for future connections have you noticed any specific patterns in the way you choose or interact with your partners

Context: i think if i didnt have this problem anymore and didnt think about him at all it would be relaxing and feel much better but i am also worried about the loneliness that comes with it i feel like he threw me out into the world by myself and as long as i stay obsessed with him its like i still have a part of him with me and im not quite so alone
Response: its understandable that letting go of the obsession brings both relief and fear of loneliness while it might be comforting to hold onto the connection with him it is important to focus on moving forward and building new connections can you think of any activities or hobbies that may help you meet new people and develop a sense of belonging so you can gradually overcome the loneliness

Context: ive been feeling really lonely and alone lately even though sylvester is out of my life im still thinking about him constantly i feel like i havent been able to set any goals or do much because my thoughts are preoccupied with him
Response: it seems that your thoughts about sylvester are making it difficult for you to focus on yourself and your own goals this could be because holding onto him provides some comfort in the face of loneliness if you were to let him go completely not only from your life but also from your thoughts it might help you feel more motivated to set goals and take action are there any specific goals you have in mind that youd like to work on

Context: lately ive been using my boyfriend as a kind of excuse not to pursue certain opportunities or make myself more available for other things im not entirely sure why im doing this though
Response: its possible that you might be experiencing some fear or insecurity regarding the opportunities youre avoiding and using your boyfriend as a safety net id like to know more about the specific situations youve avoided and the reasons behind them this can help us better understand the pattern and work towards overcoming it

Context: ive been struggling with being alone and the idea of being without a man in my life im trying to toy with the idea of taking the risk but im not quite ready to commit to it yet
Response: its normal to feel some anxiety about being alone especially when youre used to being in a relationship however its essential to learn how to be independent and embrace the opportunity to grow can you identify any specific fears or concerns that might be preventing you from taking this step

Context: as a patient i feel like the clients that counsellors think theyre helping the most might just be pretending and the ones that appear to not have been helped at all might have actually benefited from the session
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concern it can be difficult to gauge the effectiveness of counseling sessions i make it a priority to create an open atmosphere where clients can provide honest feedback in this sense its important for both the client and the counsellor to communicate openly about the process and progress do you have any specific concerns regarding your own therapy progress

Context: as a patient i visited a therapist only once or twice but i want to express my gratitude for the significant difference they made in my life i made several changes after our sessions and i just remembered that i never really thanked them properly
Response: as a counsellor it is always rewarding to hear that our work has had a positive impact on our clients lives it is not uncommon for clients to only have a few sessions before experiencing growth and change remember that selfreflection and openness to new ideas are key elements in the therapeutic process keep embracing these qualities to continue your personal development and thank you for sharing your gratitude

Context: as a patient im not sure which therapy theory to choose but my mentor suggested one that he strongly supports what do you think about following that specific theory
Response: as a counsellor i agree that starting with a theory that your mentor or supervisor recommends is a good starting point however its essential to keep in mind that it may not be the perfect fit for you and could evolve as you learn and grow in your practice remember the purpose of a theory is to guide and inform your therapeutic approach and its normal for therapists to adapt their methods over time

Context: as a patient i noticed that the counsellor was following a personcentered approach to build a relationship with me however during the middle of our session i felt that they seemed to be feeling trapped what could be the reasons behind this
Response: as a counsellor i may have felt trapped due to the potential complexity of your situation or it could be related to my own personal feelings or experiences that might be influencing my approach to our session it is important for me to maintain selfawareness and address any personal issues that might impact my ability to effectively help you rest assured im committed to providing the best possible care and support for you if you have any concerns please feel free to share them

Context: i remember talking to my previous counselor about what i didnt like about their approach and she had warned me however i feel as if i was set up to experience the same thing again i labeled my experience in a more personcentered way but i still feel uncomfortable
Response: it sounds like you experienced some challenges with your previous counselors approach and were hoping for a different experience this time as your new counsellor i want to make sure we avoid any negative feelings going forward can you please provide more details about what specifically made you uncomfortable with the previous approach by understanding your concerns i can better adapt my approach to your needs

Context: as the patient i felt like my counsellor really listened to me and helped me feel heard they took their time to understand my concerns and kept referring back to them throughout the conversation i was impressed with how they were able to keep track of everything i mentioned
Response: as the counsellor i appreciate your positive feedback its important for me to ensure that my clients feel heard and understood my goal is to provide a safe space for you to express your concerns and by referring back to them show that i am actively engaged in our conversation is there anything you would like to discuss further or any areas you feel we could explore deeper

Context: ive been learning counseling for 25 years and had some really good mentors with the dominant model back then however ive moved beyond that but i still feel like theres much more for me to learn
Response: its great to hear that you have been in the counseling field for 25 years and have learned from good mentors its natural to feel like theres more to learn especially in an everevolving field like counseling every experience and interaction can provide you with new knowledge and understanding if you can please share an instance where you felt challenged in adapting to new counseling models or situations

Context: ive been seeing a therapist who has given me some affirmations for positive thinking which has been helpful she also had me create a list of tasks and provided me with support and encouragement when i completed them this made me feel better because ive been lacking support in my life
Response: it sounds like your therapist has been helping you develop a more positive mindset and has provided you with valuable support how do you think these techniques can be extended in your daily life to help you continue making progress and coping with challenges

Context: lately ive been going through a lot of stuff and i didnt have much support in my life at that time but i had a friend who was very supportive i would just vent to her and she would listen to me and i would feel better after i left because i got a lot of things that were bothering me out
Response: its really important to have someone supportive in your life that you can talk to and trust when youre going through difficult times im glad to hear that your friend has been there for you it sounds like being able to vent to her has helped you process and release some of the stress and emotions youve been experiencing is there something specific thats causing you the most stress lately

Context: ive been having a hard time getting away from a destructive relationship because i tend to forget what we discuss in our sessions my therapist pointed out that this person is similar to my family background and we made a chart comparing their qualities to those of my family and exhusband then we made a chart of what i really want and she showed me that what i want and what this person is are different however i still feel like i might be addicted to him and cant let go
Response: its important to recognize that breaking free from a destructive relationship is not an easy task but your therapist is providing helpful tools such as the charts to help you see the differences between what you want and what your current situation is the feeling of addiction could be an indication of codependency which can be addressed in therapy remain diligent in your sessions and actively work on your personal growth and selfawareness are there any specific strategies or coping mechanisms that youve found helpful in your attempts to create distance in this relationship

Context: sometimes my brain tells me that something is the right thing to do but i still feel hesitant and unsure about it why does this happen
Response: its common for people to experience a conflict between their thoughts and emotions your mind might be telling you one thing while your emotions pull you in a different direction this can be confusing and challenging to navigate its important to acknowledge both your thoughts and feelings and try to find a balance between them reflect on your values and longterm goals and consider discussing your concerns with someone you trust or a professional counsellor for guidance

Context: im holding on to sylvester because i feel like it might be my last chance sometimes i think that maybe in a few years hell realize what a wonderful person i am and how good i am for him
Response: it does seem sad that there was potential in your relationship with sylvester but both of you were not able to make it work in some ways he was really afraid of you and the relationship and did what he could to sabotage it as we have limited time left i want you to reflect on your feelings and thoughts when you drive home today

Context: ill probably remember what you said about him sabotaging the relationship and about not isolating myself and maybe having my counselor talk about ways to feel good about myself being alone i think maybe thats where we should work on
Response: its great that youre taking these insights with you in the next session with your counselor discuss ways to develop a positive selfimage while being alone and explore other areas that might help you in personal growth remember focusing on yourself and building a strong support network can significantly contribute to your wellbeing

Context: im attending meetings and trying to let go of someone whos significant in my life but im still hesitant about this decision i dont like being pushed by others to make choices im not ready for yet what do you suggest i do
Response: its completely normal to feel hesitant about such decisions and its important to take your time to process your feelings youre already attending meetings which is a great start i encourage you to focus on selfcare explore your emotions and take advice from others cautiously remember only you know whats best for yourself so trust your instincts and make decisions when you feel fully ready

Context: i think i need to have a plan in order to manage my life better
Response: its great that you recognize the need for a plan in your life having a plan can help create structure and keep you focused on your goals think about what you want to achieve break those goals into smaller milestones and prioritize them this will make it easier to track your progress and stay motivated if you feel overwhelmed dont hesitate to ask for assistance from friends family or professionals

Context: i recently realized that i have abandonment issues and i think im love addicted because ive been reading a lot about it i really want love in my life but sometimes im afraid that it might be too late for me being an older person i might tell my counselor about what ive learned about isolating myself
Response: its great that youve recognized your abandonment issues and love addiction it would definitely help to discuss these with your counselor remember its never too late to work on yourself and find love in various aspects of your life as for your fear of being isolated it could potentially lead to a breakthrough in your therapy consider sharing all of these insights with your counselor to take your work together to the next level

Context: ive noticed a pattern in my relationships where the other person takes from me and doesnt give back i guess i need to find someone who loves me back but maybe i should also focus on finding love and support in other ways without a man
Response: yes realizing this pattern is important in your relationships its crucial to find someone who loves you back and shares a mutual balanced connection additionally finding love and support within yourself and from other sources like friends and family will help you establish a strong foundation without depending on a romantic relationship remember you have a lot of love to give and you deserve to be surrounded by support and care

Context: its just been so frustrating for me that it doesnt feel like my efforts have been reciprocated in this one dimension or area and in some ways i do feel discouraged about whether im ever going to be able to enjoy that kind of equal relationship with someone
Response: i understand that youre feeling frustrated and discouraged about not having an equal relationship with someone its natural to feel this way when your efforts are not reciprocated would you like to share more about the particular situation or relationship that is causing you this frustration so we can explore ways to overcome it

Context: i first came to counseling because i was feeling depressed about a relationship and struggling to manage different aspects of my life such as classes children and work my counselor has helped me to think more positive and start to feel better but im still trying to find a way to juggle all these responsibilities
Response: its great to hear that you have already made progress with thinking more positively and feeling better its important to maintain a healthy balance in life so lets focus on the remaining challenge youre facing which is juggling your various commitments one option could be prioritizing your tasks and setting realistic goals for yourself can you share which tasks currently demand most of your time and energy

Context: i was dealing with stress and a verbally abusive relationship which my previous therapist was helping me with we would work on how to build myself back up after being hurt recently i finally broke up with the person but now im feeling sad again im trying to get over the break up
Response: it sounds like youve been through a tough time facing a cycle of stress and an abusive relationship its important to acknowledge the progress youve made by ending that relationship now we can work on healing and moving forward from the experience also remember to consider other aspects of your life that might require support such as your children and personal goals how has the breakup impacted your daily life and what kind of support do you have around you

Context: i have been under a lot of stress because of work and my children are going away to school leaving me alone additionally im going through a job change where ill be doing something completely new
Response: its understandable that youre feeling stressed due to your children leaving and job transition it can be difficult to adapt to new situations and face uncertainties but remember that change can also bring growth and new opportunities try focusing on ways to manage stress such as exercise connecting with friends or finding new interests is there anything specific about the new job that has you worried

Context: ive been working with a patient who is already seeing another counselor so im being cautious because i dont want to mess anything up i want to make sure my work supports the existing therapy
Response: its important to approach this situation with sensitivity and maintain open communication with the patient ask the patient about their progress and goals in the ongoing therapy and offer your support and insights to enrich their therapeutic experience be mindful not to contradict the other counselors approach but rather collaborate and enhance the overall process for the patients benefit

Context: as i was watching counseling videos i noticed how skilled the counsellor was in several different theories and approaches i worry that as a counseling student i might feel overwhelmed trying to become proficient in so many areas how can beginners manage this and avoid feeling overwhelmed
Response: its understandable that you might feel overwhelmed when observing the use of multiple theories in counseling sessions however its important to remember that as a beginner you dont have to master all of these approaches at once focus on learning the fundamentals of one theory and as you gain experience you can gradually integrate other approaches it takes time to become proficient so be patient with yourself and embrace the learning process

Context: recently i have been trying various relaxation techniques and ive tried 13 different ones but i cant seem to find one that works for me could you please suggest how i can find the right technique
Response: its great that youre exploring relaxation techniques but finding the right one can take time and experimentation i would recommend focusing on one technique at a time and give it some time to see if its effective for you keep a relaxation journal to track which techniques youve tried and your experiences with each if youre still having difficulty finding the right one consider seeking a professionals assistance who can tailor a relaxation strategy specifically for your needs

Context: ive been feeling that things like risktaking bungee jumping and parachuting can be important metaphors for what were asking in our lives but im concerned about how taking more risks may lead to ethical problems or exploitation in relationships
Response: its understandable that you view risktaking as an important aspect of personal growth and selfdiscovery however its crucial to strike a balance between taking calculated risks and maintaining healthy relationships without crossing ethical boundaries lets discuss strategies to navigate these challenges while still embracing the opportunities for growth that come with risktaking are there any specific situations you have in mind that concern you

Context: i feel uncomfortable when i realize my own hypocrisy in a session i find it difficult to ask clients to do something that im unwilling or unable to do myself and it makes me question my effectiveness as a therapist
Response: it is important for therapists to have selfawareness and examine their own behaviors and inconsistencies the fact that youre noticing this shows that youre a reflective counselor which can help you grow professionally if you are worried about your effectiveness consider seeking supervision engaging in personal therapy or participating in professional development activities to enhance your skills and address any areas of concern

Context: ive been struggling lately to even get out of bed in the morning but somehow i manage to drag myself to work and do a good job with my clients
Response: it sounds like you are facing some difficulty in your personal life but you still manage to find the strength to go on with your professional responsibilities its important to acknowledge your resilience in managing to do well at work despite your challenges maybe its time to take a deeper look into the issues youre experiencing and find ways to address them have you considered seeking support or trying out any coping strategies to help with your situation

Context: as a patient i have been struggling with feelings of worthlessness specifically that im not worthwhile unless there is a man in my life this has led me to make sacrifices in my relationships as my dad used to say that i pay a lot for a man
Response: as a counsellor i understand that youve been struggling with feelings of low selfworth and dependence on a male partner for validation from a feminist perspective its important to recognize your inherent worth as an individual separate from any relationship i encourage you to reflect on the source of these beliefs and work towards building your selfesteem independently of any romantic partner do you have any specific experiences that might have led you to form these beliefs

Context: ive been experiencing some problems lately and im not sure how to deal with them i feel like these situations might be something familiar from my past
Response: as a counsellor i would like to help you explore these situations further its interesting that you mentioned the familiarity of these problems i wonder how this is related to your past experiences and what patterns might be repeating in your life in order to understand better could you share an example of a situation that has been troubling you and how it may be linked to your past

Context: i feel like my behavior is meant to keep me from being alone and i wonder if my actions are functional in achieving that goal is there a specific scheme or structure you have in mind for counselling me in this situation
Response: its not uncommon for people to adopt behaviors to avoid loneliness in counselling we would explore the goals and purpose behind your behavior and work towards understanding its functionality an adlerian approach may be helpful in this case as it focuses on your behaviors purpose and identifying potential areas for growth can you tell me more about the actions you have taken to avoid being alone

Context: ive been having trouble with my therapist as we seem to be stuck in our sessions and i feel like im not making progress i get along better with other therapists and tend to be more cooperative with them what should i do
Response: its important to have good communication and trust with your therapist for effective therapy id like to know more about your experiences with your current therapist and how it differs from your experiences with others however i suggest discussing your concerns with your current therapist and exploring whether there are any communication barriers or misunderstandings that might be impeding progress remember its always an option to consider seeking help from another therapist if you feel it would be more beneficial for you

Context: im a counselor trainee and i see that theres a higher level of connection between the counselor therapist and the client beyond our current understanding im wondering how we can encourage junior counselors or therapists to admire and explore this freedom and space that exists beyond our conceptualization
Response: its important for counselors and therapists to develop not only their professional skills but also themselves as individuals the changes we promote in others occur not just because of what were doing but who we are therefore i encourage junior counselors and therapists to focus on personal growth and selfawareness striving to practice what they preach in their own lives this will help them connect with clients on a deeper level and discover the freedom and space that exists beyond traditional methods

Context: ive been obsessing over this one area of my life involving sylvester but i recently took an inventory of my whole life context which made me realize that while this situation may not be going so well i have other aspects such as roller skating and friends who have been supportive about the situation
Response: its great that you took the initiative to take a holistic inventory of your life allowing you to recognize whats going well besides the area involving sylvester support from friends and engaging in activities like roller skating can definitely provide a good balance how do your children feel about the situation and have you tried discussing it with them

Context: i have been feeling low and i dont want to interact with people my friends and family make comments about me looking sad and it makes me want to isolate myself further when i do go out i pretend to be feeling better than i actually am
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some tough emotions and struggling with social interactions its important to acknowledge your feelings and not force yourself to pretend to be okay would you like to share more about whats been causing your sadness or any specific triggers that made you feel this way

Context: lately ive been feeling overwhelmed and stressed about my personal life and work im not sure how to cope with these emotions in my next session with my counselor i will talk about our conversation and how it affected me
Response: i appreciate you sharing your feelings with me its essential to discuss your concerns in your next counseling session you might mention feeling overwhelmed and stressed and together with your counselor you can explore coping strategies and resources to help you manage your emotions its also important to address how our conversation has impacted you as it might help tailor future sessions remember seeking support from a professional is a crucial step towards improving your overall mental wellbeing

Context: i felt like i was so low that i couldnt get direction my previous counsellor even told me how i looked stating that i appeared like a little lonely child sitting in the corner it made me feel worse and i cried because i felt like she was beating me up her confrontations made me feel like i should just go and hide instead of facing the world
Response: it seems that your previous counsellors approach was not helpful for you at that time and her comments made you feel worse about yourself confrontations can sometimes make a person feel more vulnerable and defeated as a counsellor my aim is to provide a safe and supportive environment to explore your concerns do you want to share more about what led you to feel so low and how you would like to move forward from that point

Context: as a patient i have been seeing a counselor already and im here just for this one meeting with you i would like to know how you can support the work i am already doing without causing any interference
Response: as a counsellor i understand your concern and i appreciate you being open about your ongoing counseling process in this single session i will focus on enhancing the progress youve made in your current counseling instead of altering anything to do that effectively i would appreciate it if you could share what strategies or techniques have been working well for you in your previous sessions this way i can align my support with what youre already doing

Context: i have been working on letting go of my children as i am living alone again and it feels more lonely since my recent relationship ended additionally i am dealing with a job transition and all the stress that comes with it
Response: it seems like you are experiencing mixed emotions due to your current life situation youre having trouble letting go of your children and your recent relationship ending coupled with the job transition has increased your stress levels what have you tried so far to cope with these changes and what hasnt been working for you

Context: ive been trying to move on from a past relationship but theres a part of me that still feels connected to him even though my previous counselor told me what to do i would often forget their advice when i went home
