Response: it seems like youre experiencing a conflict between wanting to let go of the relationship and still feeling connected to your expartner its possible that you havent fully internalized your counselors advice or that there are aspects of the relationship you valued and appreciated its important to reflect on what these aspects might be and if they are worth holding onto or if they are hindering your process of letting go and moving on

Context: i always felt that my previous partner was the one for me we got along very well had good conversations and he was intelligent however there were a lot of things that he did that werent good for me at all and made me not feel good about myself
Response: it is important to recognize both the positive and negative aspects of previous relationships it seems like your counselor has helped you to look more clearly at the situation can you explain some specific instances where your partner has made you not feel good about yourself and how your counselor has assisted you in dealing with those situations

Context: ive been having trouble in my previous counseling sessions because when my relationship ended for the second time my previous counsellor didnt seem to want to help me instead she just told me that i had to make up my own mind which left me feeling really bad and distraught
Response: it sounds like you were seeking guidance and support during a difficult time but you felt that your previous counsellor didnt provide the help you needed its important that you feel understood and supported in your counseling sessions in our sessions together i will make sure to listen to your concerns and provide guidance to help you navigate through your emotions and decisions what would you like to focus on or achieve during our time together

Context: ive been working on things like doing my artwork getting more physical exercise and bettering myself in school however ive isolated myself and dont have a lot of support ive recently started attending some 12step meetings
Response: its great to hear that youre focusing on personal growth and finding activities that you find fulfilling while isolation can be a challenge attending 12step meetings is a good step towards building a supportive community what kind of connections or support are you hoping to find in these meetings

Context: lately ive been attending a spiritual group meeting which has helped me to think more clearly about situations in my past relationship i feel like i was somewhat controlling because i was trying to push my partner to have the relationship with me i have started to blame myself for this behavior
Response: it sounds like attending the spiritual group has been beneficial for you in gaining clarity and selfawareness its important to recognize your part in past relationships but also to practice selfcompassion and try to learn from your past experiences one aspect of the 12step program involves letting go how are you working on implementing this in your life

Context: ive been realizing how powerless i am over people places and things and that i have no control over them however putting my life in gods hands and following the 12step program has been helping me
Response: its great to hear that the 12step program has been helping you recognizing and accepting the things you cannot control is an essential part of growth and healing it seems that your relationship with god has provided you with strength and guidance keep working on your recovery and stay focused on your spiritual journey is there any particular challenge youre facing right now that youd like to discuss

Context: i recently attended a group session where people shared their stories and i realized that its mostly this one area in my life where i feel out of control while other people seemed to struggle with multiple areas i felt less alone and it was actually good for me in a way because my issues seem less overwhelming compared to others
Response: im glad to hear that attending the group session was a positive experience for you its important to feel connected with others who share similar experiences as it can provide support and perspective on your own situation remember everyones journey is different and its not a competition focus on your own personal growth and take inspiration from the progress of others as you work on improving that one area in your life if youre comfortable sharing what is the specific area you feel you need to work on

Context: i have a history of making poor choices in relationships i was with a drug addict who put me through a lot of hardship and i went into a deep depression i avoided relationships for about three years before getting involved with sylvester who is also very angry i feel like i just pick the wrong people
Response: it seems youve experienced a pattern of difficult relationships which has led to emotional distress and depression its important to recognize these patterns and understand the factors that contribute to making such choices can you identify any common traits or characteristics in these partners that may have drawn you to them initially despite their negative behaviors

Context: ive been feeling really consumed by negative emotions lately and ive noticed that i tend to take myself too seriously ive heard that humor could potentially be an antidote for my depression but sometimes its hard for me to see the absurdity in my situation can you help me with this
Response: its completely normal to feel overwhelmed by negativity sometimes but its important to remind ourselves not to take everything too seriously as a counsellor i would suggest exploring ways to incorporate humor into your daily life which could help alleviate the intensity of those negative emotions additionally we can work on recognizing the absurdity of certain situations and use this perspective to help reduce depression and gain a more balanced outlook on life

Context: as the patient i think i need a breakthrough but it feels like the whole world has to change i havent been completely honest with my counselor yet and theres so much i havent told them about what i do and how it affects me
Response: as the counsellor i appreciate your vulnerability and willingness to share more with me its important that we have an open line of communication to help facilitate your growth and progress so what is one significant thing you feel you havent shared with me yet this information might be crucial for us to find the breakthrough you are seeking and help identify changes that need to happen within rather than expecting the world to change

Context: as a patient i recently had a therapy session where my therapist used various techniques he was strategic used some reframing and asked me what works and what doesnt work he also used some cognitive approaches about cueing and being language sensitive he didnt use as much cognitive stuff as he normally would but asked me what i was thinking about and what i would think about after the session
Response: as a counsellor it seems like your therapist is adopting an integrative approach combining elements from different therapeutic modalities to better address your concerns it is helpful for you to pay attention to the techniques that resonate with you most and share your experiences with your therapist in the next session you can discuss the strategies that were most effective for you and if there were any parts of the session that felt uncomfortable or not helpful so that your therapist can continue to tailor their approach to your needs

Context: ive been feeling stuck in my situation with sylvester and its been affecting me negatively im trying to understand the stories i tell myself from a constructivist point of view and my own phenomenological experience what are some alternative stories that i could consider to help me feel better what would things be like if this problem was resolved
Response: as a counsellor id like to acknowledge your selfawareness and willingness to explore alternative perspectives given the constructivist approach we can work together to identify the stories youre telling yourself and examine how theyre shaping your experiences we can then consider other narrative possibilities that might change your outlook to envision a resolution think about the benefits of being unstuck from your situation with sylvester and the potential consequences reflect on the secondary gains you might be receiving from your current situation and how that might be playing a role in keeping you stuck ultimately understanding the factors that contribute to your feelings of being stuck will help us develop strategies for overcoming the challenges

Context: im having a hard time dealing with how much control and power ive given away to certain men in my life i feel like its affecting my sense of selfworth and selfrespect can you help me with this issue
Response: its important to recognize these feelings and the patterns of giving away power in relationships i see that youre aware of the issue which is a great first step lets explore some possible reasons behind this behavior and work on developing strategies to regain control and empower yourself if there was a specific situation that brought up these feelings can you share more details about it

Context: as a patient i have a question about how your integrative approach which i find fluid and different for every client relates to cultural intentionality like in allen iveys model i notice how ivey stresses on skills techniques and cultural aspects so im curious how your approach is different or similar to his in terms of incorporating culture
Response: as a counsellor i believe that my integrative approach shares similarities with allen iveys model in terms of our thought processes however our methods might look different in implementation as my approach focuses on fluidity and personalization for each clients unique needs while ivey emphasizes specific skills techniques and cultural considerations in either approach we aim to be culturally sensitive and respond to cultural factors that affect our clients but the specific techniques or balance of how we integrate culture might vary from case to case

Context: i feel like the people in south chicago have a very different culture from the suburbs in the north and it also varies by gender religion and ethnicity its important to change our approach according to these different aspects to understand who a person is and where they come from
Response: as a counsellor i completely agree with your observation the culture of an individual is crucial in understanding their background values and experiences it enables me to tailor my counselling approach effectively to meet your needs could you please share any specific cultural or personal factors that you believe are impacting your current situation so we can address them appropriately together

Context: i am feeling a bit overwhelmed because youre discussing a variety of subjects such as culturalmindedness and incorporating 12 or 13 different theories or techniques i sense that theres an authentic use of self in your approach but when i hear words like chameleon and eclectic i cant help but feel like we might be playing games or acting mechanically can you help me understand how to manage these feelings
Response: i understand how you might feel overwhelmed with the various topics weve discussed its essential in counselling to maintain an authentic approach while also utilizing a variety of theories and techniques synchronizing these elements can feel daunting but its not about playing games or being mechanical as a counsellor i try to adapt my approach based on your individual needs and background to provide the most effective support over time you may find that you can trust the process and embrace the eclectic approach in a positive way

Context: i was in a relationship with someone who would often say mean and cruel things to push me away i tried to overlook it and made excuses for him but he didnt seem to care about me as much as i cared about him even after talking to my counselor about all the reasons why this relationship wasnt good for me i still feel confused and frustrated
Response: its natural to feel confused and frustrated when youve invested emotionally in a relationship that doesnt seem to be working its important to acknowledge your feelings and start working on healing yourself you may want to explore the reasons you were drawn to this person and why you stayed despite the hurtful behavior in the future try to set boundaries and prioritize your selfworth to avoid this kind of situation remember that selfcare and seeking professional help when required are crucial steps towards healing

Context: i feel like i have two conflicting thoughts in my head one part of me wants to end my relationship because its not good for me but the other part loves and cares for my partner and ive invested a lot in this relationship when im with them the negative thoughts dont seem as important
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing an internal conflict between your rational thinking and your emotional attachment to your partner this is quite normal in complex relationships its important to listen to both voices and weigh the pros and cons of staying or leaving the relationship consider seeking professional support to help you navigate this decisionmaking process if necessary

Context: ive been going back and forth about a decision and its making me very tired i think about it constantly morning and night
Response: its normal to feel tired and overwhelmed when youre constantly thinking about a difficult decision try setting aside some specific time to analyze the situation and list the pros and cons of each option once youve made a decision remind yourself of the reasons behind your choice and trust your judgment can you share more about the decision youre trying to make

Context: im feeling worried about making mistakes and looking foolish especially with the pressure from managed care to make quick progress
Response: its normal to feel nervous about making mistakes and trying to meet expectations managed care can add extra pressure to achieve results quickly its important to remember that therapy is a process and its okay to take time to address feelings of anxiety or worry it might be more beneficial to focus on developing trust and understanding in the initial sessions rather than rushing for quick results

Context: ive been struggling with trying to imitate the way other people work especially my mentors i attend workshops but i still feel incompetent and its getting me into trouble
Response: its normal to feel inspired by mentors and want to adopt their methods but its also important to develop your own unique style focus on building your own strengths and skills and dont be too hard on yourself have you discussed your feelings of incompetence with your mentors or sought their guidance on how to improve

Context: as a patient i have experienced some tragic results with more intrusive and paradoxical techniques they were quite aggressive and did not work out the way they were shown in the video tapes
Response: as a counsellor i understand how disheartening it can be when a technique doesnt work as anticipated its important to remember that every individual is unique and not every method will be effective for everyone can you provide more details on how you specifically reacted to the technique so we can identify a more suitable approach for your situation

Context: i dont know what it would take for me to move on in my relationship with sylvester i guess maybe look for another man but im not really ready to let go of sylvester yet despite my counselor and friends advice
Response: it sounds like youre not quite ready to let go of sylvester and thats completely normal people can give you advice but ultimately you have to make the decision to move on when youre ready instead of seeking a new relationship right away maybe focus on yourself and what makes you happy and fulfilled this will help you in being prepared to move on when the time is right

Context: i feel so annoyed and controlled by sylvester hes the one who decided to end things and its not good for me
Response: it sounds like youre feeling frustrated and powerless due to sylvesters actions its important to remember that you have control over your own life and decisions moving forward can you tell me more about your relationship with him and why you feel hes not good for you

Context: i am struggling to move forward in my life and feel like i deserve more i want to become the kind of person who can confidently say no to people who make me feel unworthy however i am not there yet how can i get to that point
Response: its great that you recognize the need for growth and the type of person you want to become to get there working with a counselor can help you identify the barriers preventing you from reaching your goal and provide support in overcoming them we can explore your thought processes beliefs and emotions and collaboratively develop strategies to build your selfesteem and assertiveness it may take some time but its important to remember that this is an ongoing journey towards selfimprovement

Context: as a patient id say that my children and other people think im a good mother but i have a hard time taking pride in my motherhood role it didnt seem important to me and i had no choice but to be in that situation
Response: as a counsellor i acknowledge your feelings toward motherhood and how you may struggle to give yourself credit for being a good mother its important to reflect on the positive feedback youve received from your children and others and also consider the reasons behind your reluctance to embrace your role can you share any specific experiences or thoughts that might have contributed to this attitude towards motherhood

Context: as a single parent i never had the luxury of thinking about what i wanted to do but now in my work and career i am finally at a point where i am asking myself what i want to do i havent been satisfied with what ive been doing and i am taking charge of my life by wanting to go in a completely new direction i am really happy about the job change
Response: its great to see that youre taking control of your life by exploring new directions in your career its a significant step especially after dedicating so much time to parenting you mentioned you are happy about the job change which is a positive sign can you please share more about your new job and how it aligns with your personal goals or interests

Context: i managed to pass a course and get a job i was on the waiting list for about a year when there was an opening they called me and asked if i was still interested after agreeing i studied hard watched videos and passed the course i only missed two questions out of 50 and im really proud of myself
Response: congratulations on your achievement you have shown great dedication and persistence by completing the course and getting the job its natural to feel proud of yourself when youve excelled in something like this continue to apply the same level of dedication in your new job and youll surely find success there as well keep up the great work

Context: i feel like i never really got too connected with anyone in my life  not my father my kids or even my boyfriend it feels like i am just going through everything without really feeling a connection is there a place for me to make these connections stronger
Response: its natural to feel lost at times and struggle with building connections as your counsellor i want to reassure you that theres always a place and opportunity to deepen connections with the people around you it might help to explore different communication styles and ways to express yourself more authentically can you share a specific situation where you felt disconnected so we can work together on navigating those moments

Context: i can sense that i have a victim mentality and carry a lot of anger and resentment around it i am also very compliant and i think my experience as an africanamerican woman has a connection to my current situation how would you help me deal with this anger and figure out its roots
Response: its important to acknowledge your emotions and experiences as an africanamerican woman i would work with you to explore the sources of your anger and resentment as well as the factors contributing to your compliance we would discuss your past experiences cultural background and any unresolved issues that might be fueling these emotions to help you cope with your anger i would also introduce healthy strategies such as assertiveness training and stress management techniques to empower you and create a more balanced emotional state is there any specific situation or incident that particularly triggers your anger and victim mentality

Context: as a patient i am stuck in a pattern where i try to change my behavior but end up doing the same thing just slower i struggle with finding constructive solutions and taking meaningful steps forward my therapist mentioned that they were trying to help me gain insight and translate that into constructive action but im still not getting the outcome i want

Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some internal conflicts and thats being projected outwardly through the interpersonal conflicts youre having its important to understand that we all have different aspects of ourselves depending on the context and situation instead of trying to pinpoint one real self focus on embracing the different parts of yourself and finding a healthy balance remember not all conflicts are harmful some can lead to invigorating conversations or personal growth if youre constantly worrying about this perhaps we could explore these conflicts together and work on embracing the various parts of your personality

Context: as a patient im struggling with an internal conflict between two aspects of myself the dork and the hip person i feel like theres a voice inside me saying youre not good enough im not sure how to relate to the world outside and resolve conflicts with other people
Response: as a counsellor i understand youre experiencing an internal conflict between the dork and the hip person aspects of yourself as well as feeling pressure from a voice saying youre not good enough its essential to explore the perspectives of both the dork and the hip person and what they would say to each other this way you can understand their roles in your life and create a healthier balance which may help you better relate to the world outside and resolve conflicts with others

Context: i dont know what theyd say but i know they wouldnt like each other
Response: it seems like youre uncertain about how these individuals would interact and express their dislike for each other considering that you dont have specific information it might be helpful to step back and acknowledge that you cannot control or predict others actions or behavior focus on what you can control such as your own reactions and interactions with others

Context: ive always thought of myself as a dork and i tend to ignore this side of myself because i find it unattractive and useless however i am starting to realize that maybe ignoring this part of me could be limiting my vitality and versatility
Response: its important to acknowledge and accept all parts of ourselves even those we might perceive as unattractive or useless by embracing these aspects we can actually tap into our full potential and enrich our lives with increased vitality and versatility so dont hide or suppress your dorky side  instead try to find ways to express and appreciate it remember every aspect of your personality contributes to making you a unique individual

Context: i feel like i have this gap between my dork side and my hip side and im not sure how to bring them together i dont want to be a dork because im scared of people and feel insecure about myself
Response: its okay to feel a gap between different aspects of your personality instead of completely rejecting your dork side lets first understand it and what it brings to your life its important to embrace all parts of yourself as this can lead to a more authentic and balanced sense of self can you share what qualities you appreciate about your hip side

Context: im having trouble with the dork and hipster sides of myself and i dont want that dork in me im wondering how the dork could take what the hipster offers and what the hipster could contribute to the dork
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing some internal conflicts between different aspects of yourself instead of seeing the dork and the hipster as separate and incompatible consider how they can learn from each other and contribute positively to your overall self they can coexist and balance each other out allowing you to show various facets of your personality when needed what positive qualities do you think each aspect can bring to the other

Context: im not comfortable with this hip thing i dont think im a hip guy and i have trouble tolerating the excitement of the idea positive thoughts about myself and the idea of my inner complexity do not sit easily within my mind
Response: its completely normal to feel uncomfortable with certain aspects of ourselves its important to remember that selfacceptance is a journey its okay to question and explore different parts of your personality i would encourage you to try embracing your strengths and acknowledging your limitations without being too hard on yourself it might help you achieve a better sense of selfunderstanding

Context: im disappointed that i couldnt help my sister it doesnt hurt me though because its not my problem we lived together for eight days but it was just like staying with her when we were 17
Response: it seems like youre feeling disappointed about the situation with your sister but youre distancing yourself from the issue because its her problem its important to note that its possible for situations to affect both people involved do you think there might be some romanticism or hidden emotions in your perspective

Context: i dont like the romantic side of myself and i dont expect great things for my sister as it seems like an idealized fantasy i feel like im in a bad way
Response: i understand that you feel conflicted about your romantic side and you dont want to have unrealistic expectations for your sister its okay to feel this way and its important to recognize your feelings can you share more about why you view these expectations as a fantasy and how it affects your relationship with your sister

Context: i have a sense that most things are vaguely boring at least vaguely boring and mundane there are real problems and i see that there are problems but it seems like i have forgotten how to want something
Response: it sounds like you are experiencing a lack of motivation and feeling like life has lost its excitement its important to recognize that its normal to feel this way at times but we can work towards reigniting your passions and desires can you think of any past experiences or activities that used to bring you joy or excitement

Context: i dont do anything exceptional i write lame ad copy for local stuff and the expectations are not high its all in the southern california area so its not a big deal this session is actually boring me
Response: i understand that you may feel unfulfilled or unchallenged in your work as the expectations are not high and its local to southern california its completely normal to experience dissatisfaction if your job doesnt challenge you or help you grow can you think of any aspects of your work that you enjoy or any possible changes you could make to your role to make it more rewarding

Context: i attended a session with my counsellor and while they found our first session illuminating and exciting i didnt share the same feeling they tried to resonate with me using provocative language thinking it would help engage me since i have an irreverent and rebellious attitude but it didnt make the session exciting for me
Response: as your counsellor i apologize if my previous approach didnt work well for you i was trying to connect with you by resonating with your presumed attitude but its clear that it didnt have the desired effect moving forward lets discuss what kind of approach you would prefer in our sessions to help me better understand and support you your feedback is important to make this a productive experience for both of us

Context: i have a habit of keeping people including my counsellor at a distance i dont think i want to keep them out but its just something i do
Response: it seems like you recognize this pattern of distancing yourself from others and it could be something youve developed for various reasons like protecting yourself emotionally as your counsellor im willing to work with you at your pace to better understand why this habit has formed and together we can explore strategies to foster more comfortable open relationships is there any particular situation or relationship where youve seen this distancing affect you most

Context: i had told her what i was gonna be wearing and described myself however i didnt mention that i would be dishevelled i was extremely selfconscious
Response: its quite normal to feel selfconscious in such situations especially when meeting someone new in the future you can choose to be more open about your appearance to avoid any misunderstandings or anxiety is there anything in particular about your appearance that makes you feel selfconscious

Context: i have been noticing and worrying about where my hands should be like if they should be here there or in another specific position
Response: it seems like you are overly conscious about the position of your hands which could be a sign of anxiety or selfconsciousness can you tell me if there are any specific situations where you feel this way so we can better understand and address your concern

Context: i was concentrating on myself during the conversation and i had this internal dialogue where i kept telling myself to say something intelligent but then i would just respond back to myself saying that i had nothing to say it was incredibly distracting
Response: it sounds like you were putting a lot of pressure on yourself to perform in the conversation which can be quite distracting keep in mind that its normal to have an internal dialogue but try not to let it overwhelm you instead of focusing on saying something intelligent just focus on being present and engaged in the conversation remember its okay to take a moment to gather your thoughts before responding

Context: i was trying to have a conversation with someone but i didnt want to make banal chatter i tried to say something witty but we ended up talking about computers  which is a topic that i am familiar with it was a dull conversation and im feeling disappointed with myself for not making it more interesting
Response: its understandable that you wanted to have a more engaging conversation but its okay that it didnt turn out as you expected dont be too hard on yourself  sometimes people have dull conversations and its not a reflection of your wit or ability to connect with others instead of focusing on this one experience consider it a learning opportunity and think about ways to improve future interactions if youre comfortable sharing can you let me know more about why you felt the need to say something witty

Context: i recently had a conversation with someone and it seemed a little tense at first we both seemed to loosen up a bit by the end of the conversation i tried asking her out on friday but she said she was busy i took that as a no and im not sure how to interpret her response
Response: its understandable that you might be feeling uncertain about her response its possible that she was genuinely busy on friday or she might not be interested in going out with you its important to respect her schedule and boundaries however since you said the conversation was getting better towards the end you can consider asking her if theres another day that works for her this way you can gauge her interest while being respectful of her time

Context: i think gerald knows himself pretty well but he misunderstands his possibilities or has given up on his needs and desires i havent left my house for 90 days and im not pleased with it but im uncomfortable around people i have everything i need and have a social life
Response: thank you for sharing your feelings gerald it seems like you are trying to cope with your discomfort around people by staying at home while it may provide some peace there might be other ways to address this discomfort to improve your opportunities to fulfill your needs and desires can you please tell me more about your social life and activities you enjoy doing

Context: i have an electronic social life and a girlfriend in toronto but the thing is i dont really know what she is and she doesnt know what i am i dont even know if its a woman and thats the weird thing about having a social life thats electronic
Response: it sounds like you are in a unique situation where you have a relationship with someone online but theres uncertainty about their identity its normal to have concerns in situations like these can you tell me more about how this uncertainty affects your feelings and thoughts about the relationship

Context: i am six foot two and im confused about the satisfaction we get from our social life im out of the house right now but i wonder whats the big deal with it
Response: it seems like you are questioning the importance and satisfaction derived from social life social interactions can be essential for our mental wellbeing as they provide a sense of belonging support and opportunities to connect with others my question to you is do you feel satisfied with your current social life and does this affect your overall life satisfaction

Context: i feel like when i say something it doesnt matter much to the other person they easily ride over my words and it seems like they have their mind made up i tried to express my thoughts but they didnt let me finish
Response: i understand that it must be frustrating to feel unheard and disregarded as a counsellor its essential to ensure that both parties are equally engaged in the conversation can you give more details on the context of the conversation and how it affects your emotional wellbeing

Context: ive never really tried to be kind but in a big emergency im able to put aside my misanthropy and help out
Response: well kindness doesnt always require effort it can be natural id like to know a specific instance when youve been kind whether it was intentional or not instead of generalizing lets focus on one particular moment of kindness you have experienced

Context: when i was in high school i had to work during the summer to help my mothers struggling business while my friends enjoyed their vacation at marthas vineyard it was an emergency situation and i did it out of kindness for someone close to me
Response: it sounds like you made a selfless decision to help your mother during a difficult time instead of indulging in the leisure activities like your friends it must have been tough to make that sacrifice but it shows your strong sense of responsibility and love for your mother can you share how this experience might have shaped your perspectives or values later in life

Context: ive been struggling with focusing on the present moment i tend to skip ahead in conversations but this time i caught myself and shared it instead of keeping it to myself
Response: its great that youre becoming more aware of your tendency to skip ahead and acknowledging it this shows progress in developing mindfulness and selfawareness keep practicing and try to fully engage in the present moment remember its okay to catch yourself and share your experience with others

Context: ive been skipping ahead in life and recently realized that it would be nice to deal with people on another level its a new thought and i wonder who could put up with me for three hours
Response: its great that youve recognized the desire to connect with people on a deeper level as your counsellor im here to help you work through your thoughts and feelings even if it might take more than one session dont worry about the time it takes the focus should be on your growth and understanding how to build stronger connections with others

Context: ive been in therapy before and im not really convinced about the idea of insight leading to change my sister a therapist convinced me to come here but im not fully on board with this process im not an idiot and i dont have a lot of faith in therapy
Response: i understand your skepticism and feelings about therapy and its okay to express your doubts its important to remember that each therapy experience can be different and some approaches may work better for you than others would you be open to discuss what aspects of therapy were unhelpful for you in the past and if theres a different approach we can explore

Context: i think a lot of people are really stupid and boring and i know im not an idiot but i dont do well with my social interactions my office went virtual and i do everything by computer my wife doesnt see that theres no difference since there are no physical office gettogethers anymore
Response: it sounds like you are struggling with social interactions and are feeling misunderstood by your wife its important to acknowledge that virtual environments can impact social connections differently have you tried discussing these changes with your wife and possibly finding alternative ways to interact with others to improve your social experiences

Context: recently i had a fun date which went as expected but still left me feeling angry and overall bad
Response: its interesting that you felt angry and bad after your fun date even though it went as expected can you tell me more about what specifically triggered these negative emotions it would be helpful to understand the situation better and offer guidance on how to cope with such emotions in the future

Context: i was recently told by someone that i appeared disheveled and even though they mentioned other things as well i cant seem to get past that term im unsure if i really looked disheveled but the fact that they thought so bothers me
Response: i understand that being called disheveled might have affected you negatively its natural to feel hurt or judged when someone makes a comment about your appearance however try focusing on why this particular comment has stuck with you and whether there is an underlying concern or insecurity if you feel the need you can share with me the other things this person said to better understand the context of that conversation

Context: i recently had an interaction with someone who was very bright and it went really badly i wasnt smooth at all and it was exactly what i had predicted
Response: i understand that the interaction didnt go as youd hoped and it can be frustrating when things dont go smoothly can you provide more details about what specifically happened during the interaction so we can better analyze the situation and find ways to improve your communication skills

Context: i went on a date with someone i liked but i didnt have funny things to say or intelligent banter to engage her with at the end of the date i asked her if she wanted to go out again but she declined surprisingly im not as miserable about it as i thought id be
Response: its good to hear that youre not feeling too miserable about the outcome of the date rejection can be hard to handle but its important to remember that not every person we meet will be a perfect match instead of focusing on the lack of connection try to learn from this experience and consider how you might improve your communication skills or find more common ground in future dates can you tell me more about what happened during the date so we have a clearer picture of the situation

Context: i dont want to hurt other people for no reason is that a positive thing or just a personality default
Response: as a counsellor its important to note that not wanting to hurt others is generally a positive thing as it demonstrates empathy and consideration for others feelings its not necessarily a personality default id like to know more about why you consider this trait to be potentially negative could you please elaborate on that concern

Context: i feel like there are two sides of me one side has moments when i could hurt someone for no reason but i choose not to i often think about whether its kind not to run over a puppy in the road
Response: its normal for people to feel like they have different aspects of their personality in your case it seems that youre trying to navigate between your aggressive impulses and your compassionate side instead of focusing on whether not running over a puppy is considered kind try to evaluate your actions based on their overall impact on others and your own personal values

Context: i want to bring my good side into the light of day but i cant see the kind side of me and i feel dominated and defeated
Response: it can be challenging to recognize your own positive qualities when feeling dominated or defeated lets focus on what you can do to genuinely express your kindness are there any specific situations or people where youve shown kindness in the past reflecting on those experiences might help you see the kind side of yourself

Context: i feel like theres something wrong but i cant quite put my finger on it you make it seem like its something that we can talk about but i dont see it i cant say ive never been kind but im just not sure what the issue is
Response: i understand that youre feeling confused about what might be troubling you sometimes it can be challenging to identify the root cause of our discomfort im here to help you explore your thoughts and feelings can you think of any specific situation or emotion that bothers you or that youd like to discuss further

Context: i got in trouble when i was eleven years old the principal called me in and threatened me and said that he would suspend me next time its not real trouble i mean they dont do anything to eleven year olds also i was treated very badly by two therapists but it doesnt really matter
Response: its interesting that you mention the trouble you had with the principal when you were eleven and then the poor treatment you received from the therapists but you also say it doesnt matter there seems to be a contradiction in how you perceive these events on one hand you describe them as terrible yet on the other you downplay their significance can you help me understand why you feel this way about these experiences

Context: im feeling upset because my friend told my principal that i was smoking when i was eleven i think it was terrible of him to do that also i want to mention that i consider myself a very analytical person and i believe that i have insight into myself
Response: i understand why you might feel betrayed by your friend for telling the principal its important to differentiate between the two issues the smoking itself and your friends choice to share that information as an analytical person you might want to consider why your friend felt the need to tell your principal and how it affects your relationship remember that no ones selfinsight is perfect so its essential to remain open to new perspectives and growth is there any particular reason you wanted to share this incident with me

Context: i felt mildly offended when the counsellor made a confrontation because they didnt want me to set the boundaries of what i can and cant learn from our sessions together i felt amused by their comment that they got through to me
Response: as a counsellor i apologize if my statement was offensive my intention was to challenge the boundaries and encourage open communication during our sessions its important to address any discomfort or frustration so we can work together to explore and address your concerns effectively can you share more on why you felt offended and what specific boundaries you would like to maintain

Context: i feel like i always have to do everything by myself and im struggling with the isolation that it brings i end up interrupting others because im always in my own world
Response: i understand that you feel isolated and the struggle that comes with it its important to work on allowing others to be a part of your life and coordinating with them to ease that feeling can you think of any situations where you can make an effort to let others in and work together on a task

Context: i feel like this is therapy and i should be telling you about myself but im unsure what to talk about
Response: thats completely normal in therapy we do focus on you so lets begin by discussing your habits of mind what influences your thoughts actions and how you perceive situations this way we can better understand what you go through on a daily basis and explore what might be causing any distress in your life

Context: i had bad therapists before and they broke confidentiality when i talked to suzanne about my issues i feel like my reflexes were established a long time ago and have nothing to do with whats going on now
Response: it sounds like youve had some negative experiences with therapists in the past and its understandable that you might be hesitant to trust in the process now as a counsellor i would like to assure you that maintaining confidentiality is a priority for me in order to help you id like to know which specific aspects of your past therapy you found unhelpful and how they might be impacting your current situation

Context: i recently had a bad experience when someone told my principal about something i said in therapy
Response: i understand that it must be frustrating to have your privacy invaded like that can you please elaborate on what exactly happened and how it has affected you this would help me in providing better guidance and support for your situation

Context: i took her attitude as a no i took her no as a no it was a clear no her attitude was no not ever
Response: as a counsellor i understand that youre interpreting her response in a very absolute manner however its important to consider that peoples feelings and thoughts can change over time instead of focusing solely on this rejection try to be more open to understanding her perspective and remember that no is not necessarily forever is there any specific situation or incident that triggered this feeling of rejection

Context: as the patient i recently had a conversation with my counsellor where i expressed my perspective on a situation i admitted that i understand why my counsellor cant trust my judgments because of the way i make them i suggested that my counsellor should call someone else to get a clearer understanding
Response: as the counsellor i acknowledge your awareness of the issue and understand the reason for your suggestion i appreciate your honesty and the growth youve made in recognizing your thought patterns instead of focusing on mistrust lets work together on improving your judgmentmaking abilities and develop a stronger trust in yourself and your perceptions

Context: ive been told that my humor is sharp and quick and my language is metaphorical and colorful ive accepted this recognition of my positive qualities for the first time however i dont know what to do about it and i worry that insight doesnt lead to change
Response: its great that youve accepted the recognition of your positive qualities and your concern about implementing change is understandable change may not be instant but insight can be a starting point you can take one step at a time reflect on your thoughts and actions and gradually integrate your unique qualities into daily life in a balanced and effective manner dont be too hard on yourself change takes time and patience

Context: i dont take compliments well i dont like compliments i dont like to be complimented why do you think that is
Response: ah the reason i think it is is because youre not going to like this but im gonna tell you the answer to your question anyway its likely that you have issues with selfesteem or selfworth which make it difficult for you to accept compliments you might feel that you dont deserve the praise or you might be uncomfortable with the attention it brings its important to work on building your selfconfidence and accepting compliments as a healthy part of social interactions

Context: ive been trying to get out of the house every day because i think its good for me when i go outside the air feels nice and it feels good to be out of the house
Response: its great that you are making an effort to get out of the house daily as it can indeed be beneficial for your mental health how do you typically spend your time when youre outdoors

Context: i feel like ive gotten something out of this therapy and i like that you dont take any nonsense from me however ive been thinking about stopping this therapy since i have a social life now what do you think about it
Response: i believe its important not to view therapy as an on or off situation but i understand if you want it to be like that i would like to remind you of your power to work through barriers and not completely disregard therapy if a problem arises in the future leaving the option openended might be beneficial

Context: im not sure if we should continue our therapy sessions or not and if we do what would be the best way to do it should we decrease the frequency of our meetings
Response: as a counsellor i believe that therapy isnt an on or off thing but rather an availability when you need it we could consider tapering off and scheduling sessions less frequently such as once a month that way youll still have access to help whenever needed while adjusting to a less frequent schedule

Context: i think it would be a good idea to see each other once a month for a few months to gradually stop our sessions we can then evaluate how things go and decide whats best for me
Response: that sounds like a reasonable plan we can schedule monthly sessions to help in your transition monitor your progress and address any concerns you might have ensuring that you feel comfortable and confident in managing on your own is our main priority lets move forward with this plan and assess its effectiveness as we go

Context: i never used to be visibly uncomfortable but this time i couldnt muster the yes bob thats a good idea and i was having troubles with it i feel like im unable to go out and interact with humans
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a change in your ability to interact and navigate social situations comfortably could there be something specific that happened recently that triggered this change in you remember its completely normal to have ups and downs and finding the root cause can help you address and work through this situation

Context: i feel like im becoming unable to do something that i used to do and its really disturbing and immobilizing
Response: i understand how distressing and immobilizing this can be for you i would like to help you address this issue if youre willing to share more information could you please explain the situation or task that youre struggling with

Context: i shared my thoughts with bob about the campaign being wrong on a couple of accounts and i didnt like the slogan i suggested that if we came up with a better idea the giveaway would be moot and people would be interested in the product already however bobs reaction was simply this is my idea
Response: it seems like you expressed your disagreement with bobs campaign idea and offered an alternative viewpoint aiming at a better outcome however it appears that bob responded defensively without acknowledging your concerns as a counsellor i suggest exploring the reasons behind your disagreement and try to approach bob in a more collaborative way to find common ground how has your working relationship with bob been before this interaction

Context: i recently overheard my coworker talking to my boss and saying i think its a damn good idea i dont know the exact details of their conversation but i feel anxious and unsure about what they were discussing it makes me feel like im always several steps behind and maybe i should be moving faster
Response: its understandable to feel worried about feeling left out of important conversations at work however its important not to jump to conclusions about what they were discussing without any concrete information instead try to focus on your own tasks and keep an open line of communication with your boss and coworkers if theres something you need to be aware of or involved in trust that they will include you when necessary

Context: im not happy with this session i feel like ive been caught in a lie and ive never thought i was unable to be caught i can see some sense in what youre saying but i dont like this situation
Response: i understand that being caught in a lie can be uncomfortable its important to acknowledge when we make mistakes or feel vulnerable its a learning experience for both of us even though you didnt like this session it might have been important for your growth are there any specific aspects of the session that bothered you

Context: i went to a party this week and it was kind of an interesting experience im thinking of becoming a party boy
Response: its great to hear that you had an interesting experience at the party remember its essential to enjoy yourself and maintain a balance in your social life however dont forget your progress and personal growth during these experiences is there anything in particular youd like to share about your party experience

Context: i attended a party and started talking to a girl in my usual corner but i felt like i wasnt doing that well i realized i was giving her contradictory cues and i generally feel like an outsider i understand what its like to be thought of as a dork
Response: its great that you can empathize with the girl and understand the feeling of being an outsider keep in mind that putting yourself in someone elses shoes can help you better navigate social situations try to be more genuine and consistent with your cues when engaging in conversations to make the experience more enjoyable for both parties

Context: i dont want to confront my boss because im afraid of losing my job i think its an act of selfdefense and i see it as a practical decision what should i do
Response: i understand that you want to protect yourself by not confronting your boss its true that it can be a practical decision but its important to evaluate the situation and determine if not addressing the issue could lead to feelings of defeat or resentment you may want to consider alternative ways to address the issue without risking your job can you think of any other approach that might work

Context: i feel defeated and feel like the whole world is my boss i feel like i have to stay away from everybody and i dont have a sense of differentiation as to who i could be what i need to be with and who i cant i hold so many people in such a high degree of disdain
Response: it sounds like youre struggling with feelings of powerlessness and difficulty in differentiating between the people in your life instead of viewing everyone as a source of negativity or potential threat try taking them one at a time and assessing your relationships individually this might help you find a clearer sense of who you can trust and who to distance yourself from allowing you to regain a feeling of control over your life

Context: several weeks ago my sister came to stay with me during a marital crisis she recently went back to her husband and i just think shes an idiot
Response: it sounds like youre frustrated with your sisters decision to return to her husband during a difficult time can you help me understand your concerns about her choice and what specifically is bothering you about her decision

Context: well im not trying to be delineated per se its just that shes in a bad situation and shes going back to this guy i think she just needs the routine
Response: so she feels she cant handle the situation does she love him too much does she feel insecure without him maybe she needs the routines feeling secure in the familiarity of the relationship despite the challenges its important for her to understand her own needs and consider alternative ways to find stability and security in her life

Context: i imagine if i were to confront him about the issue he would tell me to clear out my desk and go to the other side of the living room but since its my apartment he cant really make me leave the office
Response: its important to communicate with people when you have concerns as a counsellor i suggest you express your feelings and thoughts in a calm and respectful manner focusing on the issue rather than the person however if this person responds negatively remember that its your apartment and you have the right to stand up for yourself laughs your sense of humor can also help in easing the tension

Context: as a patient i have trouble with expressing humor and making jokes i sometimes hold up my hand to let others know when its a joke
Response: as a counsellor i appreciate your effort in trying to communicate humor to others but it might not be the most effective way instead consider working on your delivery and observing how others use tone facial expressions and timing to convey humor practice and over time youll feel more comfortable expressing humor without relying on gestures

Context: i feel like if i say whats really on my mind especially to my boss id be in big trouble and possibly lose my job i dont think i need to tell people what i think about them even if its not my boss
Response: its important to maintain a good working relationship with your boss but its also essential to express your thoughts and opinions in a constructive manner you can try to find ways to communicate your ideas without being confrontational it might be helpful to practice assertive communication techniques so you can share your views without compromising your professional relationships do you have any specific situations where you feel particularly uncomfortable expressing yourself

Context: i have a tendency to withdraw from certain situations or not say certain things to people because i dont want to hurt their feelings it could be seen as an act of kindness but at the same time i feel like theres no conflict or energy within me
Response: it seems that you are trying to avoid conflict by withholding your thoughts and feelings from others while this might be an act of kindness it also limits your personal growth and the energy that comes from dealing with conflicts lets explore the other side of you the one that cares for others deeply and try to identify ways in which you can express your thoughts without causing harm to your relationships

Context: as the patient i find these exercises to be silly what exactly are we trying to accomplish with them
Response: as the counsellor i understand your concern about the exercises and its okay to find them silly these exercises are designed to help you express your thoughts and emotions in a safe and open environment they also help us to establish trust between us and understand each other better if youd like im open to discussing any suggestions or adjustments youd prefer to make the sessions more effective for you

Context: i dont want to win or compete i just want to understand whats going on in this situation however im feeling extremely uncomfortable right now and i think this session is not going well
Response: i understand that you feel uncomfortable and might be frustrated with how the session is going when i mentioned that i thought you were lying i need to clarify what i meant please tell me more about your thoughts and feelings as it will help me understand your perspective and provide better assistance lets work together to figure out whats going on

Context: i know something but i usually say i dont know to avoid confrontation i feel like im lying when i say that i dont know why i do it but i think we all lie at some point in our lives so yes i have lied before
Response: its common for people to feel uncertain or uncomfortable about sharing their thoughts and feelings and sometimes that leads to lying the fact that you recognize this behavior in yourself is a positive step towards addressing it to better understand why you choose to lie in certain situations try reflecting on the emotions or fears that might be driving this behavior if youd like you can share more about a specific situation where this has occurred and we can discuss it further

Context: ive been having trouble with my partner suzanne she always wants to go out and get me out of the house but i tell her that im unable to however deep down i know that its a lie
Response: it seems like you might be experiencing some resistance or fear towards going out even though youre capable of doing so can you tell me what is the main reason thats holding you back from going out with suzanne

Context: ive been struggling with feeling like im not being honest with myself or others and i finally admitted that ive been lying
Response: its great that youve acknowledged this issue and are willing to talk about it lying can be harmful to our relationships and our selfimage now that youve recognized this behavior lets explore why youve been lying and work on finding healthier ways to communicate

Context: i know im not big in like affectph boy i know im not really outgoing but i just you know i
Response: it seems like you have a certain concept of yourself and youre aware that you might not be very outgoing is there something specific thats bothering you or something youd like to work on with regards to this aspect of yourself

Context: ive been staying home and not attending my classes because my husband who is the breadwinner and paying for my classes said theres no point in me going i feel that if theres no need for our family then theres no point in me continuing my education even though it will take a couple more years to finish

Context: im annie and its my first time getting counseling im feeling a bit nervous and unfamiliar with the process to be honest i didnt really want to come
Response: hi annie im glad you decided to come in even though you didnt want to its completely normal to feel nervous and unfamiliar with the process as your counsellor im here to support and help you throughout this journey can you tell me a little bit about what brought you here today

Context: i havent been going to class and my friend was worried about me shes been trying to contact me for a few weeks but i wasnt answering her calls eventually she came to my door and made me go with her i think im dropping out anyway so i feel like theres no point in going to class anymore
Response: it seems like your friend cares about you and is concerned about your wellbeing its natural to feel overwhelmed sometimes but completely avoiding classes might not be the best solution in the long run can you tell me more about why you think youre dropping out and if theres any particular reason behind your decision

Response: it sounds like you initially enrolled in college for financial reasons but now that your husband has found a new job the pressure to contribute financially has lessened its important to consider how much personal interest or enjoyment you have in pursuing your education apart from the financial aspect do you feel a genuine desire to continue your studies or explore a particular field

Context: i thought that we thought that at this point in our life you know wed be starting a family and thats what i thought i wanted and i do i still do maybe not yet so yea so i dont know its different than what i thought i wanted i guess i remember getting an a on a paper analyzing a character from a movie and my professors appreciated the insight and depth i put into it it made me feel that those things are worth something
Response: it sounds like youre experiencing a bit of uncertainty in your life regarding starting a family and discovering that achieving a sense of meaning and purpose seems to bring you more fulfillment than you initially thought its important to remember that its okay to reevaluate what you want in life and to consider the value and meaning of your endeavors im wondering if youve had a chance to discuss these feelings with your husband and how he might feel about this newfound perspective

Context: i feel like it doesnt matter what i want and its frustrating i am more frustrated with myself than my husband we argue and i cant win arguments with him because im not quick on my feet i also feel like im flip flopping a lot
Response: it seems that youre feeling frustrated and invalidated possibly because you believe your opinions are not being considered its natural to feel upset when we cant effectively communicate our thoughts in an argument can you tell me more about the situations where you feel like youre flip flopping

Context: i have been experiencing conflicting feelings about returning to school as it has given me a sense of purpose and i have discovered new talents in myself however my husband is not supportive and says that i shouldnt be doing this i feel like im caught between my own desires and his opinions im not really sure what to expect from this counseling session as my friend suggested it but i havent had any experience with therapy before
Response: its understandable that you are feeling conflicted especially when you are receiving mixed messages from your own internal desires and the opinions of your husband during our sessions i would like us to focus on gaining a better understanding of your own thoughts feelings and hopes regarding your personal growth and aspirations this will allow you to make an informed decision about how to proceed with regards to your schooling keep in mind that its okay to feel unsure about therapy at first but communication and selfexploration are important aspects of this process

Context: when i was in school i started to feel purposeful and found meaning in my daily life through the conversations with my classmates the questions professors asked and the papers i wrote it was fun to apply the things i was learning seeing patterns and understanding cause and effect i felt good at it though not the best
Response: its great to hear that you were feeling purposeful and finding meaning in your school life engaging with your classmates professors and assignments can indeed contribute to a sense of purpose and personal growth embrace those positive experiences and continue to seek out intellectual challenges to help maintain your sense of accomplishment and fulfillment remember its not about being the best but rather about enjoying the process and developing your skills

Context: ive been feeling very overwhelmed lately and im not sure why ive been trying to figure out if theres a pattern to my emotions but i havent had any luck yet
Response: its good that youre trying to identify a pattern as it can be helpful in understanding the triggers behind your emotions next time we meet well focus on finding possible patterns in your emotions and develop strategies to cope with them in the meantime try to observe any changes in your mood or emotions and take note of any possible triggers

Context: i feel torn between my roles as a housewife and as a student looking for purpose and meaning i even felt childish when i was crying earlier i am willing to do the homework youve suggested to help me between our sessions
Response: its important to recognize and understand the different parts of yourself that are contributing to your emotions as your counsellor i suggest you reflect on these roles and the feelings they evoke for your homework try to find the sources of your feeling childish and keep a journal to note any thoughts or events that trigger these emotions well further discuss these findings in our next session to help you better understand and manage your emotions

Context: my counsellor gave me homework where i have to catch my thoughts and notice who they are coming from they believe that as i start to change those thoughts that are hurting me i will be able to function better i just need to name where these thoughts are coming from
Response: i understand how challenging it can be to deal with thoughts that are holding you back the homework your counsellor gave you is a step towards identifying and changing these thoughts its important to recognize the source of these thoughts and evaluate which ways of thinking are the best for you keep practicing this exercise and dont hesitate to ask your counsellor any questions next time you meet

Context: lately my partner and i have been fighting but only regarding a specific issue before this issue we didnt really have fights because i am very easygoing and usually just go along with what he wants its been affecting my daily life and i try not to think about it
Response: it sounds like this particular issue has been causing tension in your relationship and impacting your daily functioning can you share more about this specific issue that you and your partner are fighting about understanding the root cause may help in finding a resolution and improving your overall wellbeing

Context: i am struggling when my partner is not at home i try to distract myself from the thoughts but it still impacts me ive been watching a lot of reality tv cleaning shopping and doing things that i wouldnt usually do
Response: it sounds like youre trying to cope with your partners absence by engaging in different activities to distract yourself however it seems that these distractions might not be entirely effective can you elaborate on how these activities impact your emotional wellbeing and if theres a specific reason you are uneasy when your partner is away

Context: sometimes when im shopping i have fleeting thoughts about the conflict between me and my friend i might notice the time and think that its time for class but then i push those thoughts aside
Response: it seems like youre experiencing some conflict with a friend but youre trying to suppress those thoughts while youre shopping when you have these fleeting thoughts its important to recognize them and allow yourself to feel the emotions surrounding the conflict suppressing them might lead to unresolved feelings in the long run is there any specific situation or conflict with your friend that triggers these thoughts

Context: im just reliving the arguments that weve had and i feel like such a child i think this is a childish reaction
Response: its completely normal to feel strong emotions during or after an argument and its not necessarily a childish reaction instead of trying to box in your emotions its important to recognize and understand them are there any specific triggers during the arguments that make you feel this way

Context: i guess i am feeling overwhelmed and struggling with the idea of my purpose in life for the longest time i thought my purpose was to be a mom and take care of my family but now i find myself flipflopping thinking that maybe i have a different purpose i feel like this is causing tension between the person who wants to have a different purpose and the person who is staying home and not going to class
Response: its completely normal to question your purpose and reevaluate your goals in life whats important is to understand that its okay to change and adapt as you grow you mentioned your frustration with flipflopping in your head and not being sure about what to do have you considered trying out different activities or exploring new interests to help you gain more clarity on what you want in life

Context: well i cant change what i want because we worked so hard you know why change the plan and if i flip flop now what if i flip flop later so you know its a concern a little bit
Response: it sounds like youre worried about being unpredictable and that changing your plan might lead to more uncertainty in the future its important to remember that its okay to reevaluate and make adjustments as needed do you think there could be a specific reason why youre hesitant to make changes to your plan

Context: i feel childish for having certain emotions because im an adult and i should be past that my partner called it childish too which hurts me as i dont like being called a child i try to push these emotions aside
Response: i can see that your partners words are having an emotional impact on you and its understandable to feel hurt by being called childish its important for us to acknowledge and explore our emotions despite any judgments we may have about them please tell me more about how these emotions are affecting you without judging yourself for feeling them

Context: sometimes i think we do that to kind of survive survive the moment you know survive the argument or survive the situation you know kind of push the emotion back down if i cry in front of him that would be more childish wouldnt it i know but its tough to do that in the moment when someone is judging you for it
Response: i understand that it can be difficult to show your true emotions in fear of being judged especially during a heated moment but it is important to acknowledge your emotions and not feel ashamed or afraid to show them emotions make us human and its okay to feel what you feel remember you dont have to go through this alone and im here to help you process these emotions and find healthier ways to cope with them

Context: im constantly flipflopping and feeling frustrated when im alone at home as my husband works my mind cant decide what i want and what i should have i feel like he doesnt understand my desire to go back to school i struggle to argue with him because i cant express my thoughts coherently and feel even more frustrated with myself

Context: i am stressed about school my friends and the expectations of my partner we hang out after school and sometimes i am not home when he wants me to be he wants dinner ready and the house in a certain way but with school and other commitments i am struggling to meet these expectations additionally he considers my schooling an unnecessary expense which causes more disagreements between us

Context: i feel like im stuck between two realities  one where im just a housewife and the other one where im a confident person who goes back to school i did fine on a couple of papers but im not like her the confident woman im not as wellspoken or commanding as she is
Response: it sounds like youre struggling to find your own identity in the middle of these two realities when you say im not her i cant be her it seems like those thoughts might be holding you back from becoming that confident version of yourself have you thought about what steps you could take to build your confidence and connect with that part of yourself

Context: i was hesitant to come in for counseling but my friend suggested it after having some time together with you i feel that its not as scary as i thought it would be i dont want to cry anymore but i think it would be okay to come back
Response: its completely normal to feel hesitant or nervous before starting counseling im glad that you find it not as scary as you thought and that youre open to coming back its important to remember that counseling is a safe space for you to express your emotions including tears we are here to support and help you through this process is there a specific area or concern that you would like us to focus on in future sessions
